# JavaDoc Help

---

## Navigation

Starting from the [Overview](index.html) page, you can browse the documentation using the links in each page, and in the navigation bar at the top of each page. The [Index](index-all.html) and Search box allow you to navigate to specific declarations and summary pages, including: [All Packages](allpackages-index.html), [All Classes and Interfaces](allclasses-index.html)

### Search

You can search for definitions of modules, packages, types, fields, methods, system properties and other terms defined in the API. These items can be searched using part or all of the name, optionally using "camelCase" abbreviations, or multiple search terms separated by whitespace. Some examples:

1. `"j.l.obj"` matches "java.lang.Object"
2. `"InpStr"` matches "java.io.InputStream"
3. `"math exact long"` matches "java.lang.Math.absExact(long)"

Refer to the [Javadoc Search Specification](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/javadoc/javadoc-search-spec.html) for a full description of search features.

### Keyboard Navigation

Documentation pages provide keyboard shortcuts to facilitate access to common navigation tasks.

* Type
  `/`
  to access the search input field in any page.
* Type
  `.`
  to access the filter input field in the sidebar of class pages.
* Type
  `Esc`
  to clear the input and release keyboard focus in any input field.
* Type
  `Tab`
  /
  `↓`
  /
  `↑`
  to select list items after entering a search term in a search or filter input field.
* Type
  `←`
  /
  `→`
  to switch between tabs in tabbed summary tables.

---

## Kinds of Pages

The following sections describe the different kinds of pages in this collection.

### Overview

The [Overview](index.html) page is the front page of this API document and provides a list of all packages with a summary for each. This page can also contain an overall description of the set of packages.

### Package

Each package has a page that contains a list of its classes and interfaces, with a summary for each. These pages may contain the following categories:

* Interfaces
* Classes
* Enums
* Exception Classes
* Annotation Types

### Class or Interface

Each class, interface, nested class and nested interface has its own separate page. Each of these pages has three sections consisting of a declaration and description, member summary tables, and detailed member descriptions. Entries in each of these sections are omitted if they are empty or not applicable.

* Class Inheritance Diagram
* Direct Subclasses
* All Known Subinterfaces
* All Known Implementing Classes
* Class or Interface Declaration
* Class or Interface Description

  

* Nested Class Summary
* Enum Constant Summary
* Field Summary
* Property Summary
* Constructor Summary
* Method Summary
* Required Element Summary
* Optional Element Summary

  

* Enum Constant Details
* Field Details
* Property Details
* Constructor Details
* Method Details
* Element Details

Note: Annotation interfaces have required and optional elements, but not methods. Only enum classes have enum constants. The components of a record class are displayed as part of the declaration of the record class. Properties are a feature of JavaFX.

The summary entries are alphabetical, while the detailed descriptions are in the order they appear in the source code. This preserves the logical groupings established by the programmer.

### Other Files

Packages and modules may contain pages with additional information related to the declarations nearby.

### Use

Each documented package, class or interface has its own Use page, which lists packages, classes, interfaces, methods, constructors and fields that use any part of that package, class or interface. Given a class or interface A, its Use page includes subclasses or subinterfaces of A, fields declared as A, methods that return A, methods and constructors with parameters of type A, and subclasses or subinterfaces with parameters of type A. You can access this page by first going to the package, class or interface, then clicking on the USE link in the navigation bar.

### Tree (Class Hierarchy)

There is a [Class Hierarchy](overview-tree.html) page for all packages, plus a hierarchy for each package. Each hierarchy page contains a list of classes and a list of interfaces. Classes are organized by inheritance structure starting with `java.lang.Object`. Interfaces do not inherit from `java.lang.Object`.

* When viewing the Overview page, clicking on TREE displays the hierarchy for all packages.
* When viewing a particular package, class or interface page, clicking on TREE displays the hierarchy for only that package.

### Deprecated API

The [Deprecated API](deprecated-list.html) page lists all of the API that have been deprecated. A deprecated API is not recommended for use, generally due to shortcomings, and a replacement API is usually given. Deprecated APIs may be removed in future implementations.

### Constant Field Values

The [Constant Field Values](constant-values.html) page lists the static final fields and their values.

### Serialized Form

Each serializable or externalizable class has a description of its serialization fields and methods. This information is of interest to those who implement rather than use the API. While there is no link in the navigation bar, you can get to this information by going to any serialized class and clicking "Serialized Form" in the "See Also" section of the class description.

### All Packages

The [All Packages](allpackages-index.html) page contains an alphabetic index of all packages contained in the documentation.

### All Classes and Interfaces

The [All Classes and Interfaces](allclasses-index.html) page contains an alphabetic index of all classes and interfaces contained in the documentation, including annotation interfaces, enum classes, and record classes.

### Index

The [Index](index-all.html) contains an alphabetic index of all classes, interfaces, constructors, methods, and fields in the documentation, as well as summary pages such as [All Packages](allpackages-index.html), [All Classes and Interfaces](allclasses-index.html).

---

## Release Details

The details for each module, package, class or interface normally include the release in which the declaration was introduced.

When a member is added after the initial introduction of the enclosing class or interface, the details of the member include the release in which it was introduced.

Some summary pages (New API, Deprecated) allow you to filter the contents of the page according to the release in which the declaration was introduced or deprecated.

  [IOUnaryOperator](IOUnaryOperator.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.function")<T>

  Like [`UnaryOperator`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/UnaryOperator.html "class or interface in java.util.function") but throws [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io").

  [Uncheck](Uncheck.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.function")

  Unchecks calls by throwing [`UncheckedIOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/UncheckedIOException.html "class or interface in java.io") instead of [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io").

# Package org.apache.commons.io.input

---

package org.apache.commons.io.input

Provides implementations of input classes, such as [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") and [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io").

* Related Packages

  Package

  Description

  [org.apache.commons.io](../package-summary.html)

  Provides classes for working with streams, readers, writers and files.

  [org.apache.commons.io.input.buffer](buffer/package-summary.html)

  Provides implementations of buffered input classes, such as
  [`CircularBufferInputStream`](buffer/CircularBufferInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input.buffer") and
  [`PeekableInputStream`](buffer/PeekableInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input.buffer").

extends [FileFilter](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileFilter.html "class or interface in java.io"), [FilenameFilter](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilenameFilter.html "class or interface in java.io"), [PathFilter](../file/PathFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.file"), [PathMatcher](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/PathMatcher.html "class or interface in java.nio.file")

# Package org.apache.commons.io.build

---

package org.apache.commons.io.build

Provides classes to implement the builder pattern for IO classes.

The main classes in this package are (indentation reflects hierarchy):

* The root class [AbstractSupplier](AbstractSupplier.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build") abstracts *supplying* an instance of type `T`
  where `T` is unbounded. This class carries no state.
  * [AbstractOrigin](AbstractOrigin.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build") extends [AbstractSupplier](AbstractSupplier.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")
    to abstract and wrap an *origin* for builders, where an origin is a `byte[]`, [Channel](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/Channel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels"),
    [CharSequence](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html "class or interface in java.lang"), [File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io"), [InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"),
    [IORandomAccessFile](../IORandomAccessFile.html "class in org.apache.commons.io"), [OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), [Path](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file"), [RandomAccessFile](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html "class or interface in java.io"), [Reader](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io"), [URI](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/net/URI.html "class or interface in java.net"), or
    [Writer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io").
  * [AbstractOriginSupplier](AbstractOriginSupplier.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build") extends [AbstractSupplier](AbstractSupplier.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build") to abstract *building* an instance of type `T` where `T` is unbounded from a wrapped
    [origin](AbstractOrigin.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build").
    * [AbstractStreamBuilder](AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build") extends
      [AbstractOriginSupplier](AbstractOriginSupplier.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build") to abstract *building* a typed instance of type `T` where
      `T` is unbounded. This class contains various properties like a buffer size, buffer size checker, a buffer size default, buffer size maximum, Charset,
      Charset default, default size checker, and open options. A subclass may use all, some, or none of these properties in building instances of `T`.

Since:
:   2.12.0

public class [CircularBufferInputStream](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/buffer/CircularBufferInputStream.html#line-35)
extends [FilterInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

Implements a buffered input stream, which is internally based on a [`CircularByteBuffer`](CircularByteBuffer.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input.buffer"). Unlike the
[`BufferedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), this one doesn't need to reallocate byte arrays internally.

# Package org.apache.commons.io

---

package org.apache.commons.io

Provides classes for working with streams, readers, writers and files. The most commonly used classes are described here:

**IOUtils** is the most frequently used class. It provides operations to read, write, copy and close streams.

**FileUtils** provides operations based around the JDK File class. These include reading, writing, copying, comparing and deleting.

**FilenameUtils** provides utilities based on filenames. This utility class manipulates file names without using File objects. It aims to
simplify the transition between Windows and Unix. Before using this class however, you should consider whether you should be using File objects.

**FileSystemUtils** allows access to the filing system in ways the JDK does not support. At present this allows you to get the free space on a
drive.

**EndianUtils** swaps data between Big-Endian and Little-Endian formats.

# Apache Commons IO Issue tracking

Apache Commons IO uses [ASF JIRA](https://issues.apache.org/jira/) for tracking issues.
See the [Apache Commons IO JIRA project page](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/IO).

To use JIRA you may need to [create an account](https://issues.apache.org/jira/secure/Signup!default.jspa)
(if you have previously created/updated Commons issues using Bugzilla an account will have been automatically
created and you can use the [Forgot Password](https://issues.apache.org/jira/secure/ForgotPassword!default.jspa)
page to get a new password).

If you would like to report a bug, or raise an enhancement request with
Apache Commons IO please do the following:

1. [Search existing open bugs](https://issues.apache.org/jira/secure/IssueNavigator.jspa?reset=true&pid=12310477&sorter/field=issuekey&sorter/order=DESC&status=1&status=3&status=4).
   If you find your issue listed then please add a comment with your details.
2. [Search the mailing list archive(s)](mail-lists.html).
   You may find your issue or idea has already been discussed.
3. Decide if your issue is a bug or an enhancement.
4. Submit either a [bug report](https://issues.apache.org/jira/secure/CreateIssueDetails!init.jspa?pid=12310477&issuetype=1&priority=4&assignee=-1)
   or [enhancement request](https://issues.apache.org/jira/secure/CreateIssueDetails!init.jspa?pid=12310477&issuetype=4&priority=4&assignee=-1).

Please also remember these points:

* the more information you provide, the better we can help you
* test cases are vital, particularly for any proposed enhancements
* the developers of Apache Commons IO are all unpaid volunteers

For more information on creating patches see the
[Apache Contributors Guide](https://www.apache.org/dev/contributors.html).

You may also find these links useful:

* [All Open Apache Commons IO bugs](https://issues.apache.org/jira/secure/IssueNavigator.jspa?reset=true&pid=12310477&sorter/field=issuekey&sorter/order=DESC&status=1&status=3&status=4)
* [All Resolved Apache Commons IO bugs](https://issues.apache.org/jira/secure/IssueNavigator.jspa?reset=true&pid=12310477&sorter/field=issuekey&sorter/order=DESC&status=5&status=6)
* [All Apache Commons IO bugs](https://issues.apache.org/jira/secure/IssueNavigator.jspa?reset=true&pid=12310477&sorter/field=issuekey&sorter/order=DESC)

* ## Method Details

  * ### littleEndian

    public static [ByteBuffer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/ByteBuffer.html "class or interface in java.nio") [littleEndian](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/ByteBuffers.html#line-42)(byte[] array)

    Allocates a new byte buffer with little-endian byte order. The bytes of a multibyte value are ordered from least significant to most significant.

    The new buffer's position is zero, the limit is its capacity, the mark is undefined, and each of element is initialized to zero. The new buffer has the
    given backing `array`, and its [`array offset`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/ByteBuffer.html#arrayOffset-- "class or interface in java.nio") is zero.

    Parameters:
    :   `array` - The array that will back the new byte buffer.

    Returns:
    :   The new byte buffer.
  * ### littleEndian

    public static [ByteBuffer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/ByteBuffer.html "class or interface in java.nio") [littleEndian](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/ByteBuffers.html#line-52)([ByteBuffer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/ByteBuffer.html "class or interface in java.nio") allocate)

    Sets the give buffer to little-endian.

    Parameters:
    :   `allocate` - The buffer to set to little-endian.

    Returns:
    :   the given buffer.
  * ### littleEndian

    public static [ByteBuffer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/ByteBuffer.html "class or interface in java.nio") [littleEndian](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/ByteBuffers.html#line-67)(int capacity)

    Allocates a new byte buffer with little-endian byte order. The bytes of a multibyte value are ordered from least significant to most significant.

    The new buffer's position is zero, the limit is its capacity, the mark is undefined, and each of element is initialized to zero. The new buffer has a
    [`backing array`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/ByteBuffer.html#array-- "class or interface in java.nio"), and its [`array offset`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/ByteBuffer.html#arrayOffset-- "class or interface in java.nio") is zero.

    Parameters:
    :   `capacity` - The new buffer's capacity, in bytes.

    Returns:
    :   The new byte buffer.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - If the `capacity` is negative.

public static class [DeferredFileOutputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/DeferredFileOutputStream.html#line-78)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[DeferredFileOutputStream](DeferredFileOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output"), [DeferredFileOutputStream.Builder](DeferredFileOutputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")>

Builds a new [`DeferredFileOutputStream`](DeferredFileOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

For example:

```
DeferredFileOutputStream s = DeferredFileOutputStream.builder()
  .setBufferSize(4096)
  .setDirectory(dir)
  .setOutputFile(outputFile)
  .setPrefix(prefix)
  .setSuffix(suffix)
  .setThreshold(threshold)
  .get();
```

The only super's aspect used is buffer size.

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

* ## Method Details

  * ### get

    public [ReversedLinesFileReader](ReversedLinesFileReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") [get](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ReversedLinesFileReader.Builder.html#line-121)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`ReversedLinesFileReader`](ReversedLinesFileReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()) on this builder, otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getPath()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getPath()) gets the target aspect.
    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getBufferSize()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getBufferSize())
    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getCharset()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getCharset())

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to a [`Path`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to a [`Path`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getPath()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getPath()).

    See Also:
    :   * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getPath()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getPath())
        * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getBufferSize()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getBufferSize())
        * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getCharset()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getCharset())
        * [`IOSupplier.getUnchecked()`](../function/IOSupplier.html#getUnchecked())

public enum [FileSystem](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileSystem.html#line-44)
extends [Enum](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Enum.html "class or interface in java.lang")<[FileSystem](FileSystem.html "enum in org.apache.commons.io")>

Abstracts an OS' file system details, currently supporting the single use case of converting a file name String to a
legal file name with [`toLegalFileName(String, char)`](#toLegalFileName(java.lang.String,char)).

The starting point of any operation is [`getCurrent()`](#getCurrent()) which gets you the enum for the file system that matches
the OS hosting the running JVM.

Since:
:   2.7

  * ### getMaxFileNameLength

    public int [getMaxFileNameLength](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileSystem.html#line-518)()

    Gets the maximum length for file names (excluding any folder path).

    This limit applies only to the file name itself, excluding any parent directories.

    The value is expressed in Java `char` units (UTF-16 code units).

    **Note:** Because many file systems enforce limits in *bytes* using a specific encoding rather than in UTF-16 code units, a name that
    fits this limit may still be rejected by the underlying file system.

    Use [`isLegalFileName(CharSequence)`](#isLegalFileName(java.lang.CharSequence)) to check whether a given name is valid for the current file system and charset.

    However, any file name longer than this limit is guaranteed to be invalid on the current file system.

    Returns:
    :   the maximum file name length in characters.
  * ### getMaxPathLength

    public int [getMaxPathLength](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileSystem.html#line-545)()

    Gets the maximum length for file paths (may include folders).

    This value is inclusive of all path components and separators. For a limit of each path component see [`getMaxFileNameLength()`](#getMaxFileNameLength()).

    The value is expressed in Java `char` units (UTF-16 code units) and represents the longest path that can be safely passed to Java
    [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") and [`Path`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") APIs.

    **Note:** many operating systems and file systems enforce path length limits in *bytes* using a specific encoding, rather than in
    UTF-16 code units. As a result, a path that fits within this limit may still be rejected by the underlying platform.

    Conversely, any path longer than this limit is guaranteed to fail with at least some operating system API calls.

    Returns:
    :   the maximum file path length in characters.

# Class PathFileComparator

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.comparator.PathFileComparator

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Serializable, Comparator<File>`

---

public class [PathFileComparator](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/comparator/PathFileComparator.html#line-56)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Compare the **path** of two files for order (see [`File.getPath()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#getPath-- "class or interface in java.io")).

This comparator can be used to sort lists or arrays of files
by their path either in a case-sensitive, case-insensitive or
system dependent case-sensitive way. A number of singleton instances
are provided for the various case sensitivity options (using [`IOCase`](../IOCase.html "enum in org.apache.commons.io"))
and the reverse of those options.

Example of a *case-sensitive* file path sort using the
[`PATH_COMPARATOR`](#PATH_COMPARATOR) singleton instance:

```
      List<File> list = ...
      ((AbstractFileComparator) PathFileComparator.PATH_COMPARATOR).sort(list);
```

Example of a *reverse case-insensitive* file path sort using the
[`PATH_INSENSITIVE_REVERSE`](#PATH_INSENSITIVE_REVERSE) singleton instance:

```
      File[] array = ...
      ((AbstractFileComparator) PathFileComparator.PATH_INSENSITIVE_REVERSE).sort(array);
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.4

# Class FilterCollectionWriter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, Flushable, Appendable, AutoCloseable`

public class [FilterCollectionWriter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/FilterCollectionWriter.html#line-47)
extends [Writer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io")

Abstract class for writing filtered character streams to a [`Collection`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Collection.html "class or interface in java.util") of writers. This is in contrast to
[`FilterWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterWriter.html "class or interface in java.io") which is backed by a single [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io").

This abstract class provides default methods that pass all requests to the contained writers. Subclasses should
likely override some of these methods.

The class [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") defines method signatures with `throws` [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io"), which in this class are
actually [`IOExceptionList`](../IOExceptionList.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") containing a list of [`IOIndexedException`](../IOIndexedException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io").

Since:
:   2.7

public static class [ValidatingObjectInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/serialization/ValidatingObjectInputStream.html#line-105)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[ValidatingObjectInputStream](ValidatingObjectInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.serialization"), [ValidatingObjectInputStream.Builder](ValidatingObjectInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.serialization")>

Builds a new [`ValidatingObjectInputStream`](ValidatingObjectInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.serialization").

## Using NIO

```
ValidatingObjectInputStream s = ValidatingObjectInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(Paths.get("MyFile.ser"))
  .get();
```

## Using IO

```
ValidatingObjectInputStream s = ValidatingObjectInputStream.builder()
  .setFile(new File("MyFile.ser"))
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.18.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

    public [ValidatingObjectInputStream](ValidatingObjectInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.serialization") [get](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/serialization/ValidatingObjectInputStream.Builder.html#line-189)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`ValidatingObjectInputStream`](ValidatingObjectInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.serialization").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()) on this builder, otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()) gets the target aspect.
    * predicate
    * charsetDecoder
    * writeImmediately

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot provide a [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()).

    See Also:
    :   * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getWriter()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getWriter())
        * [`IOSupplier.getUnchecked()`](../function/IOSupplier.html#getUnchecked())

  * ### read

    int [read](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/Tailer.RandomAccessResourceBridge.html#line-390)(byte[] b)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Reads up to `b.length` bytes of data from this tailable into an array of bytes. This method blocks until at
    least one byte of input is available.

    Parameters:
    :   `b` - the buffer into which the data is read.

    Returns:
    :   the total number of bytes read into the buffer, or `-1` if there is no more data because the end of
        this tailable has been reached.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - If the first byte cannot be read for any reason other than end of tailable, or if the random
        access tailable has been closed, or if some other I/O error occurs.
  * ### seek

    void [seek](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/Tailer.RandomAccessResourceBridge.html#line-402)(long pos)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Sets the file-pointer offset, measured from the beginning of this tailable, at which the next read or write occurs.
    The offset may be set beyond the end of the tailable. Setting the offset beyond the end of the tailable does not
    change the tailable length. The tailable length will change only by writing after the offset has been set beyond the
    end of the tailable.

    Parameters:
    :   `pos` - the offset position, measured in bytes from the beginning of the tailable, at which to set the tailable
        pointer.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if `pos` is less than `0` or if an I/O error occurs.

public class [AutoCloseInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/AutoCloseInputStream.html#line-39)
extends [ProxyInputStream](ProxyInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

Proxy stream that closes and discards the underlying stream as soon as the end of input has been reached or when the stream is explicitly closed. Not even a
reference to the underlying stream is kept after it has been closed, so any allocated in-memory buffers can be freed even if the client application still
keeps a reference to the proxy stream.

This class is typically used to release any resources related to an open stream as soon as possible even if the client application (by not explicitly closing
the stream when no longer needed) or the underlying stream (by not releasing resources once the last byte has been read) do not do that.

To build an instance, use [`AutoCloseInputStream.Builder`](AutoCloseInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

Since:
:   1.4

See Also:
:   * [`AutoCloseInputStream.Builder`](AutoCloseInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Closes the underlying input stream and replaces the reference to it with a [`ClosedInputStream`](ClosedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") instance.

    This method is automatically called by the read methods when the end of input has been reached.

    Note that it is safe to call this method any number of times. The original underlying input stream is closed and discarded only once when this method is
    first called.

# Class FileFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.FileFileFilter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [FileFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/FileFileFilter.html#line-67)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

This filter accepts [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")s that are files (not directories).

For example, here is how to print out a list of the real files
within the current directory:

## Using Classic IO

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(FileFileFilter.INSTANCE);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

## Using NIO

```
final Path dir = PathUtils.current();
final AccumulatorPathVisitor visitor = AccumulatorPathVisitor.withLongCounters(FileFileFilter.INSTANCE);
//
// Walk one directory
Files.walkFileTree(dir, Collections.emptySet(), 1, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
//
visitor.getPathCounters().reset();
//
// Walk directory tree
Files.walkFileTree(dir, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getDirList());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.3

See Also:
:   * [`FileFilterUtils.fileFileFilter()`](FileFilterUtils.html#fileFileFilter())
    * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.FileFileFilter)

  * ### contentEquals

    public static boolean [contentEquals](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/file/PathUtils.html#line-327)([FileSystem](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/FileSystem.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") fileSystem1,
    [FileSystem](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/FileSystem.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") fileSystem2)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Compares the files of two FileSystems to determine if they are equal or not while considering file contents. The comparison includes all files in all
    subdirectories.

    For example, to compare two ZIP files:

    ```
    final Path zipPath1 = Paths.get("file1.zip");
    final Path zipPath2 = Paths.get("file2.zip");
    try (FileSystem fileSystem1 = FileSystems.newFileSystem(zipPath1, null); FileSystem fileSystem2 = FileSystems.newFileSystem(zipPath2, null)) {
        assertTrue(PathUtils.directoryAndFileContentEquals(dir1, dir2));
    }
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `fileSystem1` - The first FileSystem.
    :   `fileSystem2` - The second FileSystem.

    Returns:
    :   Whether the two FileSystem contain the same files while considering file contents.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error is thrown by a visitor method.

    Since:
    :   2.19.0

  * ### delete

    public static [Counters.PathCounters](Counters.PathCounters.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.file") [delete](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/file/PathUtils.html#line-510)([Path](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") path)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Deletes a file or directory. If the path is a directory, delete it and all subdirectories.

    The difference between [`File.delete()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#delete-- "class or interface in java.io") and this method are:

    * A directory to delete does not have to be empty.
    * You get exceptions when a file or directory cannot be deleted; [`File.delete()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#delete-- "class or interface in java.io") returns a boolean.

    Parameters:
    :   `path` - file or directory to delete, must not be `null`

    Returns:
    :   The visitor used to delete the given directory.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the directory is `null`
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error is thrown by a visitor method or if an I/O error occurs.

    Compares the file contents of two Paths to determine if they are equal or not.

    File content is accessed through [`Files.newInputStream(Path,OpenOption...)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Files.html#newInputStream-java.nio.file.Path-java.nio.file.OpenOption...- "class or interface in java.nio.file").

    Parameters:
    :   `path1` - the first file path.
    :   `path2` - the second file path.

    Returns:
    :   true if the content of the streams are equal or they both don't exist, false otherwise.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if either input is null.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.

    See Also:
    :   * [`FileUtils.contentEquals(java.io.File, java.io.File)`](../FileUtils.html#contentEquals(java.io.File,java.io.File))

  * ### filter

    public static [Path](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file")[] [filter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/file/PathUtils.html#line-893)([PathFilter](PathFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.file") filter,
    [Path](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file")... paths)

    Applies an [`IOFileFilter`](../filefilter/IOFileFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter") to the provided [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") objects. The resulting array is a subset of the original file list that matches the provided
    filter.

    The [`Set`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Set.html "class or interface in java.util") returned by this method is not guaranteed to be thread safe.

    ```
    Set<File> allFiles = ...
    Set<File> javaFiles = FileFilterUtils.filterSet(allFiles,
        FileFilterUtils.suffixFileFilter(".java"));
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `filter` - the filter to apply to the set of files.
    :   `paths` - the array of files to apply the filter to.

    Returns:
    :   a subset of `files` that is accepted by the file filter.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the filter is `null`
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if `files` contains a `null` value.

    Since:
    :   2.9.0

  * ### getExtension

    public static [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") [getExtension](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/file/PathUtils.html#line-991)([Path](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") path)

    Gets the extension of a Path.

    This method returns the textual part of the Path after the last period.

    ```
    foo.txt      --> "txt"
    a/b/c.jpg    --> "jpg"
    a/b.txt/c    --> ""
    a/b/c        --> ""
    ```

    The output will be the same irrespective of the machine that the code is running on.

    Parameters:
    :   `path` - the path to query.

    Returns:
    :   the extension of the file or an empty string if none exists or `null` if the fileName is `null`.

    Since:
    :   2.16.0

    Gets the file's last modified time or null if the file does not exist.

    The method provides a workaround for bug [JDK-8177809](https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8177809) where [`File.lastModified()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#lastModified-- "class or interface in java.io")
    looses milliseconds and always ends in 000. This bug is in OpenJDK 8 and 9, and fixed in 11.

    Parameters:
    :   `file` - the file to query.

    Returns:
    :   the file's last modified time.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - Thrown if an I/O error occurs.

    Since:
    :   2.12.0

  * ### sizeOf

    public static long [sizeOf](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/file/PathUtils.html#line-1746)([Path](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") path)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Returns the size of the given file or directory. If the provided [`Path`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") is a regular file, then the file's size is returned. If the argument is a
    directory, then the size of the directory is calculated recursively.

    Note that overflow is not detected, and the return value may be negative if overflow occurs. See [`sizeOfAsBigInteger(Path)`](#sizeOfAsBigInteger(java.nio.file.Path)) for an alternative
    method that does not overflow.

    Parameters:
    :   `path` - the regular file or directory to return the size of, must not be `null`.

    Returns:
    :   the length of the file, or recursive size of the directory, in bytes.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the file is `null`.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the file does not exist.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.

    Since:
    :   2.12.0

    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    alternative method that does not overflow.

    :   `directory` - directory to inspect, must not be `null`.

    Returns:

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the directory is `null`.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.

    Since:

# Class QueueInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [QueueInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/QueueInputStream.html#line-65)
extends [InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

Simple alternative to JDK [`PipedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/PipedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"); queue input stream provides what's written in queue output stream.

To build an instance, use [`QueueInputStream.Builder`](QueueInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

Example usage:

```
QueueInputStream inputStream = new QueueInputStream();
QueueOutputStream outputStream = inputStream.newQueueOutputStream();

outputStream.write("hello world".getBytes(UTF_8));
inputStream.read();
```

Unlike JDK [`PipedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/PipedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") and [`PipedOutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/PipedOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), queue input/output streams may be used safely in a single thread or multiple threads.
Also, unlike JDK classes, no special meaning is attached to initial or current thread. Instances can be used longer after initial threads exited.

Closing a [`QueueInputStream`](QueueInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") has no effect. The methods in this class can be called after the stream has been closed without generating an
[`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io").

Since:
:   2.9.0

See Also:
:   * [`QueueInputStream.Builder`](QueueInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")
    * [`QueueOutputStream`](../output/QueueOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

  * ### read

    public int [read](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/QueueInputStream.html#line-246)(byte[] b,
    int offset,
    int length)

    Reads up to `length` bytes of data from the input stream into
    an array of bytes. The first byte is read while honoring the timeout; the rest are read while *not* honoring
    the timeout. The number of bytes actually read is returned as an integer.

    Overrides:
    :   `read` in class `InputStream`

    Parameters:
    :   `b` - the buffer into which the data is read.
    :   `offset` - the start offset in array `b` at which the data is written.
    :   `length` - the maximum number of bytes to read.

    Returns:
    :   the total number of bytes read into the buffer, or `-1` if there is no more data because the
        end of the stream has been reached.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - If `b` is `null`.
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if thread is interrupted while waiting for the first byte.
    :   `IndexOutOfBoundsException` - if `offset` is negative, `length` is negative, or `length` is
        greater than `b.length - offset`.

    Since:
    :   2.20.0

# Class SizeFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.SizeFileFilter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [SizeFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/SizeFileFilter.html#line-71)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Filters files based on size, can filter either smaller files or
files equal to or larger than a given threshold.

For example, to print all files and directories in the
current directory whose size is greater than 1 MB:

## Using Classic IO

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(new SizeFileFilter(1024 * 1024));
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

## Using NIO

```
final Path dir = PathUtils.current();
final AccumulatorPathVisitor visitor = AccumulatorPathVisitor.withLongCounters(new SizeFileFilter(1024 * 1024));
//
// Walk one directory
Files.walkFileTree(dir, Collections.emptySet(), 1, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
//
visitor.getPathCounters().reset();
//
// Walk directory tree
Files.walkFileTree(dir, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getDirList());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.2

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

public final class [ChecksumInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ChecksumInputStream.html#line-43)
extends [CountingInputStream](CountingInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

Automatically verifies a [`Checksum`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/zip/Checksum.html "class or interface in java.util.zip") value once the stream is exhausted or the count threshold is reached.

If the [`Checksum`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/zip/Checksum.html "class or interface in java.util.zip") does not meet the expected value when exhausted, then the input stream throws an
[`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io").

If you do not need the verification or threshold feature, then use a plain [`CheckedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/zip/CheckedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.util.zip").

To build an instance, use [`ChecksumInputStream.Builder`](ChecksumInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

:   2.16.0

# Class FileEntry

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.monitor.FileEntry

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Serializable`

---

public class [FileEntry](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/monitor/FileEntry.html#line-54)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

The state of a file or directory, capturing the following [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") attributes at a point in time.

* File Name (see [`File.getName()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#getName-- "class or interface in java.io"))
* Exists - whether the file exists or not (see [`File.exists()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#exists-- "class or interface in java.io"))
* Directory - whether the file is a directory or not (see [`File.isDirectory()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#isDirectory-- "class or interface in java.io"))
* Last Modified Date/Time (see [`FileUtils.lastModifiedUnchecked(File)`](../FileUtils.html#lastModifiedUnchecked(java.io.File)))
* Length (see [`File.length()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#length-- "class or interface in java.io")) - directories treated as zero
* Children - contents of a directory (see [`File.listFiles(java.io.FileFilter)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#listFiles-java.io.FileFilter- "class or interface in java.io"))

## Custom Implementations

If the state of additional [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") attributes is required then create a custom
[`FileEntry`](FileEntry.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.monitor") with properties for those attributes. Override the
[`newChildInstance(File)`](#newChildInstance(java.io.File)) to return a new instance of the appropriate type.
You may also want to override the [`refresh(File)`](#refresh(java.io.File)) method.

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   2.0

# Class SymbolicLinkFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.SymbolicLinkFileFilter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [SymbolicLinkFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/SymbolicLinkFileFilter.html#line-67)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

This filter accepts [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")s that are symbolic links.

For example, here is how to print out a list of the real files
within the current directory:

## Using Classic IO

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(SymbolicLinkFileFilter.INSTANCE);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

## Using NIO

```
final Path dir = PathUtils.current();
final AccumulatorPathVisitor visitor = AccumulatorPathVisitor.withLongCounters(SymbolicLinkFileFilter.INSTANCE);
//
// Walk one directory
Files.walkFileTree(dir, Collections.emptySet(), 1, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
//
visitor.getPathCounters().reset();
//
// Walk directory tree
Files.walkFileTree(dir, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getDirList());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   2.11.0

See Also:
:   * [`FileFilterUtils.fileFileFilter()`](FileFilterUtils.html#fileFileFilter())

# Class AccumulatorPathVisitor

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.nio.file.SimpleFileVisitor](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/SimpleFileVisitor.html "class or interface in java.nio.file")<[Path](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file")>

[org.apache.commons.io.file.SimplePathVisitor](SimplePathVisitor.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.file")

[org.apache.commons.io.file.CountingPathVisitor](CountingPathVisitor.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.file")

org.apache.commons.io.file.AccumulatorPathVisitor

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileVisitor<Path>, PathVisitor`

---

public class [AccumulatorPathVisitor](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/file/AccumulatorPathVisitor.html#line-61)
extends [CountingPathVisitor](CountingPathVisitor.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.file")

Accumulates normalized paths during visitation.

Use with care on large file trees as each visited Path element is remembered.

## Example

```
Path dir = PathUtils.current();
// We are interested in files older than one day
Instant cutoff = Instant.now().minus(Duration.ofDays(1));
AccumulatorPathVisitor visitor = AccumulatorPathVisitor.withLongCounters(new AgeFileFilter(cutoff));
//
// Walk one directory
Files.walkFileTree(dir, Collections.emptySet(), 1, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
//
visitor.getPathCounters().reset();
//
// Walk directory tree
Files.walkFileTree(dir, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getDirList());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
```

Since:
:   2.7

    public [XmlStreamWriter](XmlStreamWriter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") [get](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/XmlStreamWriter.Builder.html#line-98)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`XmlStreamWriter`](XmlStreamWriter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getOutputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getOutputStream()) on this builder, otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getOutputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getOutputStream())
    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getCharset()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getCharset())

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to an [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getOutputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getOutputStream()).

    See Also:
    :   * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getOutputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getOutputStream())
        * [`IOSupplier.getUnchecked()`](../function/IOSupplier.html#getUnchecked())

public class [CountingOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/CountingOutputStream.html#line-29)
extends [ProxyOutputStream](ProxyOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

A decorating output stream that counts the number of bytes that have passed
through.

A typical use case would be during debugging, to ensure that data is being
written as expected.

extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Deprecated.

As of 2.6 deprecated without replacement. Use equivalent methods in [`FileStore`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/FileStore.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") instead,
`Files.getFileStore(Paths.get("/home")).getUsableSpace()` or iterate over `FileSystems.getDefault().getFileStores()`

General File System utilities.

This class provides static utility methods for general file system functions not provided before Java 6's [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") class.

The current functions provided are:

* Get the free space on a drive

    [@Deprecated](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Deprecated.html "class or interface in java.lang")
    public static long [freeSpace](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileSystemUtils.html#line-63)([String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") path)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Deprecated.

    Use freeSpaceKb(String) Deprecated from 1.3, may be removed in 2.0

    Gets the number of kibibytes (1024 bytes) available to this Java virtual machine on the given file store.

    Note that some OS's are NOT currently supported, including OS/390, OpenVMS.

    ```
    FileSystemUtils.freeSpace("C:"); // Windows
    FileSystemUtils.freeSpace("/volume"); // *nix
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `path` - the path to get free space for, not null, not empty on Unix

    Returns:
    :   the amount of free drive space on the drive or volume

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the path is invalid.

    Since:
    :   1.1, enhanced OS support in 1.2 and 1.3

    Gets the number of kibibytes (1024 bytes) available to this Java virtual machine on the given file store.

    ```
    FileSystemUtils.freeSpaceKb("/volume"); // *nix
    ```

    :   the amount of free drive space on the drive or volume in kilobytes

    Throws:

    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the path is invalid.

# Class ProxyReader

public abstract class [ProxyReader](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ProxyReader.html#line-38)
extends [FilterReader](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterReader.html "class or interface in java.io")

A Proxy stream which acts as expected, that is it passes the method
calls on to the proxied stream and doesn't change which methods are
being called.

It is an alternative base class to FilterReader
to increase reusability, because FilterReader changes the
methods being called, such as read(char[]) to read(char[], int, int).

* ## Method Details

  * ### afterRead

    protected void [afterRead](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ProxyReader.html#line-67)(int n)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Invoked by the read methods after the proxied call has returned
    successfully. The number of chars returned to the caller (or -1 if
    the end of stream was reached) is given as an argument.

    Subclasses can override this method to add common post-processing
    functionality without having to override all the read methods.
    The default implementation does nothing.

    Note this method is *not* called from [`skip(long)`](#skip(long)) or
    [`reset()`](#reset()). You need to explicitly override those methods if
    you want to add post-processing steps also to them.

    Parameters:
    :   `n` - number of chars read, or -1 if the end of stream was reached

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if the post-processing fails

    Since:
    :   2.0
  * ### beforeRead

    protected void [beforeRead](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ProxyReader.html#line-90)(int n)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Invoked by the read methods before the call is proxied. The number
    of chars that the caller wanted to read (1 for the [`read()`](#read())
    method, buffer length for [`read(char[])`](#read(char%5B%5D)), etc.) is given as
    an argument.

    Subclasses can override this method to add common pre-processing
    functionality without having to override all the read methods.
    The default implementation does nothing.

    Note this method is *not* called from [`skip(long)`](#skip(long)) or
    [`reset()`](#reset()). You need to explicitly override those methods if
    you want to add pre-processing steps also to them.

    Parameters:
    :   `n` - number of chars that the caller asked to be read

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if the pre-processing fails

    Since:
    :   2.0

# Class UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

org.apache.commons.io.input.UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, AutoCloseable`

Direct Known Subclasses:
:   `UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream`

---

public class [UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.html#line-45)
extends [InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

An unsynchronized version of [`FilterInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), not thread-safe.

Wraps an existing [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") and performs some transformation on the input data while it is being read. Transformations can be anything from a
simple byte-wise filtering input data to an on-the-fly compression or decompression of the underlying stream. Input streams that wrap another input stream
and provide some additional functionality on top of it usually inherit from this class.

To build an instance, use [`UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.Builder`](UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

Provenance: Apache Harmony and modified.

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.Builder`](UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")
    * [`FilterInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

# Class ReversedLinesFileReader

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.input.ReversedLinesFileReader

All Implemented Interfaces:

public class [ReversedLinesFileReader](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ReversedLinesFileReader.html#line-66)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Closeable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html "class or interface in java.io"), [IOIterable](../function/IOIterable.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.function")<[String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang")>

Reads lines in a file reversely (similar to a BufferedReader, but starting at the last line). Useful for e.g. searching in log files.

To build an instance, use [`ReversedLinesFileReader.Builder`](ReversedLinesFileReader.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

For example:

```
try (ReversedLinesFileReader reader = ReversedLinesFileReader.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setBufferSize(4096)
  .setCharset(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
  .get()) {
     reader.forEach(line -> System.out.println(line));
}
```

Since:
:   2.2

See Also:
:   * [`ReversedLinesFileReader.Builder`](ReversedLinesFileReader.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

# Class WriterOutputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

org.apache.commons.io.output.WriterOutputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, Flushable, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [WriterOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/WriterOutputStream.html#line-83)
extends [OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

[`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") implementation that transforms a byte stream to a character stream using a specified charset encoding and writes the resulting stream to
a [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io"). The stream is transformed using a [`CharsetDecoder`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/CharsetDecoder.html "class or interface in java.nio.charset") object, guaranteeing that all charset encodings supported by the JRE are handled
correctly.

The output of the [`CharsetDecoder`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/CharsetDecoder.html "class or interface in java.nio.charset") is buffered using a fixed size buffer. This implies that the data is written to the underlying [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") in
chunks that are no larger than the size of this buffer. By default, the buffer is flushed only when it overflows or when [`flush()`](#flush()) or [`close()`](#close())
is called. In general there is therefore no need to wrap the underlying [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") in a [`BufferedWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedWriter.html "class or interface in java.io"). [`WriterOutputStream`](WriterOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") can
also be instructed to flush the buffer after each write operation. In this case, all available data is written immediately to the underlying [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io"),
implying that the current position of the [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") is correlated to the current position of the [`WriterOutputStream`](WriterOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

[`WriterOutputStream`](WriterOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") implements the inverse transformation of [`OutputStreamWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStreamWriter.html "class or interface in java.io"); in the following example, writing to `out2`
would have the same result as writing to `out` directly (provided that the byte sequence is legal with respect to the charset encoding):

To build an instance, use [`WriterOutputStream.Builder`](WriterOutputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

```
OutputStream out = ...
Charset cs = ...
OutputStreamWriter writer = new OutputStreamWriter(out, cs);
WriterOutputStream out2 = WriterOutputStream.builder()
  .setWriter(writer)
  .setCharset(cs)
  .get();
```

[`WriterOutputStream`](WriterOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") implements the same transformation as [`InputStreamReader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStreamReader.html "class or interface in java.io"), except that the control flow is reversed: both classes
transform a byte stream into a character stream, but [`InputStreamReader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStreamReader.html "class or interface in java.io") pulls data from the underlying stream, while
[`WriterOutputStream`](WriterOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") pushes it to the underlying stream.

Note that while there are use cases where there is no alternative to using this class, very often the need to use this class is an indication of a flaw in
the design of the code. This class is typically used in situations where an existing API only accepts an [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") object, but where the stream is
known to represent character data that must be decoded for further use.

Instances of [`WriterOutputStream`](WriterOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") are not thread safe.

Since:
:   2.0

See Also:
:   * [`WriterOutputStream.Builder`](WriterOutputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")
    * [`ReaderInputStream`](../input/ReaderInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

# Class TaggedInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [TaggedInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/TaggedInputStream.html#line-69)
extends [ProxyInputStream](ProxyInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

An input stream decorator that tags potential exceptions so that the
stream that caused the exception can easily be identified. This is
done by using the [`TaggedIOException`](../TaggedIOException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") class to wrap all thrown
[`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")s. See below for an example of using this class.

```
TaggedInputStream stream = new TaggedInputStream(...);
try {
    // Processing that may throw an IOException either from this stream
    // or from some other IO activity like temporary files, etc.
    processStream(stream);
} catch (IOException e) {
    if (stream.isCauseOf(e)) {
        // The exception was caused by this stream.
        // Use e.getCause() to get the original exception.
    } else {
        // The exception was caused by something else.
    }
}
```

Alternatively, the [`throwIfCauseOf(Throwable)`](#throwIfCauseOf(java.lang.Throwable)) method can be
used to let higher levels of code handle the exception caused by this
stream while other processing errors are being taken care of at this
lower level.

```
TaggedInputStream stream = new TaggedInputStream(...);
try {
    processStream(stream);
} catch (IOException e) {
    stream.throwIfCauseOf(e);
    // ... or process the exception that was caused by something else
}
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   2.0

See Also:
:   * [`TaggedIOException`](../TaggedIOException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io")

# Class FileCleaningTracker

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.FileCleaningTracker

---

public class [FileCleaningTracker](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileCleaningTracker.html#line-46)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Keeps track of files awaiting deletion, and deletes them when an associated
marker object is reclaimed by the garbage collector.

This utility creates a background thread to handle file deletion.
Each file to be deleted is registered with a handler object.
When the handler object is garbage collected, the file is deleted.

In an environment with multiple class loaders (a servlet container, for
example), you should consider stopping the background thread if it is no
longer needed. This is done by invoking the method
`exitWhenFinished`, typically in
`javax.servlet.ServletContextListener.contextDestroyed(javax.servlet.ServletContextEvent)` or similar.

* ## Method Details

  * ### exitWhenFinished

    public void [exitWhenFinished](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileCleaningTracker.html#line-208)()

    Call this method to cause the file cleaner thread to terminate when
    there are no more objects being tracked for deletion.

    In a simple environment, you don't need this method as the file cleaner
    thread will simply exit when the JVM exits. In a more complex environment,
    with multiple class loaders (such as an application server), you should be
    aware that the file cleaner thread will continue running even if the class
    loader it was started from terminates. This can constitute a memory leak.

    For example, suppose that you have developed a web application, which
    contains the commons-io jar file in your WEB-INF/lib directory. In other
    words, the FileCleaner class is loaded through the class loader of your
    web application. If the web application is terminated, but the servlet
    container is still running, then the file cleaner thread will still exist,
    posing a memory leak.

    This method allows the thread to be terminated. Simply call this method
    in the resource cleanup code, such as
    `javax.servlet.ServletContextListener.contextDestroyed(javax.servlet.ServletContextEvent)`.
    Once called, no new objects can be tracked by the file cleaner.
