# Class AbstractOrigin<T, B extends AbstractOrigin<T,B>>

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.build.AbstractSupplier](AbstractSupplier.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<T,B>

org.apache.commons.io.build.AbstractOrigin<T,B>

Type Parameters:
:   `T` - the type produced by the builder.
:   `B` - the concrete builder subclass type.

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `IOSupplier<T>`

Direct Known Subclasses:
:   `AbstractOrigin.AbstractRandomAccessFileOrigin, AbstractOrigin.ByteArrayOrigin, AbstractOrigin.ChannelOrigin, AbstractOrigin.CharSequenceOrigin, AbstractOrigin.FileOrigin, AbstractOrigin.InputStreamOrigin, AbstractOrigin.OutputStreamOrigin, AbstractOrigin.PathOrigin, AbstractOrigin.ReaderOrigin, AbstractOrigin.URIOrigin, AbstractOrigin.WriterOrigin`

---

public abstract class [AbstractOrigin](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/build/AbstractOrigin.html#line-347)<T, B extends AbstractOrigin<T,B>>
extends [AbstractSupplier](AbstractSupplier.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<T,B>

Abstracts and wraps an *origin* for builders, where an origin is a `byte[]`, [`Channel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/Channel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels"), [`CharSequence`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html "class or interface in java.lang"), [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io"),
[`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), [`IORandomAccessFile`](../IORandomAccessFile.html "class in org.apache.commons.io"), [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), [`Path`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file"), [`RandomAccessFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html "class or interface in java.io"), [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io"), [`URI`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/net/URI.html "class or interface in java.net"),
or [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io").

An origin represents where bytes/characters come from or go to. Concrete subclasses
expose only the operations that make sense for the underlying source or sink; invoking an unsupported operation
results in [`UnsupportedOperationException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/UnsupportedOperationException.html "class or interface in java.lang") (see, for example, [`getFile()`](#getFile()) and [`getPath()`](#getPath())).

An instance doesn't own its origin, it holds on to it to allow conversions. There are two use cases related to resource management for a Builder:

* A client allocates a [Closeable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html "class or interface in java.io") (or [AutoCloseable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/AutoCloseable.html "class or interface in java.lang")) resource, creates a Builder, and gives the Builder that resource by calling a
  setter method. No matter what happens next, the client is responsible for releasing the resource (`Closeable.close()`). In this case, the origin
  wraps but doesn't own the closeable resource. There is no transfer of ownership.
* A client creates a Builder and gives it a non-Closeable object, like a File or a Path. The client then calls the Builder's factory method
  (like [get()](#get())), and that call returns a Closeable or a resource that requires releasing in some other way. No matter what happens next, the
  client is responsible for releasing that resource. In this case, the origin doesn't wrap a closeable resource.

In both cases, the client causes the allocation and is responsible for releasing the resource.

The table below summarizes which views and conversions are supported for each origin type.
Column headers show the target view; cells indicate whether that view is available from the origin in that row.

Supported Conversions

| Origin Type | byte[] | CS | File | Path | RAF | IS | Reader | RBC | OS | Writer | WBC | Channel type2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| byte[] | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | SBC |
| [`CharSequence`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html "class or interface in java.lang") (CS) | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✔1 | ✔ | ✔1 | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | SBC |
| [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | FC |
| [`Path`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | FC |
| [`IORandomAccessFile`](../IORandomAccessFile.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | FC |
| [`RandomAccessFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html "class or interface in java.io") (RAF) | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | FC |
| [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") (IS) | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | RBC |
| [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✔1 | ✔ | ✔1 | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | RBC |
| [`ReadableByteChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/ReadableByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels") (RBC) | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | RBC |
| [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") (OS) | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | WBC |
| [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✔1 | ✔ | ✔1 | WBC |
| [`WritableByteChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/WritableByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels") (WBC) | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | WBC |
| [`URI`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/net/URI.html "class or interface in java.net") (FileSystem) | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | FC |
| [`URI`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/net/URI.html "class or interface in java.net") (http/https) | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✖ | ✖ | ✖ | RBC |

**Legend**

* ✔ = Supported
* ✖ = Not supported (throws [`UnsupportedOperationException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/UnsupportedOperationException.html "class or interface in java.lang"))
* 1 = Characters are converted to bytes using the default [`Charset`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/Charset.html "class or interface in java.nio.charset").
* 2 Minimum channel type provided by the origin:
  * RBC = [ReadableByteChannel](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/ReadableByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
  * WBC = [WritableByteChannel](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/WritableByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
  * SBC = [SeekableByteChannel](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/SeekableByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
  * FC = [FileChannel](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/FileChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")The exact channel type may be a subtype of the minimum shown.

Since:
:   2.12.0

# Class NameFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.NameFileFilter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [NameFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/NameFileFilter.html#line-73)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Filters file names for a certain name.

For example, to print all files and directories in the
current directory whose name is `Test`:

## Using Classic IO

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(new NameFileFilter("Test"));
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

## Using NIO

```
final Path dir = PathUtils.current();
final AccumulatorPathVisitor visitor = AccumulatorPathVisitor.withLongCounters(new NameFileFilter("Test"));
//
// Walk one directory
Files.walkFileTree(dir, Collections.emptySet(), 1, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
//
visitor.getPathCounters().reset();
//
// Walk directory tree
Files.walkFileTree(dir, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getDirList());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.0

public class [TeeInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/TeeInputStream.html#line-40)
extends [ProxyInputStream](ProxyInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

InputStream proxy that transparently writes a copy of all bytes read
from the proxied stream to a given OutputStream. Using [`ProxyInputStream.skip(long)`](ProxyInputStream.html#skip(long))
or [`ProxyInputStream.mark(int)`](ProxyInputStream.html#mark(int))/[`ProxyInputStream.reset()`](ProxyInputStream.html#reset()) on the stream will result on some
bytes from the input stream being skipped or duplicated in the output
stream.

The proxied input stream is closed when the [`close()`](#close()) method is
called on this proxy. You may configure whether the input stream closes the
output stream.

Since:
:   1.4

See Also:
:   * [`ObservableInputStream`](ObservableInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

public class [ProxyOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/ProxyOutputStream.html#line-34)
extends [FilterOutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

A Proxy stream which acts as expected, that is it passes the method calls on to the proxied stream and doesn't change which methods are being called. It is
an alternative base class to FilterOutputStream to increase reusability.

See the protected methods for ways in which a subclass can easily decorate a stream with custom pre-, post- or error processing functionality.

* ## Method Details

  * ### afterWrite

    protected void [afterWrite](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/ProxyOutputStream.html#line-103)(int n)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Invoked by the write methods after the proxied call has returned successfully. The number of bytes written (1 for the [`write(int)`](#write(int)) method, buffer
    length for [`write(byte[])`](#write(byte%5B%5D)), etc.) is given as an argument.

    Subclasses can override this method to add common post-processing functionality without having to override all the write methods. The default
    implementation does nothing.

    Parameters:
    :   `n` - number of bytes written.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if the post-processing fails.

    Since:
    :   2.0
  * ### beforeWrite

    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

public final class [UncheckedFilterInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UncheckedFilterInputStream.html#line-40)
extends [FilterInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

A [`BufferedReader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedReader.html "class or interface in java.io") that throws [`UncheckedIOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/UncheckedIOException.html "class or interface in java.io") instead of [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io").

To build an instance, use [`UncheckedFilterInputStream.Builder`](UncheckedFilterInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

Since:

public final class [UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.html#line-40)
extends [AbstractByteArrayOutputStream](AbstractByteArrayOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")<[UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream](UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")>

Implements a version of [`AbstractByteArrayOutputStream`](AbstractByteArrayOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") **without** any concurrent thread safety.

To build an instance, use [`UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.Builder`](UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

Since:
:   2.7

See Also:
:   * [`UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.Builder`](UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

  * ### toBufferedInputStream

    public static [InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") [toBufferedInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.html#line-124)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Fetches entire contents of an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") and represent same data as result InputStream.

    This method is useful where,

    * Source InputStream is slow.
    * It has network resources associated, so we cannot keep it open for long time.
    * It has network timeout associated.

    It can be used in favor of [`toByteArray()`](#toByteArray()), since it avoids unnecessary allocation and copy of byte[].  
    This method buffers the input internally, so there is no need to use a [`BufferedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - Stream to be fully buffered.

    Returns:
    :   A fully buffered stream.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.

public static class [UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.html#line-84)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream](UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.Builder](UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream`](UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

Using File IO:

```
UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream s = UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.builder()
  .setFile(file)
  .setBufferSize(8192)
  .get();
```

Using NIO Path:

```
UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream s = UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setBufferSize(8192)
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream`](UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()) on this builder, otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream())
    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getBufferSize()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getBufferSize())

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()).

    See Also:
    :   * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream())
        * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getBufferSize()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getBufferSize())

public abstract class [AbstractFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/AbstractFileFilter.html#line-42)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [IOFileFilter](IOFileFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter"), [PathVisitor](../file/PathVisitor.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.file")

Abstracts the implementation of the [`FileFilter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileFilter.html "class or interface in java.io") (IO), [`FilenameFilter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilenameFilter.html "class or interface in java.io") (IO), [`PathFilter`](../file/PathFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.file") (NIO)
interfaces via our own [`IOFileFilter`](IOFileFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter") interface.

Note that a subclass MUST override one of the `accept` methods, otherwise that subclass will infinitely loop.

Since:
:   1.0

extends [OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

Always throws an exception from all [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") methods where [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io") is declared.

This class is mostly useful for testing error handling.

Since:
:   2.0

public class [ClassLoaderObjectInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ClassLoaderObjectInputStream.html#line-35)
extends [ObjectInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/ObjectInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

A special ObjectInputStream that loads a class based on a specified
[`ClassLoader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/ClassLoader.html "class or interface in java.lang") rather than the system default.

This is useful in dynamic container environments.

Since:
:   1.1

# Class ExtensionFileComparator

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.comparator.ExtensionFileComparator

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Serializable, Comparator<File>`

---

public class [ExtensionFileComparator](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/comparator/ExtensionFileComparator.html#line-59)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Compare the file name **extensions** for order
(see [`FilenameUtils.getExtension(String)`](../FilenameUtils.html#getExtension(java.lang.String))).

This comparator can be used to sort lists or arrays of files
by their file extension either in a case-sensitive, case-insensitive or
system dependent case-sensitive way. A number of singleton instances
are provided for the various case sensitivity options (using [`IOCase`](../IOCase.html "enum in org.apache.commons.io"))
and the reverse of those options.

Example of a *case-sensitive* file extension sort using the
[`EXTENSION_COMPARATOR`](#EXTENSION_COMPARATOR) singleton instance:

```
      List<File> list = ...
      ((AbstractFileComparator) ExtensionFileComparator.EXTENSION_COMPARATOR).sort(list);
```

Example of a *reverse case-insensitive* file extension sort using the
[`EXTENSION_INSENSITIVE_REVERSE`](#EXTENSION_INSENSITIVE_REVERSE) singleton instance:

```
      File[] array = ...
      ((AbstractFileComparator) ExtensionFileComparator.EXTENSION_INSENSITIVE_REVERSE).sort(array);
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.4

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.io.comparator.ExtensionFileComparator)

public class [CloseShieldInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/CloseShieldInputStream.html#line-31)
extends [ProxyInputStream](ProxyInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

Proxy stream that prevents the underlying input stream from being closed.

This class is typically used in cases where an input stream needs to be
passed to a component that wants to explicitly close the stream even if more
input would still be available to other components.

# Class BoundedInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

All Implemented Interfaces:

---

public class [BoundedInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/BoundedInputStream.html#line-89)
extends [ProxyInputStream](ProxyInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

Reads bytes up to a maximum count and stops once reached.

To build an instance: Use the [`builder()`](#builder()) to access all features.

By default, a [`BoundedInputStream`](BoundedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") is *unbound*; so make sure to call `BoundedInputStream.AbstractBuilder.setMaxCount(long)`.

You can find out how many bytes this stream has seen so far by calling [`getCount()`](#getCount()). This value reflects bytes read and skipped.

## Using a ServletInputStream

A `ServletInputStream` can block if you try to read content that isn't there
because it doesn't know whether the content hasn't arrived yet or whether the content has finished. Initialize an [`BoundedInputStream`](BoundedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") with the
`Content-Length` sent in the `ServletInputStream`'s header, this stop it from blocking, providing it's been sent with a correct content
length in the first place.

## Using NIO

```
BoundedInputStream s = BoundedInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(Paths.get("MyFile.xml"))
  .setMaxCount(1024)
  .setPropagateClose(false)
  .get();
```

## Using IO

```
BoundedInputStream s = BoundedInputStream.builder()
  .setFile(new File("MyFile.xml"))
  .setMaxCount(1024)
  .setPropagateClose(false)
  .get();
```

## Counting Bytes

You can set the running count when building, which is most useful when starting from another stream:

```
InputStream in = ...;
BoundedInputStream s = BoundedInputStream.builder()
  .setInputStream(in)
  .setCount(12)
  .setMaxCount(1024)
  .setPropagateClose(false)
  .get();
```

## Listening for the maximum count reached

```
BoundedInputStream s = BoundedInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(Paths.get("MyFile.xml"))
  .setMaxCount(1024)
  .setOnMaxCount((max, count) -> System.out.printf("Maximum count %,d reached with a last read count of %,d%n", max, count))
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.0

See Also:
:   * [`BoundedInputStream.Builder`](BoundedInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

public static class [BOMInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/BOMInputStream.html#line-130)
extends [ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder](ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")<[BOMInputStream](BOMInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [BOMInputStream.Builder](BOMInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`BOMInputStream`](BOMInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

## Using NIO

```
BOMInputStream s = BOMInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(Paths.get("MyFile.xml"))
  .setByteOrderMarks(ByteOrderMark.UTF_8)
  .setInclude(false)
  .get();
```

## Using IO

```
BOMInputStream s = BOMInputStream.builder()
  .setFile(new File("MyFile.xml"))
  .setByteOrderMarks(ByteOrderMark.UTF_8)
  .setInclude(false)
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()).

* ## Constructor Details

  * ### CharSequenceReader

    public [CharSequenceReader](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/CharSequenceReader.html#line-87)([CharSequence](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html "class or interface in java.lang") charSequence)

    Constructs a new instance with the specified character sequence.

    Parameters:
    :   `charSequence` - The character sequence, may be `null`
  * ### CharSequenceReader

    public [CharSequenceReader](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/CharSequenceReader.html#line-106)([CharSequence](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html "class or interface in java.lang") charSequence,
    int start)

    Constructs a new instance with a portion of the specified character sequence.

    The start index is not strictly enforced to be within the bounds of the
    character sequence. This allows the character sequence to grow or shrink
    in size without risking any [`IndexOutOfBoundsException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/IndexOutOfBoundsException.html "class or interface in java.lang") to be thrown.
    Instead, if the character sequence grows smaller than the start index, this
    instance will act as if all characters have been read.

    Parameters:
    :   `charSequence` - The character sequence, may be `null`
    :   `start` - The start index in the character sequence, inclusive

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the start index is negative

    Since:
    :   2.7
  * ### CharSequenceReader

    public [CharSequenceReader](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/CharSequenceReader.html#line-128)([CharSequence](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html "class or interface in java.lang") charSequence,
    int start,
    int end)

    Constructs a new instance with a portion of the specified character sequence.

    The start and end indexes are not strictly enforced to be within the bounds
    of the character sequence. This allows the character sequence to grow or shrink
    in size without risking any [`IndexOutOfBoundsException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/IndexOutOfBoundsException.html "class or interface in java.lang") to be thrown.
    Instead, if the character sequence grows smaller than the start index, this
    instance will act as if all characters have been read; if the character sequence
    grows smaller than the end, this instance will use the actual character sequence
    length.

    Parameters:
    :   `charSequence` - The character sequence, may be `null`
    :   `start` - The start index in the character sequence, inclusive
    :   `end` - The end index in the character sequence, exclusive

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the start index is negative, or if the end index is smaller than the start index

    Since:
    :   2.7

# Class DeferredFileOutputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

[org.apache.commons.io.output.ThresholdingOutputStream](ThresholdingOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

org.apache.commons.io.output.DeferredFileOutputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, Flushable, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [DeferredFileOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/DeferredFileOutputStream.html#line-52)
extends [ThresholdingOutputStream](ThresholdingOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

An output stream which will retain data in memory until a specified threshold is reached, and only then commit it to disk. If the stream is closed before the
threshold is reached, the data will not be written to disk at all.

To build an instance, use [`DeferredFileOutputStream.Builder`](DeferredFileOutputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

The caller is responsible for deleting the output file ([`getFile()`](#getFile()), [`getPath()`](#getPath())) created by a DeferredFileOutputStream when the caller only
configured a prefix.

The caller is responsible for deleting the output file passed to a constructor or builder through [`DeferredFileOutputStream.Builder.setOutputFile(File)`](DeferredFileOutputStream.Builder.html#setOutputFile(java.io.File)) or
[`DeferredFileOutputStream.Builder.setOutputFile(Path)`](DeferredFileOutputStream.Builder.html#setOutputFile(java.nio.file.Path)).

This class originated in FileUpload processing. In this use case, you do not know in advance the size of the file being uploaded. If the file is small you
want to store it in memory (for speed), but if the file is large you want to store it to file (to avoid memory issues).

See Also:
:   * [`DeferredFileOutputStream.Builder`](DeferredFileOutputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

    public [DeferredFileOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/DeferredFileOutputStream.html#line-348)(int threshold,

  * ### getFile

    public [File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") [getFile](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/DeferredFileOutputStream.html#line-386)()

    Gets either the output File specified in the constructor or the temporary File created or null.

    If the constructor specifying the File is used then it returns that same output File, even when threshold has not been reached.

    If constructor specifying a temporary File prefix/suffix is used then the temporary File created once the threshold is reached is returned if the
    threshold was not reached then `null` is returned.

    Returns:
    :   The File for this output stream, or `null` if no such File exists.
  * ### getPath

    public [Path](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") [getPath](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/DeferredFileOutputStream.html#line-403)()

    Gets either the output Path specified in the constructor or the temporary Path created or null.

    If the constructor specifying the file is used then it returns that same output Path, even when threshold has not been reached.

    If constructor specifying a temporary Path prefix/suffix is used then the temporary Path created once the threshold is reached is returned if the
    threshold was not reached then `null` is returned.

    :   The Path for this output stream, or `null` if no such Path exists.

    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

  * ### toInputStream

    public [InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") [toInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/DeferredFileOutputStream.html#line-462)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Converts the current contents of this byte stream to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"). If the data for this output stream has been retained in memory, the returned
    stream is backed by buffers of `this` stream, avoiding memory allocation and copy, thus saving space and time.  
    Otherwise, the returned stream will be one that is created from the data that has been committed to disk.

    Returns:
    :   the current contents of this output stream.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if this stream is not yet closed or an error occurs.

    Since:
    :   2.9.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`ByteArrayOutputStream.toInputStream()`](ByteArrayOutputStream.html#toInputStream())

public final class [Uncheck](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/function/Uncheck.html#line-29)

# Class CanReadFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [CanReadFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/CanReadFileFilter.html#line-68)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

This filter accepts [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")s that can be read.

Example, showing how to print out a list of the current directory's *readable* files:

## Using Classic IO

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(CanReadFileFilter.CAN_READ);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

Example, showing how to print out a list of the current directory's *un-readable* files:

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(CanReadFileFilter.CANNOT_READ);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

Example, showing how to print out a list of the current directory's *read-only* files:

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(CanReadFileFilter.READ_ONLY);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.3

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.CanReadFileFilter)

public interface [IOTriFunction](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/function/IOTriFunction.html#line-39)<T,U,V,R>

[`IOFunction`](IOFunction.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.function").

This is a [functional interface](package-summary.html) whose functional method is
[`apply(Object, Object, Object)`](#apply(T,U,V)).

public static class [ReadAheadInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ReadAheadInputStream.html#line-71)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[ReadAheadInputStream](ReadAheadInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [ReadAheadInputStream.Builder](ReadAheadInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`ReadAheadInputStream`](ReadAheadInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

For example:

```
ReadAheadInputStream s = ReadAheadInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setExecutorService(Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor(ReadAheadInputStream::newThread))
  .get();
```

# Class BoundedReader

All Implemented Interfaces:

---

public class [BoundedReader](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/BoundedReader.html#line-39)
extends [Reader](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io")

A reader that imposes a limit to the number of characters that can be read from an underlying reader, returning EOF
when this limit is reached, regardless of state of underlying reader.

One use case is to avoid overrunning the readAheadLimit supplied to [`Reader.mark(int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html#mark-int- "class or interface in java.io"), since reading
too many characters removes the ability to do a successful reset.

Since:
:   2.5

# Class FileUtils

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.FileUtils

---

public class [FileUtils](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-118)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

General file manipulation utilities.

Facilities are provided in the following areas:

* writing to a file* reading from a file* make a directory including parent directories* copying files and directories* deleting files and directories* converting to and from a URL* listing files and directories by filter and extension* comparing file content* file last changed date* calculating a checksum

Note that a specific charset should be specified whenever possible. Relying on the platform default means that the
code is Locale-dependent. Only use the default if the files are known to always use the platform default.

[`SecurityException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/SecurityException.html "class or interface in java.lang") are not documented in the Javadoc.

Provenance: Excalibur, Alexandria, Commons-Utils

* ## Method Details

  * ### byteCountToDisplaySize

    public static [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") [byteCountToDisplaySize](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-240)([BigInteger](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/math/BigInteger.html "class or interface in java.math") size)

    Returns a human-readable version of the file size, where the input represents a specific number of bytes.

    If the size is over 1GB, the size is returned as the number of whole GB, the size is rounded down to the
    nearest GB boundary.

    Similarly for the 1MB and 1KB boundaries.

    Parameters:
    :   `size` - the number of bytes

    Returns:
    :   a human-readable display value (includes units - QB, RB, YB, ZB, EB, PB, TB, GB, MB, KB or bytes)

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the given [`BigInteger`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/math/BigInteger.html "class or interface in java.math") is `null`.

    Since:
    :   2.4

    See Also:
    :   * [IO-226 - should the rounding be changed?](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/IO-226)
  * ### byteCountToDisplaySize

    public static [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") [byteCountToDisplaySize](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-284)(long size)

    public static [Checksum](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/zip/Checksum.html "class or interface in java.util.zip") [checksum](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-368)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") file,

    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Computes the checksum of a file using the specified checksum object. Multiple files may be checked using one
    [`Checksum`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/zip/Checksum.html "class or interface in java.util.zip") instance if desired simply by reusing the same checksum object. For example:

    ```
    long checksum = FileUtils.checksum(file, new CRC32()).getValue();
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `file` - the file to checksum, must not be `null`
    :   `checksum` - the checksum object to be used, must not be `null`

    Returns:
    :   the checksum specified, updated with the content of the file

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the given [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") is `null`.
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the given [`Checksum`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/zip/Checksum.html "class or interface in java.util.zip") is `null`.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the given [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") is not a file.
    :   `FileNotFoundException` - if the file does not exist
    :   `IOException` - if an IO error occurs reading the file.

    Since:
    :   1.3

  * ### copyDirectory

    public static void [copyDirectory](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-553)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") srcDir,
    [File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") destDir)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Copies a whole directory to a new location, preserving the file dates.

    This method copies the specified directory and all its child directories and files to the specified destination.
    The destination is the new location and name of the directory. That is, copying /home/bar to /tmp/bang
    copies the contents of /home/bar into /tmp/bang. It does not create /tmp/bang/bar.

    The destination directory is created if it does not exist. If the destination directory does exist, then this
    method merges the source with the destination, with the source taking precedence.

    **Note:** This method tries to preserve the file's last
    modified date/times using [`BasicFileAttributeView.setTimes(FileTime, FileTime, FileTime)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/attribute/BasicFileAttributeView.html#setTimes-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime- "class or interface in java.nio.file.attribute"). However it is
    not guaranteed that the operation will succeed. If the modification operation fails, it falls back to
    [`File.setLastModified(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#setLastModified-long- "class or interface in java.io"). If that fails, the method throws IOException.

    Symbolic links in the source directory are copied to new symbolic links in the destination
    directory that point to the original target. The target of the link is not copied unless
    it is also under the source directory. Even if it is under the source directory, the new symbolic
    link in the destination points to the original target in the source directory, not to the
    newly created copy of the target.

    Parameters:
    :   `srcDir` - an existing directory to copy, must not be `null`.
    :   `destDir` - the new directory, must not be `null`.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if any of the given [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")s are `null`.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if `srcDir` exists but is not a directory,
        the source and the destination directory are the same
    :   `FileNotFoundException` - if the source does not exist.
    :   `IOException` - if an error occurs, the destination is not writable, or setting the last-modified time didn't succeed

    Since:
    :   1.1
  * ### copyDirectory

    public static void [copyDirectory](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-581)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") srcDir,
    [File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") destDir,
    boolean preserveFileDate)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Copies a whole directory to a new location.

    This method copies the contents of the specified source directory to within the specified destination directory.

    The destination directory is created if it does not exist. If the destination directory does exist, then this
    method merges the source with the destination, with the source taking precedence.

    **Note:** Setting `preserveFileDate` to `true` tries to preserve the files' last
    modified date/times using [`File.setLastModified(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#setLastModified-long- "class or interface in java.io"). However it is not guaranteed that those operations
    will succeed. If the modification operation fails, the method throws IOException.

    Parameters:
    :   `srcDir` - an existing directory to copy, must not be `null`.
    :   `destDir` - the new directory, must not be `null`.
    :   `preserveFileDate` - true if the file date of the copy should be the same as the original.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if `srcDir` exists but is not a directory, or
        the source and the destination directory are the same
    :   `FileNotFoundException` - if the source does not exist.
    :   `IOException` - if an error occurs, the destination is not writable, or setting the last-modified time didn't succeed

    Since:
    :   1.1
  * ### copyDirectory

    public static void [copyDirectory](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-631)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") srcDir,
    [File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") destDir,
    [FileFilter](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileFilter.html "class or interface in java.io") filter)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Copies a filtered directory to a new location preserving the file dates.

    This method copies the contents of the specified source directory to within the specified destination directory.

    The destination directory is created if it does not exist. If the destination directory does exist, then this
    method merges the source with the destination, with the source taking precedence.

    **Note:** This method tries to preserve the files' last modified date/times using
    [`File.setLastModified(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#setLastModified-long- "class or interface in java.io"). However it is not guaranteed that those operations will succeed. If the
    modification operation fails, the method throws IOException.

    **Example: Copy directories only**

    ```
    // only copy the directory structure
    FileUtils.copyDirectory(srcDir, destDir, DirectoryFileFilter.DIRECTORY);
    ```

    **Example: Copy directories and txt files**

    ```
    // Create a filter for ".txt" files
    IOFileFilter txtSuffixFilter = FileFilterUtils.suffixFileFilter(".txt");
    IOFileFilter txtFiles = FileFilterUtils.andFileFilter(FileFileFilter.INSTANCE, txtSuffixFilter);

    // Create a filter for either directories or ".txt" files
    FileFilter filter = FileFilterUtils.orFileFilter(DirectoryFileFilter.DIRECTORY, txtFiles);

    // Copy using the filter
    FileUtils.copyDirectory(srcDir, destDir, filter);
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `srcDir` - an existing directory to copy, must not be `null`.
    :   `destDir` - the new directory, must not be `null`.
    :   `filter` - the filter to apply, null means copy all directories and files should be the same as the original.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if any of the given [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")s are `null`.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if `srcDir` exists but is not a directory, or
        the source and the destination directory are the same
    :   `FileNotFoundException` - if the source does not exist.
    :   `IOException` - if an error occurs, the destination is not writable, or setting the last-modified time didn't succeed

    Since:
    :   1.4

    public static void [copyFile](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-810)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") srcFile,

    Copies a file to a new location preserving the file date.

    This method copies the contents of the specified source file to the specified destination file. The directory
    holding the destination file is created if it does not exist. If the destination file exists, then this method
    overwrites it. A symbolic link is resolved before copying so the new file is not a link.

    **Note:** This method tries to preserve the file's last modified date/times using

    modified date/times using [`BasicFileAttributeView.setTimes(FileTime, FileTime, FileTime)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/attribute/BasicFileAttributeView.html#setTimes-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime- "class or interface in java.nio.file.attribute").     [`File.setLastModified(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#setLastModified-long- "class or interface in java.io"), and if that fails, the method throws IOException.

    :   `srcFile` - an existing file to copy, must not be `null`.
    :   `destFile` - the new file, must not be `null`.
    :   `preserveFileDate` - true if the file date of the copy should be the same as the original.

    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Copies the contents of a file to a new location.

    This method copies the contents of the specified source file to the specified destination file. The directory
    holding the destination file is created if it does not exist. If the destination file exists, you can overwrite
    it with [`StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/StandardCopyOption.html#REPLACE_EXISTING "class or interface in java.nio.file").

    By default, a symbolic link is resolved before copying so the new file is not a link.
    To copy symbolic links as links, you can pass `LinkOption.NO_FOLLOW_LINKS` as the last argument.

    **Note:** Setting `preserveFileDate` to `true` tries to preserve the file's last
    modified date/times using [`BasicFileAttributeView.setTimes(FileTime, FileTime, FileTime)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/attribute/BasicFileAttributeView.html#setTimes-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime- "class or interface in java.nio.file.attribute"). However, it is
    not guaranteed that the operation will succeed. If the modification operation fails, it falls back to
    [`File.setLastModified(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#setLastModified-long- "class or interface in java.io"), and if that fails, the method throws IOException.

    Parameters:
    :   `srcFile` - an existing file to copy, must not be `null`.
    :   `destFile` - the new file, must not be `null`.
    :   `preserveFileDate` - true if the file date of the copy should be the same as the original.
    :   `copyOptions` - options specifying how the copy should be done, for example [`StandardCopyOption`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/StandardCopyOption.html "class or interface in java.nio.file").

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if any of the given [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")s are `null`.
    :   `FileNotFoundException` - if the source does not exist.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if `srcFile` or `destFile` is not a file
    :   `IOException` - if the output file length is not the same as the input file length after the copy completes.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs, setting the last-modified time didn't succeed,
        or the destination is not writable

    Since:
    :   2.8.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`copyFileToDirectory(File, File, boolean)`](#copyFileToDirectory(java.io.File,java.io.File,boolean))

    This method copies the source file or directory, along with all its contents, to a directory of the same name in the
    specified destination directory.

    The destination directory is created if it does not exist. If the destination directory does exist, then this method
    merges the source with the destination, with the source taking precedence.

    **Note:** Setting `preserveFileDate` to `true` tries to preserve the file's last
    modified date/times using [`BasicFileAttributeView.setTimes(FileTime, FileTime, FileTime)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/attribute/BasicFileAttributeView.html#setTimes-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime-java.nio.file.attribute.FileTime- "class or interface in java.nio.file.attribute"). However, it is
    not guaranteed that the operation will succeed. If the modification operation fails it falls back to
    [`File.setLastModified(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#setLastModified-long- "class or interface in java.io") and if that fails, the method throws IOException.

    Parameters:
    :   `sourceFile` - an existing file or directory to copy, must not be `null`.
    :   `destinationDir` - the directory to place the copy in, must not be `null`.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if any of the given [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")s are `null`.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the source or destination is invalid.
    :   `FileNotFoundException` - if the source does not exist.
    :   `IOException` - if an error occurs or setting the last-modified time didn't succeed.

    :   `destination` - the non-directory [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") to write bytes to (possibly overwriting), must not be
        `null`
    :   `connectionTimeoutMillis` - the number of milliseconds until this method will time out if no connection could
        be established to the `source`
    :   `readTimeoutMillis` - the number of milliseconds until this method will time out if no data could be read from
        the `source`

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if `source` URL cannot be opened
    :   `IOException` - if `destination` is a directory
    :   `IOException` - if `destination` cannot be written
    :   `IOException` - if `destination` needs creating but can't be
    :   `IOException` - if an IO error occurs during copying

    Since:
    :   2.0

  * ### directoryContains

    public static boolean [directoryContains](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-1341)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") directory,
    [File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") child)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Tests whether the `parent` directory contains the `child` element (a file or directory).

    Files are normalized before comparison.

    Edge cases:
    * A `directory` must not be null: if null, throw NullPointerException
    * A `directory` must be a directory: if not a directory, throw IllegalArgumentException
    * A directory does not contain itself: return false
    * A null child file is not contained in any parent: return false

    Parameters:
    :   `directory` - the file to consider as the parent.
    :   `child` - the file to consider as the child.

    Returns:
    :   true is the candidate leaf is under by the specified composite. False otherwise.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if an IO error occurs while checking the files.
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the parent is `null`.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the parent is not a directory.

    Since:
    :   2.2

    See Also:
    :   * [`FilenameUtils.directoryContains(String, String)`](FilenameUtils.html#directoryContains(java.lang.String,java.lang.String))

    public static boolean [isFileNewer](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-1639)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") file,

    Tests if the specified [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") is newer than the specified [`ChronoLocalDate`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/time/chrono/ChronoLocalDate.html "class or interface in java.time.chrono")
    at the end of day.

    Note: The input date is assumed to be in the system default time-zone with the time
    part set to the current time. To use a non-default time-zone use the method
    [`isFileNewer(file, chronoLocalDate.atTime(LocalTime.now(zoneId)), zoneId)`](#isFileNewer(java.io.File,java.time.chrono.ChronoLocalDateTime,java.time.ZoneId)) where

    Parameters:
    :   `file` - the [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") of which the modification date must be compared.
    :   `chronoLocalDate` - the date reference.

    Returns:

        [`ChronoLocalDate`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/time/chrono/ChronoLocalDate.html "class or interface in java.time.chrono") at the current time.

    Throws:
    :   `UncheckedIOException` - if an I/O error occurs
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the file or local date is `null`.

    Since:
    :   2.8.0

        [`ChronoLocalDate`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/time/chrono/ChronoLocalDate.html "class or interface in java.time.chrono") at the current time.

    [JDK-8177809](https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8177809) where [`File.lastModified()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#lastModified-- "class or interface in java.io") is
    losing milliseconds (always ends in 000). This bug exists in OpenJDK 8 and 9, and is fixed in 10.

    Parameters:

    Returns:
    :   See [`FileTime.toMillis()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/attribute/FileTime.html#toMillis-- "class or interface in java.nio.file.attribute").

  * ### lineIterator

    public static [LineIterator](LineIterator.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") [lineIterator](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-2286)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") file,
    [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") charsetName)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Returns an Iterator for the lines in a [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io").

    This method opens an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") for the file.
    When you have finished with the iterator you should close the stream
    to free internal resources. This can be done by using a try-with-resources block or calling the
    [`LineIterator.close()`](LineIterator.html#close()) method.

    The recommended usage pattern is:

    ```
    LineIterator it = FileUtils.lineIterator(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8.name());
    try {
      while (it.hasNext()) {
        String line = it.nextLine();
        // do something with line
      }
    } finally {
      LineIterator.closeQuietly(iterator);
    }
    ```

    If an exception occurs during the creation of the iterator, the
    underlying stream is closed.

    Parameters:
    :   `file` - the file to open for input, must not be `null`.
    :   `charsetName` - the name of the requested charset, `null` means platform default.

    Returns:
    :   a LineIterator for lines in the file, never `null`; MUST be closed by the caller.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if file is `null`.
    :   `FileNotFoundException` - if the file does not exist, is a directory rather than a regular file, or for some
        other reason cannot be opened for reading.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.

    Since:
    :   1.2
  * ### listFiles

    public static [Collection](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Collection.html "class or interface in java.util")<[File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")> [listFiles](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-2370)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") directory,
    [IOFileFilter](filefilter/IOFileFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter") fileFilter,
    [IOFileFilter](filefilter/IOFileFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter") dirFilter)

    Finds files within a given directory (and optionally its
    subdirectories). All files found are filtered by an IOFileFilter.

    If your search should recurse into subdirectories you can pass in
    an IOFileFilter for directories. You don't need to bind a
    DirectoryFileFilter (via logical AND) to this filter. This method does
    that for you.

    An example: If you want to search through all directories called
    "temp" you pass in `FileFilterUtils.NameFileFilter("temp")`.

    Another common usage of this method is find files in a directory
    tree but ignoring the directories generated CVS. You can simply pass
    in `FileFilterUtils.makeCVSAware(null)`.

    Parameters:
    :   `directory` - The directory to search.
    :   `fileFilter` - filter to apply when finding files. Must not be `null`,
        use [`TrueFileFilter.INSTANCE`](filefilter/TrueFileFilter.html#INSTANCE) to match all files in selected directories.
    :   `dirFilter` - optional filter to apply when finding subdirectories.
        If this parameter is `null`, subdirectories will not be included in the
        search. Use [`TrueFileFilter.INSTANCE`](filefilter/TrueFileFilter.html#INSTANCE) to match all directories.

    Returns:
    :   a collection of [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") with the matching files.

    See Also:
    :   * [`FileFilterUtils`](filefilter/FileFilterUtils.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
        * [`NameFileFilter`](filefilter/NameFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

    public static [Collection](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Collection.html "class or interface in java.util")<[File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")> [listFilesAndDirs](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-2438)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") directory,

    [IOFileFilter](filefilter/IOFileFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter") dirFilter)

    Finds files within a given directory (and optionally its
    subdirectories). All files found are filtered by an IOFileFilter.

    The resulting collection includes the starting directory and
    any subdirectories that match the directory filter.

    Parameters:
    :   `directory` - The directory to search.
    :   `fileFilter` - filter to apply when finding files.
    :   `dirFilter` - optional filter to apply when finding subdirectories.
        If this parameter is `null`, subdirectories will not be included in the
        search. Use TrueFileFilter.INSTANCE to match all directories.

    Returns:
    :   a collection of [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") with the matching files.

  * ### openInputStream

    public static [FileInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") [openInputStream](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-2675)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") file)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Opens a [`FileInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") for the specified file, providing better error messages than simply calling
    `new FileInputStream(file)`.

    At the end of the method either the stream will be successfully opened, or an exception will have been thrown.

    An exception is thrown if the file does not exist. An exception is thrown if the file object exists but is a
    directory. An exception is thrown if the file exists but cannot be read.

    Parameters:
    :   `file` - the file to open for input, must not be `null`.

    Returns:
    :   a new [`FileInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") for the specified file.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if file is `null`.
    :   `FileNotFoundException` - if the file does not exist, is a directory rather than a regular file, or for some
        other reason cannot be opened for reading.
    :   `IOException` - See FileNotFoundException above, FileNotFoundException is a subclass of IOException.

    Since:
    :   1.3
  * ### openOutputStream

    public static [FileOutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") [openOutputStream](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-2703)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") file)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Opens a [`FileOutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") for the specified file, checking and
    creating the parent directory if it does not exist.

    At the end of the method either the stream will be successfully opened,
    or an exception will have been thrown.

    The parent directory will be created if it does not exist.
    The file will be created if it does not exist.
    An exception is thrown if the file object exists but is a directory.
    An exception is thrown if the file exists but cannot be written to.
    An exception is thrown if the parent directory cannot be created.

    Parameters:
    :   `file` - the file to open for output, must not be `null`.

    Returns:
    :   a new [`FileOutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") for the specified file

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the file object is `null`.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the file object is a directory
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the file is not writable.
    :   `IOException` - if the directories could not be created.

    Since:
    :   1.3
  * ### openOutputStream

    public static [FileOutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") [openOutputStream](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-2731)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") file,
    boolean append)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Opens a [`FileOutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") for the specified file, checking and
    creating the parent directory if it does not exist.

    At the end of the method either the stream will be successfully opened,
    or an exception will have been thrown.

    The parent directory will be created if it does not exist.
    The file will be created if it does not exist.
    An exception is thrown if the file object exists but is a directory.
    An exception is thrown if the file exists but cannot be written to.
    An exception is thrown if the parent directory cannot be created.

    Parameters:
    :   `file` - the file to open for output, must not be `null`.
    :   `append` - if `true`, then bytes will be added to the
        end of the file rather than overwriting.

    Returns:
    :   a new [`FileOutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") for the specified file.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the file object is `null`.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the file object is a directory.
    :   `IOException` - if the directories could not be created, or the file is not writable.

    Since:
    :   2.1

    [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") is a regular file, then the file's length is returned.
    If the argument is a directory, then the size of the directory is
    calculated recursively. If a directory or subdirectory is security
    restricted, its size will not be included.

    Note that overflow is not detected, and the return value may be negative if
    overflow occurs. See [`sizeOfAsBigInteger(File)`](#sizeOfAsBigInteger(java.io.File)) for an alternative
    method that does not overflow.

    Parameters:
    :   `file` - the regular file or directory to return the size
        of (must not be `null`).

    Returns:
    :   the length of the file, or recursive size of the directory,
        provided (in bytes).

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the file is `null`.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the file does not exist.
    :   `UncheckedIOException` - if an IO error occurs.

    Since:
    :   2.0

  * ### streamFiles

    public static [Stream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/stream/Stream.html "class or interface in java.util.stream")<[File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")> [streamFiles](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-3045)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") directory,
    boolean recursive,
    [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang")... extensions)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Streams over the files in a given directory (and optionally its subdirectories) which match an array of extensions.

    The returned [`Stream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/stream/Stream.html "class or interface in java.util.stream") may wrap one or more [`DirectoryStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/DirectoryStream.html "class or interface in java.nio.file")s. When you require timely disposal of file system resources, use a
    `try`-with-resources block to ensure invocation of the stream's [`BaseStream.close()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/stream/BaseStream.html#close-- "class or interface in java.util.stream") method after the stream operations are completed. Calling a
    closed stream causes a [`IllegalStateException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/IllegalStateException.html "class or interface in java.lang").

    Parameters:
    :   `directory` - The directory to search.
    :   `recursive` - if true all subdirectories are searched as well.
    :   `extensions` - an array of extensions, for example, `{"java", "xml"}`. If this parameter is `null`, all files are returned.

    Returns:
    :   a Stream of [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") for matching files.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error is thrown when accessing the starting file.

    Since:
    :   2.9.0
  * ### toFile

    public static [File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") [toFile](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-3064)([URL](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/net/URL.html "class or interface in java.net") url)

    Converts from a [`URL`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/net/URL.html "class or interface in java.net") to a [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Syntax such as `file:///my%20docs/file.txt` will be correctly decoded to `/my docs/file.txt`. UTF-8 is used to decode percent-encoded octets
    to characters. Additionally, malformed percent-encoded octets are handled leniently by passing them through literally.

    Parameters:
    :   `url` - the file URL to convert, `null` returns `null`.

    Returns:
    :   the equivalent [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") object, or `null` if the URL's protocol is not `file`.
  * ### toFiles

    public static [File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")[] [toFiles](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileUtils.html#line-3088)([URL](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/net/URL.html "class or interface in java.net")... urls)

    Converts each of an array of [`URL`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/net/URL.html "class or interface in java.net") to a [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Returns an array of the same size as the input. If the input is `null`, an empty array is returned. If the input contains `null`, the output
    array contains `null` at the same index.

    This method will decode the URL. Syntax such as `file:///my%20docs/file.txt` will be correctly decoded to `/my docs/file.txt`.

    Parameters:
    :   `urls` - the file URLs to convert, `null` returns empty array.

    Returns:
    :   a non-`null` array of Files matching the input, with a `null` item if there was a `null` at that index in the input array.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if any file is not a URL file.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if any file is incorrectly encoded.

    Since:

    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Implements behavior similar to the Unix "touch" utility. Creates a new file with size 0, or, if the file exists, just

    of the file cannot be set. It creates parent directories if they do not exist.

    Throws:

    :   `IOException` - if setting the last-modified time failed or an I/O problem occurs.

# Class OrFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.OrFileFilter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, ConditionalFileFilter, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [OrFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/OrFileFilter.html#line-43)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [ConditionalFileFilter](ConditionalFileFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter"), [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

A [`FileFilter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileFilter.html "class or interface in java.io") providing conditional OR logic across a list of file filters. This filter returns
`true` if any filters in the list return `true`. Otherwise, it returns `false`. Checking of the
file filter list stops when the first filter returns `true`.

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.0

See Also:
:   * [`FileFilterUtils.or(IOFileFilter...)`](FileFilterUtils.html#or(org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.IOFileFilter...))
    * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.OrFileFilter)

# Class DirectoryFileComparator

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

All Implemented Interfaces:
