public static class [UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.html#line-83)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream](UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.Builder](UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream`](UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

Using a Byte Array:

```
UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream s = UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.builder()
  .setByteArray(byteArray)
  .setOffset(0)
  .setLength(byteArray.length)
  .get();
```

Using File IO:

```
UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream s = UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.builder()
  .setFile(file)
  .setOffset(0)
  .setLength(byteArray.length)
  .get();
```

Using NIO Path:

```
UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream s = UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setOffset(0)
  .setLength(byteArray.length)
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.7

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream`](UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    You must set an aspect that supports `byte[]` on this builder, otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * `byte[]`
    * offset
    * length

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot provide a `byte[]`.
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an `byte[]` using [`AbstractOrigin.getByteArray()`](../build/AbstractOrigin.html#getByteArray()).

    See Also:
    :   * [`AbstractOrigin.getByteArray()`](../build/AbstractOrigin.html#getByteArray())

# Class IOUtils

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils

---

public class [IOUtils](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-130)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

General IO stream manipulation utilities.

This class provides static utility methods for input/output operations.

* closeQuietly - these methods close a stream ignoring nulls and exceptions* toXxx/read - these methods read data from a stream* write - these methods write data to a stream* copy - these methods copy all the data from one stream to another* contentEquals - these methods compare the content of two streams

The byte-to-char methods and char-to-byte methods involve a conversion step.
Two methods are provided in each case, one that uses the platform default
encoding and the other which allows you to specify an encoding. You are
encouraged to always specify an encoding because relying on the platform
default can lead to unexpected results, for example when moving from
development to production.

All the methods in this class that read a stream are buffered internally.
This means that there is no cause to use a [`BufferedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")
or [`BufferedReader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedReader.html "class or interface in java.io"). The default buffer size of 4K has been shown
to be efficient in tests.

The various copy methods all delegate the actual copying to one of the following methods:

* [`copyLarge(InputStream, OutputStream, byte[])`](#copyLarge(java.io.InputStream,java.io.OutputStream,byte%5B%5D))
* [`copyLarge(InputStream, OutputStream, long, long, byte[])`](#copyLarge(java.io.InputStream,java.io.OutputStream,long,long,byte%5B%5D))
* [`copyLarge(Reader, Writer, char[])`](#copyLarge(java.io.Reader,java.io.Writer,char%5B%5D))
* [`copyLarge(Reader, Writer, long, long, char[])`](#copyLarge(java.io.Reader,java.io.Writer,long,long,char%5B%5D))

For example, [`copy(InputStream, OutputStream)`](#copy(java.io.InputStream,java.io.OutputStream)) calls [`copyLarge(InputStream, OutputStream)`](#copyLarge(java.io.InputStream,java.io.OutputStream))
which calls [`copy(InputStream, OutputStream, int)`](#copy(java.io.InputStream,java.io.OutputStream,int)) which creates the buffer and calls
[`copyLarge(InputStream, OutputStream, byte[])`](#copyLarge(java.io.InputStream,java.io.OutputStream,byte%5B%5D)).

Applications can re-use buffers by using the underlying methods directly.
This may improve performance for applications that need to do a lot of copying.

Wherever possible, the methods in this class do *not* flush or close
the stream. This is to avoid making non-portable assumptions about the
streams' origin and further use. Thus the caller is still responsible for
closing streams after use.

Provenance: Excalibur.

  * ### checkFromIndexSize

    public static void [checkFromIndexSize](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-570)(byte[] array,
    int off,
    int len)

    Validates that the sub-range `[off, off + len)` is within the bounds of the given array.

    The range is valid if all of the following hold:

    * `off >= 0`
    * `len >= 0`
    * `off + len <= array.length`

    If the range is invalid, throws [`IndexOutOfBoundsException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/IndexOutOfBoundsException.html "class or interface in java.lang") with a descriptive message.

    Typical usage in [`InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#read-byte:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io") and [`OutputStream.write(byte[], int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html#write-byte:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io") implementations:

    ```
    public int read(byte[] b, int off, int len) throws IOException {
        IOUtils.checkFromIndexSize(b, off, len);
        if (len == 0) {
            return 0;
        }
        ensureOpen();
        // perform read...
    }

    public void write(byte[] b, int off, int len) throws IOException {
        IOUtils.checkFromIndexSize(b, off, len);
        if (len == 0) {
            return;
        }
        ensureOpen();
        // perform write...
    }
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `array` - the array against which the range is validated
    :   `off` - the starting offset into the array (inclusive)
    :   `len` - the number of elements to access

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if `array` is `null`
    :   `IndexOutOfBoundsException` - if the range `[off, off + len)` is out of bounds for `array`

    Since:
    :   2.21.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#read-byte:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io")
        * [`OutputStream.write(byte[], int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html#write-byte:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io")
  * ### checkFromIndexSize

    public static void [checkFromIndexSize](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-617)(char[] array,
    int off,
    int len)

    Validates that the sub-range `[off, off + len)` is within the bounds of the given array.

    The range is valid if all of the following hold:

    * `off >= 0`
    * `len >= 0`
    * `off + len <= array.length`

    If the range is invalid, throws [`IndexOutOfBoundsException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/IndexOutOfBoundsException.html "class or interface in java.lang") with a descriptive message.

    Typical usage in [`Reader.read(char[], int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html#read-char:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io") and [`Writer.write(char[], int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html#write-char:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io") implementations:

    ```
    public int read(char[] cbuf, int off, int len) throws IOException {
        ensureOpen();
        IOUtils.checkFromIndexSize(cbuf, off, len);
        if (len == 0) {
            return 0;
        }
        // perform read...
    }

    public void write(char[] cbuf, int off, int len) throws IOException {
        ensureOpen();
        IOUtils.checkFromIndexSize(cbuf, off, len);
        if (len == 0) {
            return;
        }
        // perform write...
    }
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `array` - the array against which the range is validated
    :   `off` - the starting offset into the array (inclusive)
    :   `len` - the number of characters to access

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if `array` is `null`
    :   `IndexOutOfBoundsException` - if the range `[off, off + len)` is out of bounds for `array`

    Since:
    :   2.21.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`Reader.read(char[], int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html#read-char:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io")
        * [`Writer.write(char[], int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html#write-char:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io")

  * ### checkFromToIndex

    public static void [checkFromToIndex](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-694)([CharSequence](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html "class or interface in java.lang") seq,
    int fromIndex,
    int toIndex)

    Validates that the sub-sequence `[fromIndex, toIndex)` is within the bounds of the given [`CharSequence`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html "class or interface in java.lang").

    The sub-sequence is valid if all of the following hold:

    * `fromIndex >= 0`
    * `fromIndex <= toIndex`
    * `toIndex <= seq.length()`

    If `seq` is `null`, it is treated as the literal string `"null"` (length `4`).

    If the range is invalid, throws [`IndexOutOfBoundsException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/IndexOutOfBoundsException.html "class or interface in java.lang") with a descriptive message.

    Typical usage in [`Appendable.append(CharSequence, int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Appendable.html#append-java.lang.CharSequence-int-int- "class or interface in java.lang") implementations:

    ```
    public Appendable append(CharSequence csq, int start, int end) throws IOException {
        IOUtils.checkFromToIndex(csq, start, end);
        // perform append...
        return this;
    }
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `seq` - the character sequence to validate (may be `null`, treated as `"null"`)
    :   `fromIndex` - the starting index (inclusive)
    :   `toIndex` - the ending index (exclusive)

    Throws:
    :   `IndexOutOfBoundsException` - if the range `[fromIndex, toIndex)` is out of bounds for `seq`

    Since:
    :   2.21.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`Appendable.append(CharSequence, int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Appendable.html#append-java.lang.CharSequence-int-int- "class or interface in java.lang")

  * ### closeQuietly

    public static void [closeQuietly](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-826)([Closeable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html "class or interface in java.io") closeable)

    Closes a [`Closeable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html "class or interface in java.io") unconditionally.

    Equivalent to [`Closeable.close()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html#close-- "class or interface in java.io"), except any exceptions will be ignored. This is typically used in
    finally blocks.

    Example code:

    ```
    Closeable closeable = null;
    try {
        closeable = new FileReader("foo.txt");
        // process closeable
        closeable.close();
    } catch (Exception e) {
        // error handling
    } finally {
        IOUtils.closeQuietly(closeable);
    }
    ```

    Closing all streams:

    ```
    try {
        return IOUtils.copy(inputStream, outputStream);
    } finally {
        IOUtils.closeQuietly(inputStream);
        IOUtils.closeQuietly(outputStream);
    }
    ```

    Also consider using a try-with-resources statement where appropriate.

    Parameters:
    :   `closeable` - the objects to close, may be null or already closed.

    Since:
    :   2.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`Throwable.addSuppressed(Throwable)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html#addSuppressed-java.lang.Throwable- "class or interface in java.lang")
  * ### closeQuietly

    public static void [closeQuietly](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-876)([Closeable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html "class or interface in java.io")... closeables)

    Closes a [`Closeable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html "class or interface in java.io") unconditionally.

    Equivalent to [`Closeable.close()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html#close-- "class or interface in java.io"), except any exceptions will be ignored.

    This is typically used in finally blocks to ensure that the closeable is closed
    even if an Exception was thrown before the normal close statement was reached.
      
    **It should not be used to replace the close statement(s)
    which should be present for the non-exceptional case.**
      
    It is only intended to simplify tidying up where normal processing has already failed
    and reporting close failure as well is not necessary or useful.

    Example code:

    ```
    Closeable closeable = null;
    try {
        closeable = new FileReader("foo.txt");
        // processing using the closeable; may throw an Exception
        closeable.close(); // Normal close - exceptions not ignored
    } catch (Exception e) {
        // error handling
    } finally {
        IOUtils.closeQuietly(closeable); // In case normal close was skipped due to Exception
    }
    ```

    Closing all streams:
      

    ```
    try {
        return IOUtils.copy(inputStream, outputStream);
    } finally {
        IOUtils.closeQuietly(inputStream, outputStream);
    }
    ```

    Also consider using a try-with-resources statement where appropriate.

    Parameters:

    public static void [closeQuietly](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-889)([Closeable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html "class or interface in java.io") closeable,
    [Consumer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Consumer.html "class or interface in java.util.function")<[Exception](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Exception.html "class or interface in java.lang")> consumer)

    Closes the given [`Closeable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html "class or interface in java.io") as a null-safe operation while consuming IOException by the given `consumer`.

    Parameters:
    :   `closeable` - The resource to close, may be null.
    :   `consumer` - Consumes the Exception thrown by [`Closeable.close()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html#close-- "class or interface in java.io").

    Since:

  * ### closeQuietly

    public static void [closeQuietly](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-930)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input)

    Closes an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") unconditionally.

    Equivalent to [`InputStream.close()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#close-- "class or interface in java.io"), except any exceptions will be ignored.
    This is typically used in finally blocks.

    Example code:

    ```
      byte[] data = new byte[1024];
      InputStream in = null;
      try {
          in = new FileInputStream("foo.txt");
          in.read(data);
          in.close(); //close errors are handled
      } catch (Exception e) {
          // error handling
      } finally {
          IOUtils.closeQuietly(in);
      }
    ```

    Also consider using a try-with-resources statement where appropriate.

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - the InputStream to close, may be null or already closed.

    See Also:
    :   * [`Throwable.addSuppressed(Throwable)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html#addSuppressed-java.lang.Throwable- "class or interface in java.lang")

    Closes an iterable of [`Closeable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html "class or interface in java.io") unconditionally.

    Equivalent calling [`Closeable.close()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html#close-- "class or interface in java.io") on each element, except any exceptions will be ignored.

    Closes an [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") unconditionally.

    Equivalent to [`OutputStream.close()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html#close-- "class or interface in java.io"), except any exceptions will be ignored.
    This is typically used in finally blocks.

    Example code:

    ```
    byte[] data = "Hello, World".getBytes();

    OutputStream out = null;
    try {
        out = new FileOutputStream("foo.txt");
        out.write(data);
        out.close(); //close errors are handled
    } catch (IOException e) {
        // error handling
    } finally {
        IOUtils.closeQuietly(out);
    }
    ```

    Also consider using a try-with-resources statement where appropriate.

    Parameters:

    public static int [copy](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-1363)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") inputStream,
    [OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") outputStream)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Copies bytes from an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to an [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    This method buffers the input internally, so there is no need to use a [`BufferedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Large streams (over 2GB) will return a bytes copied value of `-1` after the copy has completed since
    the correct number of bytes cannot be returned as an int. For large streams use the
    [`copyLarge(InputStream, OutputStream)`](#copyLarge(java.io.InputStream,java.io.OutputStream)) method.

    Parameters:
    :   `inputStream` - the [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to read.
    :   `outputStream` - the [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to write.

    Returns:
    :   the number of bytes copied, or -1 if greater than [`Integer.MAX_VALUE`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Integer.html#MAX_VALUE "class or interface in java.lang").

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the InputStream is `null`.
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the OutputStream is `null`.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.

    Since:
    :   1.1

    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") using the specified character encoding.

    This method buffers the input internally, so there is no need to use a
    [`BufferedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Character encoding names can be found at
    [IANA](https://www.iana.org/assignments/character-sets).

    This method uses [`InputStreamReader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStreamReader.html "class or interface in java.io").

    :   `inputCharsetName` - the name of the requested charset for the InputStream, null means platform default.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the input or output is null.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.
    :   `UnsupportedCharsetException` - if the encoding is not supported.

  * ### copy

    public static [QueueInputStream](input/QueueInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") [copy](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-1483)([ByteArrayOutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/ByteArrayOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") outputStream)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Copies bytes from a [`ByteArrayOutputStream`](output/ByteArrayOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") to a [`QueueInputStream`](input/QueueInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    Unlike using JDK [`PipedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/PipedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") and [`PipedOutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/PipedOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") for this, this
    solution works safely in a single thread environment.

    Example usage:

    ```
    ByteArrayOutputStream outputStream = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
    outputStream.writeBytes("hello world".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));

    InputStream inputStream = IOUtils.copy(outputStream);
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `outputStream` - the [`ByteArrayOutputStream`](output/ByteArrayOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") to read.

    Returns:
    :   the [`QueueInputStream`](input/QueueInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") filled with the content of the outputStream.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the [`ByteArrayOutputStream`](output/ByteArrayOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") is `null`.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.

    Since:
    :   2.12

    Use [`copy(Reader, OutputStream, Charset)`](#copy(java.io.Reader,java.io.OutputStream,java.nio.charset.Charset)) instead

    Copies chars from a [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") to bytes on an [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using the the virtual machine's [default
    charset](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/Charset.html#defaultCharset-- "class or interface in java.nio.charset"), and calling flush.

    This method buffers the input internally, so there is no need to use a [`BufferedReader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedReader.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Due to the implementation of OutputStreamWriter, this method performs a flush.

    This method uses [`OutputStreamWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStreamWriter.html "class or interface in java.io").

    :   `NullPointerException` - if the input or output is null.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.

    public static long [copyLarge](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-1772)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input,
    [OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") output,
    long inputOffset,
    long length)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Copies some or all bytes from a large (over 2GB) [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to an
    [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), optionally skipping input bytes.

    This method buffers the input internally, so there is no need to use a
    [`BufferedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Note that the implementation uses [`skip(InputStream, long)`](#skip(java.io.InputStream,long)).
    This means that the method may be considerably less efficient than using the actual skip implementation,
    this is done to guarantee that the correct number of characters are skipped.

    The buffer size is given by [`DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE`](#DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE).

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - the [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to read.
    :   `output` - the [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to write.
    :   `inputOffset` - number of bytes to skip from input before copying, these bytes are ignored.
    :   `length` - number of bytes to copy.

    Returns:
    :   the number of bytes copied.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the input or output is null.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.

    Since:
    :   2.2

  * ### lineIterator

    public static [LineIterator](LineIterator.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") [lineIterator](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2038)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input,
    [Charset](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/Charset.html "class or interface in java.nio.charset") charset)

    Returns an Iterator for the lines in an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), using
    the character encoding specified (or default encoding if null).

    [`LineIterator`](LineIterator.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") holds a reference to the open
    [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") specified here. When you have finished with
    the iterator you should close the stream to free internal resources.
    This can be done by using a try-with-resources block, closing the stream directly, or by calling
    [`LineIterator.close()`](LineIterator.html#close()).

    The recommended usage pattern is:

    ```
    try {
      LineIterator it = IOUtils.lineIterator(stream, charset);
      while (it.hasNext()) {
        String line = it.nextLine();
        /// do something with line
      }
    } finally {
      IOUtils.closeQuietly(stream);
    }
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - the [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to read, not null.
    :   `charset` - the charset to use, null means platform default.

    Returns:
    :   an Iterator of the lines in the reader, never null.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the input is null.

    Since:
    :   2.3

    public static [LineIterator](LineIterator.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") [lineIterator](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2074)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input,

    Returns an Iterator for the lines in an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), using
    the character encoding specified (or default encoding if null).

    [`LineIterator`](LineIterator.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") holds a reference to the open
    [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") specified here. When you have finished with
    the iterator you should close the stream to free internal resources.
    This can be done by using a try-with-resources block, closing the stream directly, or by calling
    [`LineIterator.close()`](LineIterator.html#close()).

    The recommended usage pattern is:

    ```
    try {
      LineIterator it = IOUtils.lineIterator(stream, StandardCharsets.UTF_8.name());
      while (it.hasNext()) {
        String line = it.nextLine();
        /// do something with line
      }
    } finally {
      IOUtils.closeQuietly(stream);
    }
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - the [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to read, not null.
    :   `charsetName` - the encoding to use, null means platform default.

    Returns:
    :   an Iterator of the lines in the reader, never null.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the input is null.
    :   `UnsupportedCharsetException` - if the encoding is not supported.

    Since:
    :   1.2

    public static int [read](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2126)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input,
    byte[] buffer)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Reads bytes from an input stream.

    This implementation guarantees that it will read as many bytes
    as possible before giving up; this may not always be the case for
    subclasses of [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - where to read input from.
    :   `buffer` - destination.

    Returns:
    :   actual length read; may be less than requested if EOF was reached.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if `input` or `buffer` is null.
    :   `IOException` - if a read error occurs.

    Since:
    :   2.2

    byte[] buffer,
    int offset,
    int length)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Reads bytes from an input stream.

    This implementation guarantees that it will read as many bytes
    as possible before giving up; this may not always be the case for
    subclasses of [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - where to read input.
    :   `buffer` - destination.
    :   `offset` - initial offset into buffer.
    :   `length` - length to read, must be >= 0.

    Returns:
    :   actual length read; may be less than requested if EOF was reached.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if `input` or `buffer` is null.
    :   `IndexOutOfBoundsException` - if `offset` or `length` is negative, or if
        `offset + length` is greater than `buffer.length`.
    :   `IOException` - if a read error occurs.

    Reads the requested number of characters or fail if there are not enough left.

    not read as many characters as requested (most likely because of reaching EOF).

    Parameters:

    :   `buffer` - destination.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if `reader` or `buffer` is null.
    :   `EOFException` - if the number of characters read was incorrect.
    :   `IOException` - if there is a problem reading the file.

    public static void [readFully](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2363)([Reader](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") reader,
    char[] buffer,

    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Reads the requested number of characters or fail if there are not enough left.

    This allows for the possibility that [`Reader.read(char[], int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html#read-char:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io") may
    not read as many characters as requested (most likely because of reaching EOF).

    Parameters:
    :   `reader` - where to read input from.
    :   `buffer` - destination.
    :   `offset` - initial offset into buffer.
    :   `length` - length to read, must be >= 0.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if `reader` or `buffer` is null.
    :   `IndexOutOfBoundsException` - if `offset` or `length` is negative, or if
        `offset + length` is greater than `buffer.length`.
    :   `EOFException` - if the number of characters read was incorrect.
    :   `IOException` - if there is a problem reading the file.

    Since:
    :   2.2

  * ### skip

    public static long [skip](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2594)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input,
    long skip)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Skips bytes from an input byte stream.

    This implementation guarantees that it will read as many bytes as possible before giving up; this may not always be the case for skip() implementations
    in subclasses of [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Note that the implementation uses [`InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#read-byte:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io") rather than delegating to [`InputStream.skip(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#skip-long- "class or interface in java.io"). This means that
    the method may be considerably less efficient than using the actual skip implementation, this is done to guarantee that the correct number of bytes are
    skipped.

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - byte stream to skip.
    :   `skip` - number of bytes to skip.

    Returns:
    :   number of bytes actually skipped.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if there is a problem reading the file.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if toSkip is negative.

    Since:
    :   2.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`InputStream.skip(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#skip-long- "class or interface in java.io")
        * [IO-203 - Add skipFully() method for InputStreams](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/IO-203)
  * ### skip

    public static long [skip](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2626)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input,
    long skip,
    [Supplier](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Supplier.html "class or interface in java.util.function")<byte[]> skipBufferSupplier)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Skips bytes from an input byte stream.

    Intended for special cases when customization of the temporary buffer is needed because, for example, a nested input stream has requirements for the
    bytes read. For example, when using [`InflaterInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/zip/InflaterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.util.zip")s from multiple threads.

    This implementation guarantees that it will read as many bytes as possible before giving up; this may not always be the case for skip() implementations
    in subclasses of [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Note that the implementation uses [`InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#read-byte:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io") rather than delegating to [`InputStream.skip(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#skip-long- "class or interface in java.io"). This means that
    the method may be considerably less efficient than using the actual skip implementation, this is done to guarantee that the correct number of bytes are
    skipped.

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - byte stream to skip.
    :   `skip` - number of bytes to skip.
    :   `skipBufferSupplier` - Supplies the buffer to use for reading.

    Returns:
    :   number of bytes actually skipped.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if there is a problem reading the file.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if toSkip is negative.

    Since:
    :   2.14.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`InputStream.skip(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#skip-long- "class or interface in java.io")
        * [IO-203 - Add skipFully() method for InputStreams](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/IO-203)

    public static void [skipFully](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2768)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input,
    long toSkip,
    [Supplier](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Supplier.html "class or interface in java.util.function")<byte[]> skipBufferSupplier)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Skips the requested number of bytes or fail if there are not enough left.

    Intended for special cases when customization of the temporary buffer is needed because, for example, a nested input stream has requirements for the
    bytes read. For example, when using [`InflaterInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/zip/InflaterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.util.zip")s from multiple threads.

    This allows for the possibility that [`InputStream.skip(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#skip-long- "class or interface in java.io") may not skip as many bytes as requested (most likely because of reaching EOF).

    Note that the implementation uses [`skip(InputStream, long)`](#skip(java.io.InputStream,long)). This means that the method may be considerably less efficient than using the actual
    skip implementation, this is done to guarantee that the correct number of characters are skipped.

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - stream to skip.
    :   `toSkip` - the number of bytes to skip.
    :   `skipBufferSupplier` - Supplies the buffer to use for reading.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if there is a problem reading the file.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if toSkip is negative.
    :   `EOFException` - if the number of bytes skipped was incorrect.

    Since:
    :   2.14.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`InputStream.skip(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#skip-long- "class or interface in java.io")

    public static void [skipFully](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2818)([Reader](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") reader,
    long toSkip)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Skips the requested number of characters or fail if there are not enough left.

    This allows for the possibility that [`Reader.skip(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html#skip-long- "class or interface in java.io") may
    not skip as many characters as requested (most likely because of reaching EOF).

    Note that the implementation uses [`skip(Reader, long)`](#skip(java.io.Reader,long)).
    This means that the method may be considerably less efficient than using the actual skip implementation,
    this is done to guarantee that the correct number of characters are skipped.

    Parameters:
    :   `reader` - stream to skip.
    :   `toSkip` - the number of characters to skip.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if there is a problem reading the file.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if toSkip is negative.
    :   `EOFException` - if the number of characters skipped was incorrect.

    Since:
    :   2.0

    :   * [`Reader.skip(long)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html#skip-long- "class or interface in java.io")
  * ### toBufferedInputStream

    public static [InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") [toBufferedInputStream](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2845)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Fetches entire contents of an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") and represent same data as result InputStream.

    This method is useful where,

    * Source InputStream is slow.
    * It has network resources associated, so we cannot keep it open for long time.
    * It has network timeout associated.

    It can be used in favor of [`toByteArray(InputStream)`](#toByteArray(java.io.InputStream)), since it avoids unnecessary allocation and copy of byte[].  
    This method buffers the input internally, so there is no need to use a [`BufferedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - Stream to be fully buffered.

    Returns:
    :   A fully buffered stream.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.

    Since:
    :   2.0

  * ### toByteArray

    public static byte[] [toByteArray](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2916)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") inputStream)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Reads all the bytes from an input stream in a byte array.

    The memory used by this method is **proportional** to the number
    of bytes read, which is only limited by [`Integer.MAX_VALUE`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Integer.html#MAX_VALUE "class or interface in java.lang"). Only streams
    which fit into a single byte array with roughly 2 GiB limit can be processed
    with this method.

    Parameters:
    :   `inputStream` - The [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to read; must not be `null`.

    Returns:
    :   A new byte array.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - If an I/O error occurs while reading or if the maximum array size is exceeded.
    :   `NullPointerException` - If `inputStream` is `null`.
  * ### toByteArray

    public static byte[] [toByteArray](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2941)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input,
    int size)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Reads exactly `size` bytes from the given [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") into a new `byte[]`.

    This variant always allocates the whole requested array size,
    for a dynamic growing variant use [`toByteArray(InputStream, int, int)`](#toByteArray(java.io.InputStream,int,int)),
    which enforces stricter memory usage constraints.

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - the [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to read; must not be `null`.
    :   `size` - the exact number of bytes to read; must be `>= 0`.

    Returns:
    :   a new byte array of length `size`.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if `size` is negative.
    :   `EOFException` - if the stream ends before `size` bytes are read.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs while reading.
    :   `NullPointerException` - if `input` is `null`.

    Since:
    :   2.1
  * ### toByteArray

    public static byte[] [toByteArray](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOUtils.html#line-2967)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input,
    int size,
    int chunkSize)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Reads exactly `size` bytes from the given [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") into a new `byte[]`.

    The memory used by this method is **proportional** to the number
    of bytes read and limited by the specified `size`. This makes it suitable for
    processing large input streams, provided that **sufficient** heap space is
    available.

    This method processes the input stream in successive chunks of up to
    `chunkSize` bytes.

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - the [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to read; must not be `null`.
    :   `size` - the exact number of bytes to read; must be `>= 0`.
        The actual bytes read are validated to equal `size`.
    :   `chunkSize` - The chunk size for incremental reading; must be `> 0`.

    Returns:
    :   a new byte array of length `size`.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if `size` is negative or `chunkSize <= 0`.
    :   `EOFException` - if the stream ends before `size` bytes are read.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs while reading.
    :   `NullPointerException` - if `input` is `null`.

    Since:
    :   2.21.0
  * ### toByteArray

    long size)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Reads exactly `size` bytes from the given [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") into a new `byte[]`.

    This variant always allocates the whole requested array size,
    for a dynamic growing variant use [`toByteArray(InputStream, int, int)`](#toByteArray(java.io.InputStream,int,int)),
    which enforces stricter memory usage constraints.

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - the [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to read; must not be `null`.
    :   `size` - the exact number of bytes to read; must be `>= 0` and `<= Integer.MAX_VALUE`.

    Returns:
    :   a new byte array of length `size`.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if `size` is negative or does not fit into an int.
    :   `EOFException` - if the stream ends before `size` bytes are read.
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs while reading.
    :   `NullPointerException` - if `input` is `null`.

    Since:
    :   2.1

    See Also:
    :   * [`toByteArray(InputStream, int, int)`](#toByteArray(java.io.InputStream,int,int))

    using the specified character encoding.

    [IANA](https://www.iana.org/assignments/character-sets).

    This method buffers the input internally, so there is no need to use a
    [`BufferedReader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedReader.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Returns:

    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.
    :   `UnsupportedCharsetException` - if the encoding is not supported.

public static class [MessageDigestInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/MessageDigestInputStream.html#line-71)
extends [ObservableInputStream.AbstractBuilder](ObservableInputStream.AbstractBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")<[MessageDigestInputStream.Builder](MessageDigestInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds new [`MessageDigestInputStream`](MessageDigestInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

For example:

```
MessageDigestInputStream s = MessageDigestInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setMessageDigest("SHA-512")
  .get();
```

You must specify a message digest algorithm name or instance.

*The MD5 cryptographic algorithm is weak and should not be used.*

Since:
:   2.15.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

* ## Method Details

  * ### get

    public [MessageDigestInputStream](MessageDigestInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") [get](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/MessageDigestInputStream.Builder.html#line-106)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds new [`MessageDigestInputStream`](MessageDigestInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()), otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()) gets the target aspect.
    * [`MessageDigest`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/security/MessageDigest.html "class or interface in java.security")

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if messageDigest is null.
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()).

    See Also:
    :   * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream())
        * [`IOSupplier.getUnchecked()`](../function/IOSupplier.html#getUnchecked())

# Class StringBuilderWriter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, Flushable, Serializable, Appendable, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [StringBuilderWriter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/StringBuilderWriter.html#line-38)
extends [Writer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

[`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") implementation that outputs to a [`StringBuilder`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/StringBuilder.html "class or interface in java.lang").

**NOTE:** This implementation, as an alternative to [`StringWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/StringWriter.html "class or interface in java.io"), provides an *un-synchronized* implementation for better
performance for use in a single thread. For safe usage with multiple [`Thread`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Thread.html "class or interface in java.lang")s, a [`StringWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/StringWriter.html "class or interface in java.io") should be used.

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   2.0

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.io.output.StringBuilderWriter)

* ## Method Details

  * ### toBufferedInputStream

    public static [InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") [toBufferedInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/ByteArrayOutputStream.html#line-52)([InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") input)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Fetches entire contents of an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") and represent same data as result InputStream.

    This method is useful where,

    * Source InputStream is slow.
    * It has network resources associated, so we cannot keep it open for long time.
    * It has network timeout associated.

    It can be used in favor of [`toByteArray()`](#toByteArray()), since it avoids unnecessary allocation and copy of byte[].  
    This method buffers the input internally, so there is no need to use a [`BufferedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - Stream to be fully buffered.

    Returns:
    :   A fully buffered stream.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs.

    Since:
    :   2.0
  * ### toBufferedInputStream

public static class [Tailer.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/Tailer.html#line-166)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[Tailer](Tailer.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [Tailer.Builder](Tailer.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`Tailer`](Tailer.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

For example:

```
Tailer t = Tailer.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setCharset(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
  .setDelayDuration(Duration.ofSeconds(1))
  .setExecutorService(Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor(Builder::newDaemonThread))
  .setReOpen(false)
  .setStartThread(true)
  .setTailable(tailable)
  .setTailerListener(tailerListener)
  .setTailFromEnd(false)
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.12.0

:   * [`get()`](#get())

public class [NullInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/NullInputStream.html#line-65)
extends [AbstractInputStream](AbstractInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

A lightweight [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") that emulates a stream of a specified size.

This implementation provides a lightweight object for testing with an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") where the contents don't matter.

One use case would be for testing the handling of large [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") as it can emulate that scenario without the overhead of actually processing large
numbers of bytes - significantly speeding up test execution times.

This implementation returns zero from the method that reads a byte and leaves the array unchanged in the read methods that are passed a byte array. If
alternative data is required the `processByte()` and `processBytes()` methods can be implemented to generate data, for example:

```
 public class TestInputStream extends NullInputStream {

     public TestInputStream(int size) {
         super(size);
     }

     protected int processByte() {
         return ... // return required value here
     }

     protected void processBytes(byte[] bytes, int offset, int length) {
         for (int i = offset; i < length; i++) {
             bytes[i] = ... // set array value here
         }
     }
 }
```

This class is not thread-safe.

Since:
:   1.3

public class [TaggedReader](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/TaggedReader.html#line-68)
extends [ProxyReader](ProxyReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

A reader decorator that tags potential exceptions so that the reader that caused the exception can easily be
identified. This is done by using the [`TaggedIOException`](../TaggedIOException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") class to wrap all thrown [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")s. See
below for an example of using this class.

```
TaggedReader reader = new TaggedReader(...);
try {
    // Processing that may throw an IOException either from this reader
    // or from some other IO activity like temporary files, etc.
    processReader(reader);
} catch (IOException e) {
    if (reader.isCauseOf(e)) {
        // The exception was caused by this reader.
        // Use e.getCause() to get the original exception.
    } else {
        // The exception was caused by something else.
    }
}
```

Alternatively, the [`throwIfCauseOf(Throwable)`](#throwIfCauseOf(java.lang.Throwable)) method can be used to let higher levels of code handle the
exception caused by this reader while other processing errors are being taken care of at this lower level.

```
TaggedReader reader = new TaggedReader(...);
try {
    processReader(reader);
} catch (IOException e) {
    reader.throwIfCauseOf(e);
    // ... or process the exception that was caused by something else
}
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   2.7

:   * [`TaggedIOException`](../TaggedIOException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io")

    [`TaggedIOException`](../TaggedIOException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") wrapper created by this decorator, and then unwraps and throws the original wrapped
    exception. Returns normally if the exception was not thrown by this reader.

public interface [IOSupplier](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/function/IOSupplier.html#line-33)<T>

Like [`Supplier`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Supplier.html "class or interface in java.util.function") but throws [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io").

Using an IOSupplier allows you to compose usage of checked and unchecked exceptions as you best see fit.

Since:
:   2.7

# Class FilesUncheck

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.file.FilesUncheck

---

public final class [FilesUncheck](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/file/FilesUncheck.html#line-59)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Delegates to [`Files`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Files.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") to uncheck calls by throwing [`UncheckedIOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/UncheckedIOException.html "class or interface in java.io") instead of [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io").

Since:
:   2.12.0

public static class [XmlStreamReader.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/XmlStreamReader.html#line-119)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[XmlStreamReader](XmlStreamReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [XmlStreamReader.Builder](XmlStreamReader.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`XmlStreamReader`](XmlStreamReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").
Constructs a Reader using an InputStream and the associated content-type header. This constructor is lenient regarding the encoding detection.

First it checks if the stream has BOM. If there is not BOM checks the content-type encoding. If there is not content-type encoding checks the XML prolog
encoding. If there is not XML prolog encoding uses the default encoding mandated by the content-type MIME type.

If lenient detection is indicated and the detection above fails as per specifications it then attempts the following:

If the content type was 'text/html' it replaces it with 'text/xml' and tries the detection again.

Else if the XML prolog had a charset encoding that encoding is used.

Else if the content type had a charset encoding that encoding is used.

Else 'UTF-8' is used.

If lenient detection is indicated an XmlStreamReaderException is never thrown.

For example:

```
XmlStreamReader r = XmlStreamReader.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setCharset(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.12.0

* ## Method Details

  * ### get

    public [XmlStreamReader](XmlStreamReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") [get](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/XmlStreamReader.Builder.html#line-155)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`XmlStreamReader`](XmlStreamReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()), otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream())
    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getCharset()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getCharset())
    * lenient
    * httpContentType

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()).
    :   `XmlStreamReaderException` - thrown if the Charset encoding could not be determined according to the specification.

public static class [CharSequenceInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/CharSequenceInputStream.html#line-83)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[CharSequenceInputStream](CharSequenceInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [CharSequenceInputStream.Builder](CharSequenceInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`CharSequenceInputStream`](CharSequenceInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

For example:

## Using a Charset

```
CharSequenceInputStream s = CharSequenceInputStream.builder()
  .setBufferSize(8192)
  .setCharSequence("String")
  .setCharset(Charset.defaultCharset())
  .get();
```

## Using a CharsetEncoder

```
CharSequenceInputStream s = CharSequenceInputStream.builder()
  .setBufferSize(8192)
  .setCharSequence("String")
  .setCharsetEncoder(Charset.defaultCharset().newEncoder()
    .onMalformedInput(CodingErrorAction.REPLACE)
    .onUnmappableCharacter(CodingErrorAction.REPLACE))
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.13.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

# Class NameFileComparator

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.comparator.NameFileComparator

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Serializable, Comparator<File>`

---

public class [NameFileComparator](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/comparator/NameFileComparator.html#line-57)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Compare the **names** of two files for order (see [`File.getName()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#getName-- "class or interface in java.io")).

This comparator can be used to sort lists or arrays of files
by their name either in a case-sensitive, case-insensitive or
system dependent case-sensitive way. A number of singleton instances
are provided for the various case sensitivity options (using [`IOCase`](../IOCase.html "enum in org.apache.commons.io"))
and the reverse of those options.

Example of a *case-sensitive* file name sort using the
[`NAME_COMPARATOR`](#NAME_COMPARATOR) singleton instance:

```
      List<File> list = ...
      ((AbstractFileComparator) NameFileComparator.NAME_COMPARATOR).sort(list);
```

Example of a *reverse case-insensitive* file name sort using the
[`NAME_INSENSITIVE_REVERSE`](#NAME_INSENSITIVE_REVERSE) singleton instance:

```
      File[] array = ...
      ((AbstractFileComparator) NameFileComparator.NAME_INSENSITIVE_REVERSE).sort(array);
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.4

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.io.comparator.NameFileComparator)

# Class UnsynchronizedBufferedReader

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

public class [UnsynchronizedBufferedReader](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UnsynchronizedBufferedReader.html#line-50)
extends [UnsynchronizedReader](UnsynchronizedReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

Wraps an existing [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") and buffers the input *without any synchronization*. Expensive interaction with the underlying reader is minimized,
since most (smaller) requests can be satisfied by accessing the buffer alone. The drawback is that some extra space is required to hold the buffer and that
copying takes place when filling that buffer, but this is usually outweighed by the performance benefits.

A typical application pattern for the class looks like this:

```
UnsynchronizedBufferedReader buf = new UnsynchronizedBufferedReader(new FileReader("file"));
```

Provenance: Apache Harmony's java.io.BufferedReader, renamed, and modified.

Since:
:   2.17.0

See Also:

extends [IOExceptionWithCause](IOExceptionWithCause.html "class in org.apache.commons.io")

An [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io") decorator that adds a serializable tag to the
wrapped exception. Both the tag and the original exception can be used
to determine further processing when this exception is caught.

    public static boolean [isTaggedWith](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/TaggedIOException.html#line-65)([Throwable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang") throwable,
    [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") tag)

    Checks whether the given throwable is tagged with the given tag.

    This check can only succeed if the throwable is a
    [`TaggedIOException`](TaggedIOException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") and the tag is [`Serializable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io"), but
    the argument types are intentionally more generic to make it easier
    to use this method without type casts.

    A typical use for this method is in a `catch` block to
    determine how a caught exception should be handled:

    ```
    Serializable tag = ...;
    try {
        ...;
    } catch (Throwable t) {
        if (TaggedIOException.isTaggedWith(t, tag)) {
            // special processing for tagged exception
        } else {
            // handling of other kinds of exceptions
        }
    }
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `throwable` - The Throwable object to check
    :   `tag` - tag object

    Returns:
    :   `true` if the throwable has the specified tag,
        otherwise `false`

    public static void [throwCauseIfTaggedWith](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/TaggedIOException.html#line-93)([Throwable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang") throwable,
    [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") tag)

    Throws the original [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io") if the given throwable is
    a [`TaggedIOException`](TaggedIOException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") decorator the given tag. Does nothing
    if the given throwable is of a different type or if it is tagged
    with some other tag.

    This method is typically used in a `catch` block to
    selectively rethrow tagged exceptions.

    ```
    Serializable tag = ...;
    try {
        ...;
    } catch (Throwable t) {
        TaggedIOException.throwCauseIfTagged(t, tag);
        // handle other kinds of exceptions
    }
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `throwable` - an exception
    :   `tag` - tag object

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - original exception from the tagged decorator, if any
