# Class DirectoryWalker<T>

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.DirectoryWalker<T>

Type Parameters:
:   `T` - The result type, like [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io").

---

[@Deprecated](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Deprecated.html "class or interface in java.lang")
public abstract class [DirectoryWalker](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/DirectoryWalker.html#line-254)<T>
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Deprecated.

Apache Commons IO no longer uses this class. Instead, use
[`PathUtils.walk(java.nio.file.Path, org.apache.commons.io.file.PathFilter, int, boolean, java.nio.file.FileVisitOption...)`](file/PathUtils.html#walk(java.nio.file.Path,org.apache.commons.io.file.PathFilter,int,boolean,java.nio.file.FileVisitOption...))
or [`Files.walkFileTree(java.nio.file.Path, java.util.Set, int, java.nio.file.FileVisitor)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Files.html#walkFileTree-java.nio.file.Path-java.util.Set-int-java.nio.file.FileVisitor- "class or interface in java.nio.file"), and
friends.

Abstract class that walks through a directory hierarchy and provides subclasses with convenient hooks to add specific
behavior.

This class operates with a [`FileFilter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileFilter.html "class or interface in java.io") and maximum depth to limit the files and directories visited. Commons
IO supplies many common filter implementations in the  [filefilter](filefilter/package-summary.html)
package.

The following sections describe:

* [1. Example Implementation](#example) - example [`FileCleaner`](FileCleaner.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") implementation.
* [2. Filter Example](#filter) - using [`FileFilter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileFilter.html "class or interface in java.io")(s) with [`DirectoryWalker`](DirectoryWalker.html "class in org.apache.commons.io").
* [3. Cancellation](#cancel) - how to implement cancellation behavior.

## 1. Example Implementation

There are many possible extensions, for example, to delete all files and '.svn' directories, and return a list of
deleted files:

```
public class FileCleaner extends DirectoryWalker {

    public FileCleaner() {
        super();
    }

    public List clean(File startDirectory) {
        List results = new ArrayList();
        walk(startDirectory, results);
        return results;
    }

    protected boolean handleDirectory(File directory, int depth, Collection results) {
        // delete svn directories and then skip
        if (".svn".equals(directory.getName())) {
            directory.delete();
            return false;
        } else {
            return true;
        }

    }

    protected void handleFile(File file, int depth, Collection results) {
        // delete file and add to list of deleted
        file.delete();
        results.add(file);
    }
}
```

## 2. Filter Example

Choosing which directories and files to process can be a key aspect of using this class. This information can be
setup in three ways, via three different constructors.

The first option is to visit all directories and files. This is achieved via the no-args constructor.

The second constructor option is to supply a single [`FileFilter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileFilter.html "class or interface in java.io") that describes the files and directories to
visit. Care must be taken with this option as the same filter is used for both directories and files.

For example, if you wanted all directories which are not hidden and files which end in ".txt":

```
public class FooDirectoryWalker extends DirectoryWalker {
    public FooDirectoryWalker(FileFilter filter) {
        super(filter, -1);
    }
}

// Build up the filters and create the walker
// Create a filter for Non-hidden directories
IOFileFilter fooDirFilter = FileFilterUtils.andFileFilter(FileFilterUtils.directoryFileFilter,
    HiddenFileFilter.VISIBLE);

// Create a filter for Files ending in ".txt"
IOFileFilter fooFileFilter = FileFilterUtils.andFileFilter(FileFilterUtils.fileFileFilter,
    FileFilterUtils.suffixFileFilter(".txt"));

// Combine the directory and file filters using an OR condition
java.io.FileFilter fooFilter = FileFilterUtils.orFileFilter(fooDirFilter, fooFileFilter);

// Use the filter to construct a DirectoryWalker implementation
FooDirectoryWalker walker = new FooDirectoryWalker(fooFilter);
```

The third constructor option is to specify separate filters, one for directories and one for files. These are
combined internally to form the correct [`FileFilter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileFilter.html "class or interface in java.io"), something which is very easy to get wrong when
attempted manually, particularly when trying to express constructs like 'any file in directories named docs'.

For example, if you wanted all directories which are not hidden and files which end in ".txt":

```
 public class FooDirectoryWalker extends DirectoryWalker {
   public FooDirectoryWalker(IOFileFilter dirFilter, IOFileFilter fileFilter) {
     super(dirFilter, fileFilter, -1);
   }
 }

 // Use the filters to construct the walker
 FooDirectoryWalker walker = new FooDirectoryWalker(
   HiddenFileFilter.VISIBLE,
   FileFilterUtils.suffixFileFilter(".txt"),
 );
```

This is much simpler than the previous example, and is why it is the preferred option for filtering.

## 3. Cancellation

The DirectoryWalker contains some of the logic required for cancel processing. Subclasses must complete the
implementation.

What [`DirectoryWalker`](DirectoryWalker.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") does provide for cancellation is:

* [`DirectoryWalker.CancelException`](DirectoryWalker.CancelException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") which can be thrown in any of the *lifecycle* methods to stop processing.
* The `walk()` method traps thrown [`DirectoryWalker.CancelException`](DirectoryWalker.CancelException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") and calls the `handleCancelled()`
  method, providing a place for custom cancel processing.

Implementations need to provide:

* The decision logic on whether to cancel processing or not.
* Constructing and throwing a [`DirectoryWalker.CancelException`](DirectoryWalker.CancelException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io").
* Custom cancel processing in the `handleCancelled()` method.

Two possible scenarios are envisaged for cancellation:

* [3.1 External / Multi-threaded](#external) - cancellation being decided/initiated by an external
  process.
* [3.2 Internal](#internal) - cancellation being decided/initiated from within a DirectoryWalker
  implementation.

The following sections provide example implementations for these two different scenarios.

### 3.1 External / Multi-threaded

This example provides a public `cancel()` method that can be called by another thread to stop the
processing. A typical example use-case is a cancel button on a GUI. Calling this method sets a
[(@code volatile}](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se8/html/jls-8.html#d5e12277)
flag to ensure it works properly in a multi-threaded environment.
The flag is returned by the `handleIsCancelled()` method, which causes the walk to stop
immediately. The `handleCancelled()` method will be the next, and last, callback method received once cancellation has occurred.

```
public class FooDirectoryWalker extends DirectoryWalker {

    private volatile boolean cancelled = false;

    public void cancel() {
        cancelled = true;
    }

    protected boolean handleIsCancelled(File file, int depth, Collection results) {
        return cancelled;
    }

    protected void handleCancelled(File startDirectory, Collection results, CancelException cancel) {
        // implement processing required when a cancellation occurs
    }
}
```

### 3.2 Internal

This shows an example of how internal cancellation processing could be implemented. **Note** the decision logic
and throwing a [`DirectoryWalker.CancelException`](DirectoryWalker.CancelException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") could be implemented in any of the *lifecycle* methods.

```
public class BarDirectoryWalker extends DirectoryWalker {

    protected boolean handleDirectory(File directory, int depth, Collection results) throws IOException {
        // cancel if hidden directory
        if (directory.isHidden()) {
            throw new CancelException(file, depth);
        }
        return true;
    }

    protected void handleFile(File file, int depth, Collection results) throws IOException {
        // cancel if read-only file
        if (!file.canWrite()) {
            throw new CancelException(file, depth);
        }
        results.add(file);
    }

    protected void handleCancelled(File startDirectory, Collection results, CancelException cancel) {
        // implement processing required when a cancellation occurs
    }
}
```

:   1.3

    This method returns a boolean to indicate if the directory should be examined or not.
    If you return false, the entire directory and any subdirectories will be skipped.
    Note that this functionality is in addition to the filtering by file filter.

    This implementation does nothing and returns true.

    :   `results` - the collection of result objects, may be updated

  * ### handleIsCancelled

    protected boolean [handleIsCancelled](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/DirectoryWalker.html#line-565)([File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") file,
    int depth,
    [Collection](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Collection.html "class or interface in java.util")<[T](#type-param-T "type parameter in DirectoryWalker")> results)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Deprecated.

    Overridable callback method invoked to determine if the entire walk
    operation should be immediately cancelled.

    This method should be implemented by those subclasses that want to
    provide a public `cancel()` method available from another
    thread. The design pattern for the subclass should be as follows:

    ```
     public class FooDirectoryWalker extends DirectoryWalker {
       private volatile boolean cancelled = false;

       public void cancel() {
           cancelled = true;
       }
       private void handleIsCancelled(File file, int depth, Collection results) {
           return cancelled;
       }
       protected void handleCancelled(File startDirectory,
                 Collection results, CancelException cancel) {
           // implement processing required when a cancellation occurs
       }
     }
    ```

    If this method returns true, then the directory walk is immediately
    cancelled. The next callback method will be [`handleCancelled(File, Collection, DirectoryWalker.CancelException)`](#handleCancelled(java.io.File,java.util.Collection,org.apache.commons.io.DirectoryWalker.CancelException)).

    This implementation returns false.

    Parameters:
    :   `file` - the file or directory being processed
    :   `depth` - the current directory level (starting directory = 0)
    :   `results` - the collection of result objects, may be updated

    Returns:
    :   true if the walk has been cancelled

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O Error occurs

    Deprecated.

    Internal method that walks the directory hierarchy in a depth-first manner.

    Users of this class do not need to call this method. This method will
    be called automatically by another (public) method on the specific subclass.

    Writers of subclasses should call this method to start the directory walk.
    Once called, this method will emit events as it walks the hierarchy.
    The event methods have the prefix `handle`.

    Parameters:
    :   `startDirectory` - the directory to start from, not null
    :   `results` - the collection of result objects, may be updated

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the start directory is null
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O Error occurs

extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Charsets required of every implementation of the Java platform.
From the Java documentation [Standard charsets](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/Charset.html):

Every implementation of the Java platform is required to support the following character encodings. Consult
the release documentation for your implementation to see if any other encodings are supported. Consult the release
documentation for your implementation to see if any other encodings are supported.

* `US-ASCII`  
  Seven-bit ASCII, a.k.a. ISO646-US, a.k.a. the Basic Latin block of the Unicode character set.
* `ISO-8859-1`  
  ISO Latin Alphabet No. 1, a.k.a. ISO-LATIN-1.
* `UTF-8`  
  Eight-bit Unicode Transformation Format.
* `UTF-16BE`  
  Sixteen-bit Unicode Transformation Format, big-endian byte order.
* `UTF-16LE`  
  Sixteen-bit Unicode Transformation Format, little-endian byte order.
* `UTF-16`  
  Sixteen-bit Unicode Transformation Format, byte order specified by a mandatory initial byte-order mark (either order
  accepted on input, big-endian used on output.)

Since:
:   2.3

See Also:
:   * [Standard charsets](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/Charset.html)

# Class MemoryMappedFileInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

[org.apache.commons.io.input.AbstractInputStream](AbstractInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

org.apache.commons.io.input.MemoryMappedFileInputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, AutoCloseable`

---

public final class [MemoryMappedFileInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/MemoryMappedFileInputStream.html#line-73)
extends [AbstractInputStream](AbstractInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

An [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") that utilizes memory mapped files to improve performance. A sliding window of the file is
mapped to memory to avoid mapping the entire file to memory at one time. The size of the sliding buffer is
configurable.

For most operating systems, mapping a file into memory is more expensive than reading or writing a few tens of
kilobytes of data. From the standpoint of performance. it is generally only worth mapping relatively large files into
memory.

Note: Use of this class does not necessarily obviate the need to use a [`BufferedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"). Depending on the
use case, the use of buffering may still further improve performance. For example:

To build an instance, use [`MemoryMappedFileInputStream.Builder`](MemoryMappedFileInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

```
BufferedInputStream s = new BufferedInputStream(new GzipInputStream(
  MemoryMappedFileInputStream.builder()
    .setPath(path)
    .setBufferSize(256 * 1024)
    .get()));
```

should outperform:

```
new GzipInputStream(new MemoryMappedFileInputStream(path))
```

```
GzipInputStream s = new GzipInputStream(
  MemoryMappedFileInputStream.builder()
    .setPath(path)
    .setBufferSize(256 * 1024)
    .get());
```

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`MemoryMappedFileInputStream.Builder`](MemoryMappedFileInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

# Class UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

public class [UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.html#line-40)
extends [InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

This is an alternative to [`ByteArrayInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/ByteArrayInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") which removes the synchronization overhead for non-concurrent access; as such this class is
not thread-safe.

To build an instance, use [`UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.Builder`](UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

Since:
:   2.7

See Also:
:   * [`UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.Builder`](UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")
    * [`ByteArrayInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/ByteArrayInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

public class [CharacterFilterReader](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/CharacterFilterReader.html#line-27)
extends [AbstractCharacterFilterReader](AbstractCharacterFilterReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

A filter reader that filters out a given character represented as an `int` code point, handy to remove
known junk characters from CSV files for example. This class is the most efficient way to filter out a single
character, as opposed to using a [`CharacterSetFilterReader`](CharacterSetFilterReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"). You can also nest [`CharacterFilterReader`](CharacterFilterReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")s.

# Class HiddenFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.HiddenFileFilter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [HiddenFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/HiddenFileFilter.html#line-79)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

This filter accepts [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")s that are hidden.

Example, showing how to print out a list of the
current directory's *hidden* files:

## Using Classic IO

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(HiddenFileFilter.HIDDEN);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

Example, showing how to print out a list of the
current directory's *visible* (not hidden) files:

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(HiddenFileFilter.VISIBLE);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

## Using NIO

```
final Path dir = PathUtils.current();
final AccumulatorPathVisitor visitor = AccumulatorPathVisitor.withLongCounters(HiddenFileFilter.HIDDEN);
//
// Walk one directory
Files.walkFileTree(dir, Collections.emptySet(), 1, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
//
visitor.getPathCounters().reset();
//
// Walk directory tree
Files.walkFileTree(dir, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getDirList());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.3

# Class ValidatingObjectInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

[java.io.ObjectInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/ObjectInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

org.apache.commons.io.serialization.ValidatingObjectInputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, DataInput, ObjectInput, ObjectStreamConstants, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [ValidatingObjectInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/serialization/ValidatingObjectInputStream.html#line-82)
extends [ObjectInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/ObjectInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

An [`ObjectInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/ObjectInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") that's restricted to deserialize a limited set of classes.

Various accept/reject methods allow for specifying which classes can be deserialized.

## Reading safely

Here is the only way to safely read a HashMap of String keys and Integer values:

```
// Defining Object fixture
final HashMap<String, Integer> map1 = new HashMap<>();
map1.put("1", 1);
// Writing serialized fixture
final byte[] byteArray;
try (ByteArrayOutputStream baos = new ByteArrayOutputStream();
        final ObjectOutputStream oos = new ObjectOutputStream(baos)) {
    oos.writeObject(map1);
    oos.flush();
    byteArray = baos.toByteArray();
}
// Reading
try (ByteArrayInputStream bais = new ByteArrayInputStream(byteArray);
        ValidatingObjectInputStream vois = ValidatingObjectInputStream.builder()
            .accept(HashMap.class, Number.class, Integer.class)
            .setInputStream(bais)
            .get()) {
    // String.class is automatically accepted
    final HashMap<String, Integer> map2 = (HashMap<String, Integer>) vois.readObject();
    assertEquals(map1, map2);
}
// Reusing a configuration
final ObjectStreamClassPredicate predicate = new ObjectStreamClassPredicate()
    .accept(HashMap.class, Number.class, Integer.class);
try (ByteArrayInputStream bais = new ByteArrayInputStream(byteArray);
        ValidatingObjectInputStream vois = ValidatingObjectInputStream.builder()
            .setPredicate(predicate)
            .setInputStream(bais)
            .get()) {
    // String.class is automatically accepted
    final HashMap<String, Integer> map2 = (HashMap<String, Integer>) vois.readObject();
    assertEquals(map1, map2);
}
```

Design inspired by a [IBM DeveloperWorks Article](https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/library/se-lookahead/).

Since:
:   2.5

public static class [ChecksumInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ChecksumInputStream.html#line-99)
extends [ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder](ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")<[ChecksumInputStream](ChecksumInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [ChecksumInputStream.Builder](ChecksumInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`ChecksumInputStream`](ChecksumInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

There is no default [`Checksum`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/zip/Checksum.html "class or interface in java.util.zip"); you MUST provide one. This avoids any issue with a default [`Checksum`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/zip/Checksum.html "class or interface in java.util.zip") being proven deficient or insecure
in the future.

## Using NIO

```
ChecksumInputStream s = ChecksumInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(Paths.get("MyFile.xml"))
  .setChecksum(new CRC32())
  .setExpectedChecksumValue(12345)
  .get();
```

## Using IO

```
ChecksumInputStream s = ChecksumInputStream.builder()
  .setFile(new File("MyFile.xml"))
  .setChecksum(new CRC32())
  .setExpectedChecksumValue(12345)
  .get();
```

## Validating only part of an InputStream

The following validates the first 100 bytes of the given input.

```
ChecksumInputStream s = ChecksumInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(Paths.get("MyFile.xml"))
  .setChecksum(new CRC32())
  .setExpectedChecksumValue(12345)
  .setCountThreshold(100)
  .get();
```

To validate input *after* the beginning of a stream, build an instance with an InputStream starting where you want to validate.

```
InputStream inputStream = ...;
inputStream.read(...);
inputStream.skip(...);
ChecksumInputStream s = ChecksumInputStream.builder()
  .setInputStream(inputStream)
  .setChecksum(new CRC32())
  .setExpectedChecksumValue(12345)
  .setCountThreshold(100)
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.16.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

# Class ReaderInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

[org.apache.commons.io.input.AbstractInputStream](AbstractInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

org.apache.commons.io.input.ReaderInputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [ReaderInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ReaderInputStream.html#line-87)
extends [AbstractInputStream](AbstractInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

[`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") implementation that reads a character stream from a [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") and transforms it to a byte stream using a specified charset encoding.
The stream is transformed using a [`CharsetEncoder`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/CharsetEncoder.html "class or interface in java.nio.charset") object, guaranteeing that all charset encodings supported by the JRE are handled correctly. In
particular for charsets such as UTF-16, the implementation ensures that one and only one byte order marker is produced.

Since in general it is not possible to predict the number of characters to be read from the [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") to satisfy a read request on the
[`ReaderInputStream`](ReaderInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), all reads from the [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") are buffered. There is therefore no well defined correlation between the current position of the
[`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") and that of the [`ReaderInputStream`](ReaderInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"). This also implies that in general there is no need to wrap the underlying [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") in a
[`BufferedReader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedReader.html "class or interface in java.io").

[`ReaderInputStream`](ReaderInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") implements the inverse transformation of [`InputStreamReader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStreamReader.html "class or interface in java.io"); in the following example, reading from `in2`
would return the same byte sequence as reading from `in` (provided that the initial byte sequence is legal with respect to the charset encoding):

To build an instance, use [`ReaderInputStream.Builder`](ReaderInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

```
InputStream inputStream = ...
Charset cs = ...
InputStreamReader reader = new InputStreamReader(inputStream, cs);
ReaderInputStream in2 = ReaderInputStream.builder()
  .setReader(reader)
  .setCharset(cs)
  .get();
```

[`ReaderInputStream`](ReaderInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") implements the same transformation as [`OutputStreamWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStreamWriter.html "class or interface in java.io"), except that the control flow is reversed: both classes
transform a character stream into a byte stream, but [`OutputStreamWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStreamWriter.html "class or interface in java.io") pushes data to the underlying stream, while [`ReaderInputStream`](ReaderInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")
pulls it from the underlying stream.

Note that while there are use cases where there is no alternative to using this class, very often the need to use this class is an indication of a flaw in
the design of the code. This class is typically used in situations where an existing API only accepts an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), but where the most natural way
to produce the data is as a character stream, by providing a [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") instance. An example of a situation where this problem may appear is when
implementing the `javax.activation.DataSource` interface from the Java Activation Framework.

The [`available()`](#available()) method of this class always returns 0. The methods [`InputStream.mark(int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#mark-int- "class or interface in java.io") and [`InputStream.reset()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#reset-- "class or interface in java.io") are not supported.

Instances of [`ReaderInputStream`](ReaderInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") are not thread safe.

Since:
:   2.0

See Also:
:   * [`ReaderInputStream.Builder`](ReaderInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")
    * [`WriterOutputStream`](../output/WriterOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

# Class LastModifiedFileComparator

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.comparator.LastModifiedFileComparator

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Serializable, Comparator<File>`

---

public class [LastModifiedFileComparator](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/comparator/LastModifiedFileComparator.html#line-55)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Compare the **last modified date/time** of two files for order
(see [`FileUtils.lastModifiedUnchecked(File)`](../FileUtils.html#lastModifiedUnchecked(java.io.File))).

This comparator can be used to sort lists or arrays of files
by their last modified date/time.

Example of sorting a list of files using the
[`LASTMODIFIED_COMPARATOR`](#LASTMODIFIED_COMPARATOR) singleton instance:

```
      List<File> list = ...
      ((AbstractFileComparator) LastModifiedFileComparator.LASTMODIFIED_COMPARATOR).sort(list);
```

Example of doing a *reverse* sort of an array of files using the
[`LASTMODIFIED_REVERSE`](#LASTMODIFIED_REVERSE) singleton instance:

```
      File[] array = ...
      ((AbstractFileComparator) LastModifiedFileComparator.LASTMODIFIED_REVERSE).sort(array);
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.4

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.io.comparator.LastModifiedFileComparator)

public static class [UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.html#line-66)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream](UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output"), [UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.Builder](UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")>

Builds a new [`UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream`](UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

Using File IO:

```
UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream s = UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.builder()
  .setBufferSize(8192)
  .get();
```

Using NIO Path:

```
UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream s = UnsynchronizedByteArrayOutputStream.builder()
  .setBufferSize(8192)
  .get();
```

:   2.7

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

[@Deprecated](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Deprecated.html "class or interface in java.lang")
public class [WildcardFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/WildcardFilter.html#line-85)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Deprecated.

Use WildcardFileFilter. Deprecated as this class performs directory
filtering which it shouldn't do, but that can't be removed due to compatibility.

Filters files using the supplied wildcards.

This filter selects files, but not directories, based on one or more wildcards
and using case-sensitive comparison.

The wildcard matcher uses the characters '?' and '\*' to represent a
single or multiple wildcard characters.
This is the same as often found on DOS/Unix command lines.
The extension check is case-sensitive.
See [`FilenameUtils.wildcardMatch(String, String)`](../FilenameUtils.html#wildcardMatch(java.lang.String,java.lang.String)) for more information.

For example:

## Using Classic IO

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
FileFilter fileFilter = new WildcardFilter("*test*.java~*~");
File[] files = dir.listFiles(fileFilter);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

## Using NIO

```
final Path dir = PathUtils.current();
final AccumulatorPathVisitor visitor = AccumulatorPathVisitor.withLongCounters(new WildcardFilter("*test*.java~*~"));
//
// Walk one directory
Files.walkFileTree(dir, Collections.emptySet(), 1, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
//
visitor.getPathCounters().reset();
//
// Walk directory tree
Files.walkFileTree(dir, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getDirList());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

# Class CharSequenceInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

All Implemented Interfaces:

public class [CharSequenceInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/CharSequenceInputStream.html#line-51)
extends [InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

Implements an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to read bytes from String, StringBuffer, StringBuilder or CharBuffer,
encoded using the specified Charset. The Charset defaults to Charset.defaultCharset().

**Note:** Supports [`mark(int)`](#mark(int)) and [`reset()`](#reset()).

To build an instance, use [`CharSequenceInputStream.Builder`](CharSequenceInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

Since:
:   2.2

See Also:
:   * [`CharSequenceInputStream.Builder`](CharSequenceInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

Builds a new [`WriterOutputStream`](WriterOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

For example:

```
WriterOutputStream s = WriterOutputStream.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setBufferSize(8192)
  .setCharset(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
  .setWriteImmediately(false)
  .get();
```

    public [WriterOutputStream.Builder](WriterOutputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") [setWriteImmediately](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/WriterOutputStream.Builder.html#line-179)(boolean writeImmediately)

    Sets whether the output buffer will be flushed after each write operation (`true`), meaning all available data will be written to the
    underlying [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") immediately. If `false`, the output buffer will only be flushed when it overflows or when [`WriterOutputStream.flush()`](WriterOutputStream.html#flush()) or
    [`WriterOutputStream.close()`](WriterOutputStream.html#close()) is called.

    Parameters:
    :   `writeImmediately` - If `true` the output buffer will be flushed after each write operation, meaning all available data will be written to
        the underlying [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") immediately. If `false`, the output buffer will only be flushed when it overflows or when
        [`WriterOutputStream.flush()`](WriterOutputStream.html#flush()) or [`WriterOutputStream.close()`](WriterOutputStream.html#close()) is called.

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.

# Class Tailer

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.input.Tailer

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `AutoCloseable, Runnable`

---

public class [Tailer](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/Tailer.html#line-140)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Runnable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Runnable.html "class or interface in java.lang"), [AutoCloseable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/AutoCloseable.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Simple implementation of the Unix "tail -f" functionality.

To build an instance, use [`Tailer.Builder`](Tailer.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

## 1. Create a TailerListener implementation

First you need to create a [`TailerListener`](TailerListener.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.input") implementation; ([`TailerListenerAdapter`](TailerListenerAdapter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") is provided for
convenience so that you don't have to implement every method).

For example:

```
public class MyTailerListener extends TailerListenerAdapter {
    public void handle(String line) {
        System.out.println(line);
    }
}
```

## 2. Using a Tailer

You can create and use a Tailer in one of three ways:

* Using a [`Tailer.Builder`](Tailer.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")
* Using an [`Executor`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/concurrent/Executor.html "class or interface in java.util.concurrent")
* Using a [`Thread`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Thread.html "class or interface in java.lang")

An example of each is shown below.

### 2.1 Using a Builder

```
TailerListener listener = new MyTailerListener();
Tailer tailer = Tailer.builder()
  .setFile(file)
  .setTailerListener(listener)
  .setDelayDuration(delay)
  .get();
```

### 2.2 Using an Executor

```
TailerListener listener = new MyTailerListener();
Tailer tailer = new Tailer(file, listener, delay);

// stupid executor impl. for demo purposes
Executor executor = new Executor() {
    public void execute(Runnable command) {
        command.run();
    }
};

executor.execute(tailer);
```

### 2.3 Using a Thread

```
TailerListener listener = new MyTailerListener();
Tailer tailer = new Tailer(file, listener, delay);
Thread thread = new Thread(tailer);
thread.setDaemon(true); // optional
thread.start();
```

## 3. Stopping a Tailer

Remember to stop the tailer when you have done with it:

```
tailer.stop();
```

## 4. Interrupting a Tailer

You can interrupt the thread a tailer is running on by calling [`Thread.interrupt()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Thread.html#interrupt-- "class or interface in java.lang").

```
thread.interrupt();
```

If you interrupt a tailer, the tailer listener is called with the [`InterruptedException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/InterruptedException.html "class or interface in java.lang").

The file is read using the default Charset; this can be overridden if necessary.

Since:
:   2.0, 2.5 Updated behavior and documentation for [`Thread.interrupt()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Thread.html#interrupt-- "class or interface in java.lang")., 2.12.0 Add [`Tailer.Tailable`](Tailer.Tailable.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.input") and [`Tailer.RandomAccessResourceBridge`](Tailer.RandomAccessResourceBridge.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.input") interfaces to tail of files accessed using
    alternative libraries such as jCIFS or [Apache Commons
    VFS](https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-vfs/).

See Also:
:   * [`Tailer.Builder`](Tailer.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")
    * [`TailerListener`](TailerListener.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.input")
    * [`TailerListenerAdapter`](TailerListenerAdapter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

public static final class [RandomAccessFileOutputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/RandomAccessFileOutputStream.html#line-55)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[RandomAccessFileOutputStream](RandomAccessFileOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output"), [RandomAccessFileOutputStream.Builder](RandomAccessFileOutputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")>

Builds a new [`RandomAccessFileOutputStream`](RandomAccessFileOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

For example:

```
RandomAccessFileOutputStream s = RandomAccessFileOutputStream.builder()
  .setFile("myfile.txt")
  .setOpenOptions(StandardOpenOption.SYNC)
  .get();
```

The only super's aspect used is buffer size.

Since:
:   2.18.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

* ## Method Details

  * ### get

    public [RandomAccessFileOutputStream](RandomAccessFileOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") [get](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/RandomAccessFileOutputStream.Builder.html#line-87)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`RandomAccessFileOutputStream`](RandomAccessFileOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`RandomAccessFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html "class or interface in java.io") or [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io"), otherwise, this method throws an exception. Only set one of
    RandomAccessFile or an origin that can be converted to a File.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`RandomAccessFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html "class or interface in java.io") is the target aspect.
    * [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")
    * closeOnClose

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if both RandomAccessFile and origin are set.
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to a [`RandomAccessFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html "class or interface in java.io").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`RandomAccessFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getRandomAccessFile()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getRandomAccessFile()).

    See Also:
    :   * [`AbstractOrigin.getFile()`](../build/AbstractOrigin.html#getFile())
        * [`IOSupplier.getUnchecked()`](../function/IOSupplier.html#getUnchecked())

    * #### Serialized Fields

      * ##### charSequence

        ```
        CharSequence charSequence
        ```

        Source for reading.
      * ##### end

        ```
        Integer end
        ```

        The end index in the character sequence, exclusive.

        When de-serializing a CharSequenceReader that was serialized before
        this fields was added, this field will be initialized to `null`,
        which gives the same behavior as before: stop reading at the
        CharSequence's length.
        If this field was an int instead, it would be initialized to 0 when the
        CharSequenceReader is de-serialized, causing it to not return any
        characters at all.

        Since:
        :   2.7

        See Also:
        :   * `CharSequenceReader.end()`
      * ##### idx

        ```
        int idx
        ```

        Reading index.
      * ##### mark

        ```
        int mark
        ```

        Reader mark.
      * ##### start

        ```
        int start
        ```

        The start index in the character sequence, inclusive.

        When de-serializing a CharSequenceReader that was serialized before
        this fields was added, this field will be initialized to 0, which
        gives the same behavior as before: start reading from the start.

        Since:
        :   2.7

        See Also:
        :   * `CharSequenceReader.start()`

# Class FileTimes

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.file.attribute.FileTimes

---

public final class [FileTimes](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/file/attribute/FileTimes.html#line-41)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Helps use [`FileTime`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/attribute/FileTime.html "class or interface in java.nio.file.attribute") and interoperate Date and NTFS times.

An NTFS file time is a 64-bit value that represents the number of 100-nanosecond intervals that have elapsed since 12:00 A.M. January 1, 1601 Coordinated
Universal Time (UTC). This is the offset of Windows time 0 to Unix epoch in 100-nanosecond intervals.

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [NTFS File Times](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sysinfo/file-times)

# Class LineIterator

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.LineIterator

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, AutoCloseable, Iterator<String>`

---

public class [LineIterator](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/LineIterator.html#line-51)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Iterator](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Iterator.html "class or interface in java.util")<[String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang")>, [Closeable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Closeable.html "class or interface in java.io")

An Iterator over the lines in a [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io").

[`LineIterator`](LineIterator.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") holds a reference to an open [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io").
When you have finished with the iterator you should close the reader
to free internal resources. This can be done by closing the reader directly,
or by calling the [`close()`](#close()) or [`closeQuietly(LineIterator)`](#closeQuietly(org.apache.commons.io.LineIterator))
method on the iterator.

The recommended usage pattern is:

```
LineIterator it = FileUtils.lineIterator(file, StandardCharsets.UTF_8.name());
try {
  while (it.hasNext()) {
    String line = it.nextLine();
    // do something with line
  }
} finally {
  it.close();
}
```

Since:
:   1.2

  * ### close

    public void [close](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/LineIterator.html#line-102)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Closes the underlying [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io").
    This method is useful if you only want to process the first few
    lines of a larger file. If you do not close the iterator
    then the [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") remains open.
    This method can safely be called multiple times.

    Specified by:
    :   `close` in interface `AutoCloseable`

    Specified by:
    :   `close` in interface `Closeable`

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if closing the underlying [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io") fails.

public class [ClosedInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ClosedInputStream.html#line-35)
extends [InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

Always returns [`IOUtils.EOF`](../IOUtils.html#EOF) to all attempts to read something from an input stream.

Typically uses of this class include testing for corner cases in methods that accept input streams and acting as a
sentinel value instead of a `null` input stream.

Since:
:   1.4

    :   `read` in class `InputStream`

    Parameters:

    :   `off` - The start offset.
    :   `len` - The number of bytes to read.

public class [CircularInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/CircularInputStream.html#line-35)
extends [AbstractInputStream](AbstractInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

An [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") that repeats provided bytes for given target byte count.

Closing this input stream has no effect. The methods in this class can be called after the stream has been closed
without generating an [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io").

Since:
:   2.8.0

See Also:
:   * [`InfiniteCircularInputStream`](InfiniteCircularInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

* ## Method Details

  * ### parseByteOrder

    public static [ByteOrder](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/ByteOrder.html "class or interface in java.nio") [parseByteOrder](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/ByteOrderParser.html#line-49)([String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") value)

    Parses the String argument as a [`ByteOrder`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/ByteOrder.html "class or interface in java.nio").

    Returns `ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN` if the given value is `"LITTLE_ENDIAN"`.

    Returns `ByteOrder.BIG_ENDIAN` if the given value is `"BIG_ENDIAN"`.

    Examples:
    * `ByteOrderParser.parseByteOrder("LITTLE_ENDIAN")` returns `ByteOrder.LITTLE_ENDIAN`
    * `ByteOrderParser.parseByteOrder("BIG_ENDIAN")` returns `ByteOrder.BIG_ENDIAN`

    Parameters:
    :   `value` - the [`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") containing the ByteOrder representation to be parsed

    Returns:
    :   the ByteOrder represented by the string argument

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the [`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") containing the ByteOrder representation to be parsed is unknown.

public class [FileWriterWithEncoding](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/FileWriterWithEncoding.html#line-53)
extends [ProxyWriter](ProxyWriter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

Writer of files that allows the encoding to be set.

This class provides a simple alternative to [`FileWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileWriter.html "class or interface in java.io") that allows an encoding to be set. Unfortunately, it cannot subclass [`FileWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileWriter.html "class or interface in java.io").

By default, the file will be overwritten, but this may be changed to append.

The encoding must be specified using either the name of the [`Charset`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/Charset.html "class or interface in java.nio.charset"), the [`Charset`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/Charset.html "class or interface in java.nio.charset"), or a [`CharsetEncoder`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/charset/CharsetEncoder.html "class or interface in java.nio.charset"). If the default encoding is
required then use the [`FileWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileWriter.html "class or interface in java.io") directly, rather than this implementation.

To build an instance, use [`FileWriterWithEncoding.Builder`](FileWriterWithEncoding.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

Since:
:   1.4

See Also:
:   * [`FileWriterWithEncoding.Builder`](FileWriterWithEncoding.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

# Class CircularByteBuffer

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.input.buffer.CircularByteBuffer

---

public class [CircularByteBuffer](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/buffer/CircularByteBuffer.html#line-32)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

A buffer, which doesn't need reallocation of byte arrays, because it
reuses a single byte array. This works particularly well, if reading
from the buffer takes place at the same time than writing to. Such is the
case, for example, when using the buffer within a filtering input stream,
like the [`CircularBufferInputStream`](CircularBufferInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input.buffer").

Since:
:   2.7

* ## Method Details

  * ### add

    public void [add](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/buffer/CircularByteBuffer.html#line-66)(byte value)

    Adds a new byte to the buffer, which will eventually be returned by following
    invocations of [`read()`](#read()).

    Parameters:
    :   `value` - The byte, which is being added to the buffer.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - The buffer is full. Use [`hasSpace()`](#hasSpace()),
        or [`getSpace()`](#getSpace()), to prevent this exception.
  * ### add

    public void [add](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/buffer/CircularByteBuffer.html#line-90)(byte[] targetBuffer,
    int offset,
    int length)

    Adds the given bytes to the buffer. This is the same as invoking [`add(byte)`](#add(byte))
    for the bytes at offsets `offset+0`, `offset+1`, ...,
    `offset+length-1` of byte array `targetBuffer`.

    Parameters:
    :   `targetBuffer` - the buffer to copy
    :   `offset` - start offset
    :   `length` - length to copy

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - The buffer doesn't have sufficient space. Use
        [`getSpace()`](#getSpace()) to prevent this exception.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - Either of `offset`, or `length` is negative.
    :   `NullPointerException` - The byte array `targetBuffer` is null.

  * ### peek

    public boolean [peek](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/buffer/CircularByteBuffer.html#line-185)(byte[] sourceBuffer,
    int offset,
    int length)

    Returns, whether the next bytes in the buffer are exactly those, given by
    `sourceBuffer`, `offset`, and `length`. No bytes are being
    removed from the buffer. If the result is true, then the following invocations
    of [`read()`](#read()) are guaranteed to return exactly those bytes.

    Parameters:
    :   `sourceBuffer` - the buffer to compare against
    :   `offset` - start offset
    :   `length` - length to compare

    Returns:
    :   True, if the next invocations of [`read()`](#read()) will return the
        bytes at offsets `sourceBuffer`+0, `offset`+1, ...,
        `offset`+`length`-1 of byte array `sourceBuffer`.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - Either of `sourceBuffer`, or `length` is negative.
    :   `NullPointerException` - The byte array `sourceBuffer` is null.
  * ### read

    public byte [read](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/buffer/CircularByteBuffer.html#line-216)()

    Returns the next byte from the buffer, removing it at the same time, so
    that following invocations won't return it again.

    Returns:
    :   The byte, which is being returned.

    public void [read](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/buffer/CircularByteBuffer.html#line-242)(byte[] targetBuffer,
    int targetOffset,
    int length)

    Returns the given number of bytes from the buffer by storing them in
    the given byte array at the given offset.

    Parameters:
    :   `targetBuffer` - The byte array, where to add bytes.
    :   `targetOffset` - The offset, where to store bytes in the byte array.
    :   `length` - The number of bytes to return.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - The byte array `targetBuffer` is null.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - Either of `targetOffset`, or `length` is negative,
        or the length of the byte array `targetBuffer` is too small.
    :   `IllegalStateException` - The buffer doesn't hold the given number
        of bytes. Use [`getCurrentNumberOfBytes()`](#getCurrentNumberOfBytes()) to prevent this
        exception.

public final class [ThrottledInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ThrottledInputStream.html#line-42)
extends [CountingInputStream](CountingInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

Provides bandwidth throttling on an InputStream as a filter input stream. The throttling examines the number of bytes read from the underlying InputStream,
and sleeps for a time interval if the byte-transfer is found to exceed the specified maximum rate. Thus, while the read-rate might exceed the maximum for a
short interval, the average tends towards the specified maximum, overall.

To build an instance, call [`builder()`](#builder()).

Inspired by Apache HBase's class of the same name.

Since:
:   2.16.0

See Also:
:   * [`ThrottledInputStream.Builder`](ThrottledInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

  * ### beforeRead

    protected void [beforeRead](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ThrottledInputStream.html#line-230)(int n)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Description copied from class: `ProxyInputStream`

    Invoked by the `read` methods before the call is proxied. The number
    of bytes that the caller wanted to read (1 for the [`ProxyInputStream.read()`](ProxyInputStream.html#read())
    method, buffer length for [`ProxyInputStream.read(byte[])`](ProxyInputStream.html#read(byte%5B%5D)), etc.) is given as
    an argument.

    Subclasses can override this method to add common pre-processing
    functionality without having to override all the read methods.
    The default implementation does nothing.

    Note this method is *not* called from [`ProxyInputStream.skip(long)`](ProxyInputStream.html#skip(long)) or
    [`ProxyInputStream.reset()`](ProxyInputStream.html#reset()). You need to explicitly override those methods if
    you want to add pre-processing steps also to them.

    Overrides:
    :   `beforeRead` in class `ProxyInputStream`

    Parameters:
    :   `n` - number of bytes that the caller asked to be read.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if the pre-processing fails in a subclass.

# Class FileAlterationObserver

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.monitor.FileAlterationObserver

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Serializable`

---

public class [FileAlterationObserver](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/monitor/FileAlterationObserver.html#line-128)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

FileAlterationObserver represents the state of files below a root directory, checking the file system and notifying listeners of create, change or delete
events.

To use this implementation:

* Create [`FileAlterationListener`](FileAlterationListener.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.monitor") implementation(s) that process the file/directory create, change and delete events
* Register the listener(s) with a [`FileAlterationObserver`](FileAlterationObserver.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.monitor") for the appropriate directory.
* Either register the observer(s) with a [`FileAlterationMonitor`](FileAlterationMonitor.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.monitor") or run manually.

## Basic Usage

Create a [`FileAlterationObserver`](FileAlterationObserver.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.monitor") for the directory and register the listeners:

```
     File directory = new File(FileUtils.current(), "src");
     FileAlterationObserver observer = new FileAlterationObserver(directory);
     observer.addListener(...);
     observer.addListener(...);
```

To manually observe a directory, initialize the observer and invoked the [`checkAndNotify()`](#checkAndNotify()) method as required:

```
     // initialize
     observer.init();
     ...
     // invoke as required
     observer.checkAndNotify();
     ...
     observer.checkAndNotify();
     ...
     // finished
     observer.finish();
```

Alternatively, register the observer(s) with a [`FileAlterationMonitor`](FileAlterationMonitor.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.monitor"), which creates a new thread, invoking the observer at the specified interval:

```
     long interval = ...
     FileAlterationMonitor monitor = new FileAlterationMonitor(interval);
     monitor.addObserver(observer);
     monitor.start();
     ...
     monitor.stop();
```

## File Filters

This implementation can monitor portions of the file system by using [`FileFilter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileFilter.html "class or interface in java.io")s to observe only the files and/or directories
that are of interest. This makes it more efficient and reduces the noise from *unwanted* file system events.

[Commons IO](https://commons.apache.org/io/) has a good range of useful, ready-made [File Filter](../filefilter/package-summary.html)
implementations for this purpose.

For example, to only observe 1) visible directories and 2) files with a ".java" suffix in a root directory called "src" you could set up a
[`FileAlterationObserver`](FileAlterationObserver.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.monitor") in the following way:

```
     // Create a FileFilter
     IOFileFilter directories = FileFilterUtils.and(
                                     FileFilterUtils.directoryFileFilter(),
                                     HiddenFileFilter.VISIBLE);
     IOFileFilter files       = FileFilterUtils.and(
                                     FileFilterUtils.fileFileFilter(),
                                     FileFilterUtils.suffixFileFilter(".java"));
     IOFileFilter filter = FileFilterUtils.or(directories, files);

     // Create the File system observer and register File Listeners
     FileAlterationObserver observer = new FileAlterationObserver(new File("src"), filter);
     observer.addListener(...);
     observer.addListener(...);
```

## FileEntry

[`FileEntry`](FileEntry.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.monitor") represents the state of a file or directory, capturing [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") attributes at a point in time. Custom implementations of
[`FileEntry`](FileEntry.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.monitor") can be used to capture additional properties that the basic implementation does not support. The [`FileEntry.refresh(File)`](FileEntry.html#refresh(java.io.File)) method is
used to determine if a file or directory has changed since the last check and stores the current state of the [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")'s properties.

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

# Class CloseShieldChannel

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.channels.CloseShieldChannel

public final class [CloseShieldChannel](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/channels/CloseShieldChannel.html#line-61)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Creates a close-shielding proxy for a [`Channel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/Channel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels").

The returned proxy implements all [`Channel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/Channel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels") sub-interfaces that are both supported by this implementation and actually implemented by the given
delegate.

The following interfaces are supported:

* [`AsynchronousChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/AsynchronousChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
* [`ByteChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/ByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
* [`Channel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/Channel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
* [`GatheringByteChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/GatheringByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
* [`InterruptibleChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/InterruptibleChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
* [`NetworkChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/NetworkChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
* [`ReadableByteChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/ReadableByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
* [`ScatteringByteChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/ScatteringByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
* [`SeekableByteChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/SeekableByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")
* [`WritableByteChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/WritableByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")

Since:
:   2.21.0

See Also:
:   * [`Channel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/Channel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")

# Class UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream

org.apache.commons.io.input.UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream

public final class [UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.html#line-56)
extends [UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream](UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

An unsynchronized version of [`BufferedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), not thread-safe.

Wraps an existing [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") and *buffers* the input. Expensive interaction with the underlying input stream is minimized, since most
(smaller) requests can be satisfied by accessing the buffer alone. The drawback is that some extra space is required to hold the buffer and that copying
takes place when filling that buffer, but this is usually outweighed by the performance benefits.

To build an instance, use [`UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.Builder`](UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

A typical application pattern for the class looks like this:

```
UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream s = new UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.Builder().
  .setInputStream(new FileInputStream("file.java"))
  .setBufferSize(8192)
  .get();
```

Provenance: Apache Harmony and modified.

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.Builder`](UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

    public void [mark](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.html#line-240)(int readLimit)

    Sets a mark position in this stream. The parameter `readLimit` indicates how many bytes can be read before a mark is invalidated. Calling
    `reset()` will reposition the stream back to the marked position if `readLimit` has not been surpassed. The underlying buffer may be
    increased in size to allow `readLimit` number of bytes to be supported.

    Overrides:
    :   `mark` in class `UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream`

    Parameters:

  * ### read

    public int [read](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.html#line-265)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Reads a single byte from this stream and returns it as an integer in the range from 0 to 255. Returns -1 if the end of the source string has been
    reached. If the internal buffer does not contain any available bytes then it is filled from the source stream and the first byte is returned.

    Overrides:
    :   `read` in class `UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream`

    Returns:
    :   the byte read or -1 if the end of the source stream has been reached.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if this stream is closed or another IOException occurs.
  * ### read

    public int [read](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.html#line-307)(byte[] dest,
    int offset,
    int length)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Reads at most `length` bytes from this stream and stores them in byte array `buffer` starting at offset `offset`. Returns the number of
    bytes actually read or -1 if no bytes were read and the end of the stream was encountered. If all the buffered bytes have been used, a mark has not been
    set and the requested number of bytes is larger than the receiver's buffer size, this implementation bypasses the buffer and simply places the results
    directly into `buffer`.

    Overrides:
    :   `read` in class `UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream`

    Parameters:
    :   `dest` - the byte array in which to store the bytes read.
    :   `offset` - the initial position in `buffer` to store the bytes read from this stream.
    :   `length` - the maximum number of bytes to store in `buffer`.

    Returns:
    :   the number of bytes actually read or -1 if end of stream.

    Throws:
    :   `IndexOutOfBoundsException` - if `offset < 0` or `length < 0`, or if `offset + length` is greater than the size of `buffer`.
    :   `IOException` - if the stream is already closed or another IOException occurs.

public class [AppendableOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/AppendableOutputStream.html#line-35)<T extends [Appendable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Appendable.html "class or interface in java.lang")>
extends [OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

OutputStream implementation that writes the data to an [`Appendable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Appendable.html "class or interface in java.lang")
Object.

For example, can be used with any [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") or a [`StringBuilder`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/StringBuilder.html "class or interface in java.lang")
or [`StringBuffer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/StringBuffer.html "class or interface in java.lang").

Since:
:   2.5

public class [ClosedOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/ClosedOutputStream.html#line-34)
extends [OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

Throws an IOException on all attempts to write to the stream.

Typically uses of this class include testing for corner cases in methods that accept an output stream and acting as a sentinel value instead of a
`null` output stream.

Since:
:   1.4

# Class ReadAheadInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

[java.io.FilterInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

org.apache.commons.io.input.ReadAheadInputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [ReadAheadInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ReadAheadInputStream.html#line-51)
extends [FilterInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

Implements [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to asynchronously read ahead from an underlying input stream when a specified amount of data has been read from the current
buffer. It does so by maintaining two buffers: an active buffer and a read ahead buffer. The active buffer contains data which should be returned when a
read() call is issued. The read ahead buffer is used to asynchronously read from the underlying input stream. When the current active buffer is exhausted, we
flip the two buffers so that we can start reading from the read ahead buffer without being blocked by disk I/O.

To build an instance, use [`ReadAheadInputStream.Builder`](ReadAheadInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

This class was ported and adapted from Apache Spark commit 933dc6cb7b3de1d8ccaf73d124d6eb95b947ed19.

Since:
:   2.9.0

# Class ThresholdingOutputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

org.apache.commons.io.output.ThresholdingOutputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, Flushable, AutoCloseable`

Direct Known Subclasses:
:   `DeferredFileOutputStream`

---

public class [ThresholdingOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/ThresholdingOutputStream.html#line-47)
extends [OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

An output stream which triggers an event on the first write that causes
the total number of bytes written to the stream to exceed a configured threshold,
and every subsequent write. The event
can be used, for example, to throw an exception if a maximum has been reached,
or to switch the underlying stream when the threshold is exceeded.

This class overrides all [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") methods. However, these overrides ultimately call the corresponding
methods in the underlying output stream implementation.

NOTE: This implementation may trigger the event *before* the threshold is actually reached, since it triggers
when a pending write operation would cause the threshold to be exceeded.

See also the subclass [`DeferredFileOutputStream`](DeferredFileOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output").

See Also:
:   * [`DeferredFileOutputStream`](DeferredFileOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

# Class TaggedWriter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.Writer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io")

[java.io.FilterWriter](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterWriter.html "class or interface in java.io")
