:   `Closeable, Flushable, Appendable, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [TaggedWriter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/TaggedWriter.html#line-65)
extends [ProxyWriter](ProxyWriter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

A writer decorator that tags potential exceptions so that the
reader that caused the exception can easily be identified. This is
done by using the [`TaggedIOException`](../TaggedIOException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") class to wrap all thrown
[`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")s. See below for an example of using this class.

```
TaggedReader reader = new TaggedReader(...);
try {
    // Processing that may throw an IOException either from this reader
    // or from some other IO activity like temporary files, etc.
    writeToWriter(writer);
} catch (IOException e) {
    if (writer.isCauseOf(e)) {
        // The exception was caused by this writer.
        // Use e.getCause() to get the original exception.
    } else {
        // The exception was caused by something else.
    }
}
```

Alternatively, the [`throwIfCauseOf(Exception)`](#throwIfCauseOf(java.lang.Exception)) method can be
used to let higher levels of code handle the exception caused by this
writer while other processing errors are being taken care of at this
lower level.

```
TaggedWriter writer = new TaggedWriter(...);
try {
    writeToWriter(writer);
} catch (IOException e) {
    writer.throwIfCauseOf(e);
    // ... or process the exception that was caused by something else
}
```

Since:
:   2.0

See Also:
:   * [`TaggedIOException`](../TaggedIOException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io")

public final class [BufferedFileChannelInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/BufferedFileChannelInputStream.html#line-44)
extends [InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

[`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") implementation which uses direct buffer to read a file to avoid extra copy of data between Java and native memory which happens when
using [`BufferedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"). Unfortunately, this is not something already available in JDK, `sun.nio.ch.ChannelInputStream` supports
reading a file using NIO, but does not support buffering.

To build an instance, use [`BufferedFileChannelInputStream.Builder`](BufferedFileChannelInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

This class was ported and adapted from Apache Spark commit 933dc6cb7b3de1d8ccaf73d124d6eb95b947ed19 where it was called `NioBufferedFileInputStream`.

Since:
:   2.9.0

:   * [`BufferedFileChannelInputStream.Builder`](BufferedFileChannelInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

# Class QueueOutputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

org.apache.commons.io.output.QueueOutputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, Flushable, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [QueueOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/QueueOutputStream.html#line-56)
extends [OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

Simple alternative to JDK [`PipedOutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/PipedOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"); queue input stream provides what's written in queue
output stream.

Example usage:

```
QueueOutputStream outputStream = new QueueOutputStream();
QueueInputStream inputStream = outputStream.newPipeInputStream();

outputStream.write("hello world".getBytes(UTF_8));
inputStream.read();
```

Unlike JDK [`PipedInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/PipedInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") and [`PipedOutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/PipedOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), queue input/output streams may be used safely in a
single thread or multiple threads. Also, unlike JDK classes, no special meaning is attached to initial or current
thread. Instances can be used longer after initial threads exited.

Closing a [`QueueOutputStream`](QueueOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output") has no effect. The methods in this class can be called after the stream has been
closed without generating an [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io").

Since:
:   2.9.0

See Also:
:   * [`QueueInputStream`](../input/QueueInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

# Class DirectoryFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.DirectoryFileFilter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [DirectoryFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/DirectoryFileFilter.html#line-68)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

This filter accepts [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")s that are directories.

For example, here is how to print out a list of the current directory's subdirectories:

## Using Classic IO

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(DirectoryFileFilter.INSTANCE);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

## Using NIO

```
final Path dir = PathUtils.current();
final AccumulatorPathVisitor visitor = AccumulatorPathVisitor.withLongCounters(DirectoryFileFilter.INSTANCE);
//
// Walk one directory
Files.walkFileTree(dir, Collections.emptySet(), 1, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
//
visitor.getPathCounters().reset();
//
// Walk directory tree
Files.walkFileTree(dir, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getDirList());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.0

See Also:
:   * [`FileFilterUtils.directoryFileFilter()`](FileFilterUtils.html#directoryFileFilter())

# Class BOMInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.InputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

[java.io.FilterInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

[org.apache.commons.io.input.ProxyInputStream](ProxyInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

org.apache.commons.io.input.BOMInputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [BOMInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/BOMInputStream.html#line-103)
extends [ProxyInputStream](ProxyInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

This class is used to wrap a stream that includes an encoded [`ByteOrderMark`](../ByteOrderMark.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") as its first bytes.

This class detects these bytes and, if required, can automatically skip them and return the subsequent byte as the
first byte in the stream.

The [`ByteOrderMark`](../ByteOrderMark.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") implementation has the following predefined BOMs:

* UTF-8 - [`ByteOrderMark.UTF_8`](../ByteOrderMark.html#UTF_8)
* UTF-16BE - [`ByteOrderMark.UTF_16LE`](../ByteOrderMark.html#UTF_16LE)
* UTF-16LE - [`ByteOrderMark.UTF_16BE`](../ByteOrderMark.html#UTF_16BE)
* UTF-32BE - [`ByteOrderMark.UTF_32LE`](../ByteOrderMark.html#UTF_32LE)
* UTF-32LE - [`ByteOrderMark.UTF_32BE`](../ByteOrderMark.html#UTF_32BE)

To build an instance, use [`BOMInputStream.Builder`](BOMInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

## Example 1 - Detecting and excluding a UTF-8 BOM

```
BOMInputStream bomIn = BOMInputStream.builder().setInputStream(in).get();
if (bomIn.hasBOM()) {
    // has a UTF-8 BOM
}
```

## Example 2 - Detecting a UTF-8 BOM without excluding it

```
boolean include = true;
BOMInputStream bomIn = BOMInputStream.builder()
    .setInputStream(in)
    .setInclude(include)
    .get();
if (bomIn.hasBOM()) {
    // has a UTF-8 BOM
}
```

## Example 3 - Detecting Multiple BOMs

```
BOMInputStream bomIn = BOMInputStream.builder()
  .setInputStream(in)
  .setByteOrderMarks(ByteOrderMark.UTF_16LE, ByteOrderMark.UTF_16BE, ByteOrderMark.UTF_32LE, ByteOrderMark.UTF_32BE)
  .get();
if (bomIn.hasBOM() == false) {
    // No BOM found
} else if (bomIn.hasBOM(ByteOrderMark.UTF_16LE)) {
    // has a UTF-16LE BOM
} else if (bomIn.hasBOM(ByteOrderMark.UTF_16BE)) {
    // has a UTF-16BE BOM
} else if (bomIn.hasBOM(ByteOrderMark.UTF_32LE)) {
    // has a UTF-32LE BOM
} else if (bomIn.hasBOM(ByteOrderMark.UTF_32BE)) {
    // has a UTF-32BE BOM
}
```

To build an instance, use [`BOMInputStream.Builder`](BOMInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

This class is not thread-safe.

Since:
:   2.0

See Also:
:   * [`BOMInputStream.Builder`](BOMInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")
    * [`ByteOrderMark`](../ByteOrderMark.html "class in org.apache.commons.io")
    * [Wikipedia - Byte Order Mark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byte_order_mark)

extends [Writer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io")

Throws an IOException on all attempts to write with [`close()`](#close()) implemented as a noop.

Typically uses of this class include testing for corner cases in methods that accept a writer and acting as a sentinel value instead of a `null`
writer.

# Class SuffixFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.SuffixFileFilter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [SuffixFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/SuffixFileFilter.html#line-74)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Filters files based on the suffix (what the file name ends with).
This is used in retrieving all the files of a particular type.

For example, to retrieve and print all `*.java` files
in the current directory:

## Using Classic IO

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(new SuffixFileFilter(".java"));
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

## Using NIO

```
final Path dir = PathUtils.current();
final AccumulatorPathVisitor visitor = AccumulatorPathVisitor.withLongCounters(new SuffixFileFilter(".java"));
//
// Walk one directory
Files.walkFileTree(dir, Collections.emptySet(), 1, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
//
visitor.getPathCounters().reset();
//
// Walk directory tree
Files.walkFileTree(dir, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getDirList());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.0

:   * [`FileFilterUtils.suffixFileFilter(String)`](FileFilterUtils.html#suffixFileFilter(java.lang.String))

public class [CloseShieldOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/CloseShieldOutputStream.html#line-31)
extends [ProxyOutputStream](ProxyOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

Proxy stream that prevents the underlying output stream from being closed.

This class is typically used in cases where an output stream needs to be passed to a component that wants to explicitly close the stream even if other
components would still use the stream for output.

# Class AbstractSupplier<T, B extends AbstractSupplier<T,B>>

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.build.AbstractSupplier<T,B>

Type Parameters:
:   `T` - the type of instances to build.
:   `B` - the type of builder subclass.

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `IOSupplier<T>`

Direct Known Subclasses:
:   `AbstractOrigin, AbstractOriginSupplier, SimplePathVisitor.AbstractBuilder, WildcardFileFilter.Builder`

---

public abstract class [AbstractSupplier](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/build/AbstractSupplier.html#line-126)<T, B extends AbstractSupplier<T,B>>
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [IOSupplier](../function/IOSupplier.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.function")<T>

Abstracts *supplying* an instance of type `T` where `T` is unbounded. This class carries no state.

Extend this class to implement the builder pattern.

For example, here is a builder, a domain class, and a test.

The builder:

```
   /**
    * Builds Foo instances.
    */
   public static class Builder extends AbstractSupplier<Foo, Builder> {

       private String bar1;
       private String bar2;
       private String bar3;

       /**
        * Builds a new Foo.
        */
       @Override
       public Foo get() {
           return new Foo(bar1, bar2, bar3);
       }

       public Builder setBar1(final String bar1) {
           this.bar1 = bar1;
           return this;
       }

       public Builder setBar2(final String bar2) {
           this.bar2 = bar2;
           return this;
       }

       public Builder setBar3(final String bar3) {
           this.bar3 = bar3;
           return this;
       }
   }
```

The domain class:

```
   /**
    * Domain class.
    */
   public class Foo {

       public static Builder builder() {
           return new Builder();
       }

       private final String bar1;
       private final String bar2;
       private final String bar3;

       private Foo(final String bar1, final String bar2, final String bar3) {
           this.bar1 = bar1;
           this.bar2 = bar2;
           this.bar3 = bar3;
       }

       public String getBar1() {
           return bar1;
       }

       public String getBar2() {
           return bar2;
       }

       public String getBar3() {
           return bar3;
       }

   }
```

The test:

```
   @Test
   public void test() {
       final Foo foo = Foo.builder()
           .setBar1("value1")
           .setBar2("value2")
           .setBar3("value3")
           .get();
       assertEquals("value1", foo.getBar1());
       assertEquals("value2", foo.getBar2());
       assertEquals("value3", foo.getBar3());
   }
```

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`IOSupplier`](../function/IOSupplier.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.function")

# Class CompositeFileComparator

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

public class [CompositeFileComparator](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/comparator/CompositeFileComparator.html#line-48)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Compare two files using a set of delegate file [`Comparator`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Comparator.html "class or interface in java.util").

This comparator can be used to sort lists or arrays of files by combining a number of other comparators.

Example of sorting a list of files by type (directory or file) and then by name:

```
      CompositeFileComparator comparator = new CompositeFileComparator(
          DirectoryFileComparator.DIRECTORY_COMPARATOR,
          NameFileComparator.NAME_COMPARATOR);
      List<File> list = ...
      comparator.sort(list);
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   2.0

# Class ByteArraySeekableByteChannel

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.channels.ByteArraySeekableByteChannel

public class [ByteArraySeekableByteChannel](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/channels/ByteArraySeekableByteChannel.html#line-44)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [SeekableByteChannel](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/SeekableByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels")

A [`SeekableByteChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/SeekableByteChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels") implementation backed by a byte array.

When used for writing, the internal buffer grows to accommodate incoming data. The natural size limit is the value of [`IOUtils.SOFT_MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH`](../IOUtils.html#SOFT_MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH)
and it's not possible to [`set the position`](#position(long)) or [`truncate`](#truncate(long)) to a value bigger than that. The raw internal buffer is
accessed via [`array()`](#array()).

Since:
:   2.21.0

* ## Method Details

  * ### wrap

    public static [ByteArraySeekableByteChannel](ByteArraySeekableByteChannel.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.channels") [wrap](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/channels/ByteArraySeekableByteChannel.html#line-64)(byte[] bytes)

    Constructs a new channel backed directly by the given byte array.

    The channel initially contains the full contents of the array, with its
    size set to `bytes.length` and its position set to `0`.

    Reads and writes operate on the shared array.
    If a write operation extends beyond the current capacity, the channel will
    automatically allocate a larger backing array and copy the existing contents.

    Parameters:
    :   `bytes` - The byte array to wrap, must not be `null`

    Returns:
    :   A new channel that uses the given array as its initial backing store

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - If `bytes` is `null`

    See Also:
    :   * [`array()`](#array())
        * [`ByteArrayInputStream(byte[])`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/ByteArrayInputStream.html#-init--byte:A- "class or interface in java.io")

public final class [UncheckedFilterWriter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/UncheckedFilterWriter.html#line-40)
extends [FilterWriter](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterWriter.html "class or interface in java.io")

A [`FilterWriter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterWriter.html "class or interface in java.io") that throws [`UncheckedIOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/UncheckedIOException.html "class or interface in java.io") instead of [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io").

public static class [BufferedFileChannelInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/BufferedFileChannelInputStream.html#line-73)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[BufferedFileChannelInputStream](BufferedFileChannelInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [BufferedFileChannelInputStream.Builder](BufferedFileChannelInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`BufferedFileChannelInputStream`](BufferedFileChannelInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

Using File IO:

```
BufferedFileChannelInputStream s = BufferedFileChannelInputStream.builder()
  .setFile(file)
  .setBufferSize(4096)
  .get();
```

Using NIO Path:

```
BufferedFileChannelInputStream s = BufferedFileChannelInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setBufferSize(4096)
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

* ## Method Details

  * ### get

    public [BufferedFileChannelInputStream](BufferedFileChannelInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") [get](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/BufferedFileChannelInputStream.Builder.html#line-106)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`BufferedFileChannelInputStream`](BufferedFileChannelInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()), otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`FileChannel`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/channels/FileChannel.html "class or interface in java.nio.channels") takes precedence is set.
    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getPath()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getPath()) if the file channel is not set.
    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getBufferSize()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getBufferSize())

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to a [`Path`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`Path`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getPath()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getPath()).

    See Also:
    :   * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getPath()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getPath())
        * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getBufferSize()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getBufferSize())
        * [`IOSupplier.getUnchecked()`](../function/IOSupplier.html#getUnchecked())
  * ### setFileChannel

    * [`RandomAccessFile(String, String)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html#-init--java.lang.String-java.lang.String- "class or interface in java.io")
    * [`Enum`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Enum.html "class or interface in java.lang")

* ## Enum Constant Summary

  Enum Constants

  Enum Constant

  Description

  `READ_ONLY`

  Defines mode "r" to open a [`RandomAccessFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html "class or interface in java.io") for reading only.

  `READ_WRITE`

  Defines mode "rw" to open a [`RandomAccessFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html "class or interface in java.io") for reading and writing.

  `READ_WRITE_SYNC_ALL`

  Defines mode "rws" to open a [`RandomAccessFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html "class or interface in java.io") for reading and writing, as with "rw", and also require that every update to the
  file's content or metadata be written synchronously to the underlying storage device.

  `READ_WRITE_SYNC_CONTENT`

  Defines mode "rwd" to open a [`RandomAccessFile`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/RandomAccessFile.html "class or interface in java.io") for reading and writing, as with "rw", and also require that every update to the
  file's content be written synchronously to the underlying storage device.

public class [AppendableWriter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/AppendableWriter.html#line-36)<T extends [Appendable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Appendable.html "class or interface in java.lang")>
extends [Writer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io")

Writer implementation that writes the data to an [`Appendable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Appendable.html "class or interface in java.lang") Object.

For example, can be used with a [`StringBuilder`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/StringBuilder.html "class or interface in java.lang") or [`StringBuffer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/StringBuffer.html "class or interface in java.lang").

Since:
:   2.7

public static class [UncheckedBufferedReader.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UncheckedBufferedReader.html#line-71)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[UncheckedBufferedReader](UncheckedBufferedReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [UncheckedBufferedReader.Builder](UncheckedBufferedReader.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`UncheckedBufferedReader`](UncheckedBufferedReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

Using File IO:

```
UncheckedBufferedReader s = UncheckedBufferedReader.builder()
  .setFile(file)
  .setBufferSize(8192)
  .setCharset(Charset.defaultCharset())
  .get();
```

Using NIO Path:

```
UncheckedBufferedReader s = UncheckedBufferedReader.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setBufferSize(8192)
  .setCharset(Charset.defaultCharset())
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

# Class FileCleaner

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.FileCleaner

---

[@Deprecated](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Deprecated.html "class or interface in java.lang")
public class [FileCleaner](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileCleaner.html#line-37)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Deprecated.

Use [`FileCleaningTracker`](FileCleaningTracker.html "class in org.apache.commons.io")

Keeps track of files awaiting deletion, and deletes them when an associated
marker object is reclaimed by the garbage collector.

This utility creates a background thread to handle file deletion.
Each file to be deleted is registered with a handler object.
When the handler object is garbage collected, the file is deleted.

In an environment with multiple class loaders (a servlet container, for
example), you should consider stopping the background thread if it is no
longer needed. This is done by invoking the method
[`exitWhenFinished()`](#exitWhenFinished()), typically in
`javax.servlet.ServletContextListener.contextDestroyed(javax.servlet.ServletContextEvent)` or similar.

* ## Method Details

  * ### exitWhenFinished

    [@Deprecated](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Deprecated.html "class or interface in java.lang")
    public static void [exitWhenFinished](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/FileCleaner.html#line-68)()

    Deprecated.

    Use [`FileCleaningTracker.exitWhenFinished()`](FileCleaningTracker.html#exitWhenFinished()).

    Call this method to cause the file cleaner thread to terminate when
    there are no more objects being tracked for deletion.

    In a simple environment, you don't need this method as the file cleaner
    thread will simply exit when the JVM exits. In a more complex environment,
    with multiple class loaders (such as an application server), you should be
    aware that the file cleaner thread will continue running even if the class
    loader it was started from terminates. This can constitute a memory leak.

    For example, suppose that you have developed a web application, which
    contains the commons-io jar file in your WEB-INF/lib directory. In other
    words, the FileCleaner class is loaded through the class loader of your
    web application. If the web application is terminated, but the servlet
    container is still running, then the file cleaner thread will still exist,
    posing a memory leak.

    This method allows the thread to be terminated. Simply call this method
    in the resource cleanup code, such as
    `javax.servlet.ServletContextListener.contextDestroyed(javax.servlet.ServletContextEvent)`.
    One called, no new objects can be tracked by the file cleaner.

# Class RegexFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.RegexFileFilter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [RegexFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/RegexFileFilter.html#line-75)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Filters files using supplied regular expression(s).

See java.util.regex.Pattern for regex matching rules.

## Using Classic IO

e.g.

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
FileFilter fileFilter = new RegexFileFilter("^.*[tT]est(-\\d+)?\\.java$");
File[] files = dir.listFiles(fileFilter);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

## Using NIO

```
final Path dir = PathUtils.current();
final AccumulatorPathVisitor visitor = AccumulatorPathVisitor.withLongCounters(new RegexFileFilter("^.*[tT]est(-\\d+)?\\.java$"));
//
// Walk one directory
Files.walkFileTree(dir, Collections.emptySet(), 1, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
//
visitor.getPathCounters().reset();
//
// Walk directory tree
Files.walkFileTree(dir, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getDirList());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.4

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.RegexFileFilter)

public static class [MemoryMappedFileInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/MemoryMappedFileInputStream.html#line-93)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[MemoryMappedFileInputStream](MemoryMappedFileInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [MemoryMappedFileInputStream.Builder](MemoryMappedFileInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`MemoryMappedFileInputStream`](MemoryMappedFileInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

For example:

```
MemoryMappedFileInputStream s = MemoryMappedFileInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setBufferSize(256 * 1024)
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.12.0

* ## Method Details

    public [MemoryMappedFileInputStream](MemoryMappedFileInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") [get](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/MemoryMappedFileInputStream.Builder.html#line-124)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`MemoryMappedFileInputStream`](MemoryMappedFileInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getPath()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getPath()), otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getPath()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getPath()) gets the target aspect.
    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getBufferSize()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getBufferSize())

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to a [`Path`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`Path`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getPath()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getPath()).

    See Also:
    :   * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getPath()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getPath())
        * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getBufferSize()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getBufferSize())
        * [`IOSupplier.getUnchecked()`](../function/IOSupplier.html#getUnchecked())

# Class TimestampedObserver

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.input.ObservableInputStream.Observer](ObservableInputStream.Observer.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

org.apache.commons.io.input.TimestampedObserver

---

public class [TimestampedObserver](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/TimestampedObserver.html#line-43)
extends [ObservableInputStream.Observer](ObservableInputStream.Observer.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

An observer with timestamps.

For example:

```
final TimestampedObserver timestampedObserver = new TimestampedObserver();
try (ObservableInputStream inputStream = new ObservableInputStream(...),
    timestampedObserver)) {
    ...
}
System.out.printf("IO duration: %s%n", timestampedObserver.getOpenToCloseDuration());
```

Since:
:   2.9.0

extends [Writer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io")

Never writes data. Calls never go beyond this class.

This [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") has no destination (file/socket etc.) and all characters written to it are ignored and lost.

public class [InfiniteCircularInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/InfiniteCircularInputStream.html#line-32)
extends [CircularInputStream](CircularInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

An [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") that infinitely repeats the provided bytes.

Closing this input stream has no effect. The methods in this class can be called after the stream has been closed
without generating an [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io").

Since:
:   2.6

public static class [MessageDigestCalculatingInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/MessageDigestCalculatingInputStream.html#line-67)
extends [ObservableInputStream.AbstractBuilder](ObservableInputStream.AbstractBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")<[MessageDigestCalculatingInputStream.Builder](MessageDigestCalculatingInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`MessageDigestCalculatingInputStream`](MessageDigestCalculatingInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

For example:

```
MessageDigestCalculatingInputStream s = MessageDigestCalculatingInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .setMessageDigest("SHA-512")
  .get();
```

*The MD5 cryptographic algorithm is weak and should not be used.*

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

    Builds a new [`MessageDigestCalculatingInputStream`](MessageDigestCalculatingInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()), otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()) gets the target aspect.

    Returns:

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if messageDigest is null.
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()).

    See Also:

public class [MarkShieldInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/MarkShieldInputStream.html#line-37)
extends [ProxyInputStream](ProxyInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

This is an alternative to [`ByteArrayInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/ByteArrayInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")
which removes the synchronization overhead for non-concurrent
access; as such this class is not thread-safe.
Proxy stream that prevents the underlying input stream from being marked/reset.

This class is typically used in cases where an input stream that supports
marking needs to be passed to a component that wants to explicitly mark
the stream, but it is not desirable to allow marking of the stream.

Since:
:   2.8.0

    Creates a composed predicate that represents a short-circuiting logical AND of this predicate and another. When
    evaluating the composed predicate, if this predicate is `false`, then the `other` predicate is not
    evaluated.

    Any exceptions thrown during evaluation of either predicate are relayed to the caller; if evaluation of this
    predicate throws an exception, the `other` predicate will not be evaluated.

    Parameters:
    :   `other` - a predicate that will be logically-ANDed with this predicate

    Returns:
    :   a composed predicate that represents the short-circuiting logical AND of this predicate and the `other`
        predicate

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if other is null

public class [XmlStreamReaderException](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/XmlStreamReaderException.html#line-34)
extends [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

The XmlStreamReaderException is thrown by the XmlStreamReader constructors if
the charset encoding cannot be determined according to the XML 1.0
specification and RFC 3023.

The exception returns the unconsumed InputStream to allow the application to
do an alternate processing with the stream. Note that the original
InputStream given to the XmlStreamReader cannot be used as that one has been
already read.

Since:
:   2.0

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.io.input.XmlStreamReaderException)

# Class CopyUtils

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.CopyUtils

---

[@Deprecated](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Deprecated.html "class or interface in java.lang")
public class [CopyUtils](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/CopyUtils.html#line-115)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Deprecated.

Use IOUtils. Will be removed in 3.0.
Methods renamed to IOUtils.write() or IOUtils.copy().
Null handling behavior changed in IOUtils (null data does not
throw NullPointerException).

This class provides static utility methods for buffered
copying between sources ([`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io"),
[`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") and `byte[]`) and destinations
([`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), [`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io"), [`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") and
`byte[]`).

Unless otherwise noted, these `copy` methods do *not*
flush or close the streams. Often doing so would require making non-portable
assumptions about the streams' origin and further use. This means that both
streams' `close()` methods must be called after copying. if one
omits this step, then the stream resources (sockets, file descriptors) are
released when the associated Stream is garbage-collected. It is not a good
idea to rely on this mechanism. For a good overview of the distinction
between "memory management" and "resource management", see
[this
UnixReview article](https://www.unixreview.com/articles/1998/9804/9804ja/ja.htm).

For byte-to-char methods, a `copy` variant allows the encoding
to be selected (otherwise the platform default is used). We would like to
encourage you to always specify the encoding because relying on the platform
default can lead to unexpected results.

We don't provide special variants for the `copy` methods that
let you specify the buffer size because in modern VMs the impact on speed
seems to be minimal. We're using a default buffer size of 4 KB.

The `copy` methods use an internal buffer when copying. It is
therefore advisable *not* to deliberately wrap the stream arguments
to the `copy` methods in `Buffered*` streams. For
example, don't do the following:

```
 copy( new BufferedInputStream( in ), new BufferedOutputStream( out ) );
```

The rationale is as follows:

Imagine that an InputStream's read() is a very expensive operation, which
would usually suggest wrapping in a BufferedInputStream. The
BufferedInputStream works by issuing infrequent
[`InputStream.read(byte[] b, int off, int len)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#read-byte:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io") requests on the
underlying InputStream, to fill an internal buffer, from which further
`read` requests can inexpensively get their data (until the buffer
runs out).

However, the `copy` methods do the same thing, keeping an
internal buffer, populated by
[`InputStream.read(byte[] b, int off, int len)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html#read-byte:A-int-int- "class or interface in java.io") requests. Having two
buffers (or three if the destination stream is also buffered) is pointless,
and the unnecessary buffer management hurts performance slightly (about 3%,
according to some simple experiments).

Behold, intrepid explorers; a map of this class:

```
      Method      Input               Output          Dependency
      ------      -----               ------          -------
1     copy        InputStream         OutputStream    (primitive)
2     copy        Reader              Writer          (primitive)

3     copy        InputStream         Writer          2

4     copy        Reader              OutputStream    2

5     copy        String              OutputStream    2
6     copy        String              Writer          (trivial)

7     copy        byte[]              Writer          3
8     copy        byte[]              OutputStream    (trivial)
```

Note that only the first two methods shuffle bytes; the rest use these
two, or (if possible) copy using native Java copy methods. As there are
method variants to specify the encoding, each row may
correspond to up to 2 methods.

Provenance: Excalibur.

public static class [UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.html#line-71)
extends [AbstractStreamBuilder](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream](UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.Builder](UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream`](UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

Using File IO:

```
UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream s = UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.builder()
  .setFile(file)
  .get();
```

Using NIO Path:

```
UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream s = UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(path)
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

* ## Method Details

  * ### get

    public [UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream](UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") [get](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.Builder.html#line-99)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream`](UnsynchronizedFilterInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()), otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream())

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()).

    See Also:
    :   * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream())
        * [`IOSupplier.getUnchecked()`](../function/IOSupplier.html#getUnchecked())

# Class CanWriteFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.CanWriteFileFilter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [CanWriteFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/CanWriteFileFilter.html#line-59)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

This filter accepts [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")s that can be written to.

Example, showing how to print out a list of the current directory's *writable* files:

## Using Classic IO

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(CanWriteFileFilter.CAN_WRITE);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

Example, showing how to print out a list of the current directory's *un-writable* files:

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
String[] files = dir.list(CanWriteFileFilter.CANNOT_WRITE);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

**N.B.** For read-only files, use `CanReadFileFilter.READ_ONLY`.

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.3

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.CanWriteFileFilter)

# Enum IOCase

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.lang.Enum](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Enum.html "class or interface in java.lang")<[IOCase](IOCase.html "enum in org.apache.commons.io")>

org.apache.commons.io.IOCase

All Implemented Interfaces:

public enum [IOCase](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOCase.html#line-41)
extends [Enum](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Enum.html "class or interface in java.lang")<[IOCase](IOCase.html "enum in org.apache.commons.io")>

Enumeration of IO case sensitivity.

Different filing systems have different rules for case-sensitivity.
Windows is case-insensitive, Unix is case-sensitive.

This class captures that difference, providing an enumeration to
control how file name comparisons should be performed. It also provides
methods that use the enumeration to perform comparisons.

Wherever possible, you should use the `check` methods in this
class to compare file names.

Since:
:   1.3

  * ### SYSTEM

    public static final [IOCase](IOCase.html "enum in org.apache.commons.io") [SYSTEM](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/IOCase.html#line-67)

    The constant for case sensitivity determined by the current operating system.
    Windows is case-insensitive when comparing file names, Unix is case-sensitive.

    **Note:** This only caters for Windows and Unix. Other operating
    systems (e.g. OSX and OpenVMS) are treated as case-sensitive if they use the
    Unix file separator and case-insensitive if they use the Windows file separator
    (see [`File.separatorChar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html#separatorChar "class or interface in java.io")).

    If you serialize this constant on Windows, and deserialize on Unix, or vice
    versa, then the value of the case-sensitivity flag will change.

# Interface IOQuadFunction<T,U,V,W,R>

Type Parameters:
:   `T` - the type of the first argument to the function
:   `U` - the type of the second argument to the function
:   `V` - the type of the third argument to the function
:   `W` - the type of the fourth argument to the function
:   `R` - the type of the result of the function

Functional Interface:
:   This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.

---

[@FunctionalInterface](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/FunctionalInterface.html "class or interface in java.lang")
public interface [IOQuadFunction](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/function/IOQuadFunction.html#line-40)<T,U,V,W,R>

Represents a function that accepts four arguments and produces a result. This is the four-arity specialization of
[`IOFunction`](IOFunction.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.function").

This is a [functional interface](package-summary.html) whose functional method is
[`apply(Object, Object, Object, Object)`](#apply(T,U,V,W)).

Since:

    Builds a new [`AutoCloseInputStream`](AutoCloseInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()).

# Class TaggedOutputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[java.io.OutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

[java.io.FilterOutputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterOutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

[org.apache.commons.io.output.ProxyOutputStream](ProxyOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

org.apache.commons.io.output.TaggedOutputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, Flushable, AutoCloseable`

---

public class [TaggedOutputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/output/TaggedOutputStream.html#line-65)
extends [ProxyOutputStream](ProxyOutputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.output")

An output stream decorator that tags potential exceptions so that the
stream that caused the exception can easily be identified. This is
done by using the [`TaggedIOException`](../TaggedIOException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io") class to wrap all thrown
[`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")s. See below for an example of using this class.

```
TaggedOutputStream stream = new TaggedOutputStream(...);
try {
    // Processing that may throw an IOException either from this stream
    // or from some other IO activity like temporary files, etc.
    writeToStream(stream);
} catch (IOException e) {
    if (stream.isCauseOf(e)) {
        // The exception was caused by this stream.
        // Use e.getCause() to get the original exception.
    } else {
        // The exception was caused by something else.
    }
}
```

Alternatively, the [`throwIfCauseOf(Exception)`](#throwIfCauseOf(java.lang.Exception)) method can be
used to let higher levels of code handle the exception caused by this
stream while other processing errors are being taken care of at this
lower level.

```
TaggedOutputStream stream = new TaggedOutputStream(...);
try {
    writeToStream(stream);
} catch (IOException e) {
    stream.throwIfCauseOf(e);
    // ... or process the exception that was caused by something else
}
```

Since:
:   2.0

See Also:
:   * [`TaggedIOException`](../TaggedIOException.html "class in org.apache.commons.io")

# Class WildcardFileFilter

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")

org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.WildcardFileFilter

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `FileFilter, FilenameFilter, Serializable, FileVisitor<Path>, PathMatcher, PathFilter, PathVisitor, IOFileFilter`

---

public class [WildcardFileFilter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/WildcardFileFilter.html#line-86)
extends [AbstractFileFilter](AbstractFileFilter.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Filters files using the supplied wildcards.

This filter selects files and directories based on one or more wildcards. Testing is case-sensitive by default, but this can be configured.

The wildcard matcher uses the characters '?' and '\*' to represent a single or multiple wildcard characters. This is the same as often found on DOS/Unix
command lines. The check is case-sensitive by default. See [`FilenameUtils.wildcardMatchOnSystem(String,String)`](../FilenameUtils.html#wildcardMatchOnSystem(java.lang.String,java.lang.String)) for more information.

To build an instance, use [`WildcardFileFilter.Builder`](WildcardFileFilter.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter").

For example:

## Using Classic IO

```
File dir = FileUtils.current();
FileFilter fileFilter = WildcardFileFilter.builder().setWildcards("*test*.java~*~").get();
File[] files = dir.listFiles(fileFilter);
for (String file : files) {
    System.out.println(file);
}
```

## Using NIO

```
final Path dir = PathUtils.current();
final AccumulatorPathVisitor visitor = AccumulatorPathVisitor.withLongCounters(
    WildcardFileFilter.builder().setWildcards("*test*.java~*~").get());
//
// Walk one directory
Files.walkFileTree(dir, Collections.emptySet(), 1, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
//
visitor.getPathCounters().reset();
//
// Walk directory tree
Files.walkFileTree(dir, visitor);
System.out.println(visitor.getPathCounters());
System.out.println(visitor.getDirList());
System.out.println(visitor.getFileList());
```

## Deprecating Serialization

*Serialization is deprecated and will be removed in 3.0.*

Since:
:   1.3

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.io.filefilter.WildcardFileFilter)

public static class [BoundedInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/BoundedInputStream.html#line-244)
extends [ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder](ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")<[BoundedInputStream](BoundedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [BoundedInputStream.Builder](BoundedInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`BoundedInputStream`](BoundedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

By default, a [`BoundedInputStream`](BoundedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") is *unbound*; so make sure to call `BoundedInputStream.AbstractBuilder.setMaxCount(long)`.

You can find out how many bytes this stream has seen so far by calling [`BoundedInputStream.getCount()`](BoundedInputStream.html#getCount()). This value reflects bytes read and skipped.

## Using a ServletInputStream

A `ServletInputStream` can block if you try to read content that isn't there
because it doesn't know whether the content hasn't arrived yet or whether the content has finished. Initialize an [`BoundedInputStream`](BoundedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") with the
`Content-Length` sent in the `ServletInputStream`'s header, this stop it from blocking, providing it's been sent with a correct content
length in the first place.

## Using NIO

```
BoundedInputStream s = BoundedInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(Paths.get("MyFile.xml"))
  .setMaxCount(1024)
  .setPropagateClose(false)
  .get();
```

## Using IO

```
BoundedInputStream s = BoundedInputStream.builder()
  .setFile(new File("MyFile.xml"))
  .setMaxCount(1024)
  .setPropagateClose(false)
  .get();
```

## Counting Bytes

You can set the running count when building, which is most useful when starting from another stream:

```
InputStream in = ...;
BoundedInputStream s = BoundedInputStream.builder()
  .setInputStream(in)
  .setCount(12)
  .setMaxCount(1024)
  .setPropagateClose(false)
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.16.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

* ## Method Details

  * ### get

    public [BoundedInputStream](BoundedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") [get](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/BoundedInputStream.Builder.html#line-280)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`BoundedInputStream`](BoundedInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()), otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    If you start from an input stream, an exception can't be thrown, and you can call [`IOSupplier.getUnchecked()`](../function/IOSupplier.html#getUnchecked()) instead.

    This builder uses the following aspects:

    * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()) gets the target aspect.
    * [`ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder.getAfterRead()`](ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder.html#getAfterRead())
    * `#getCount()`
    * `#getMaxCount()`
    * `#getOnMaxCount()`
    * `#isPropagateClose()`

    Returns:
    :   a new instance.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if the `origin` is `null`.
    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()).

    See Also:
    :   * [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream())
        * [`IOSupplier.getUnchecked()`](../function/IOSupplier.html#getUnchecked())
  * ### setCount

    public [BoundedInputStream.Builder](BoundedInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") setCount(long count)

    Sets the current number of bytes counted.

    Useful when building from another stream to carry forward a read count.

    Default is `0`, negative means 0.

    Parameters:

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.
  * ### setMaxCount

    public [BoundedInputStream.Builder](BoundedInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") setMaxCount(long maxCount)

    Sets the maximum number of bytes to return.

    Default is [-1](../IOUtils.html#EOF), negative means unbound.

    Parameters:
    :   `maxCount` - The maximum number of bytes to return, negative means unbound.

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.
  * ### setOnMaxCount

    public [BoundedInputStream.Builder](BoundedInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") setOnMaxCount([IOBiConsumer](../function/IOBiConsumer.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.function")<[Long](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Long.html "class or interface in java.lang"),[Long](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Long.html "class or interface in java.lang")> onMaxCount)

    Sets the default [`BoundedInputStream.onMaxLength(long, long)`](BoundedInputStream.html#onMaxLength(long,long)) behavior, `null` resets to a NOOP.

    The first Long is the number of bytes remaining to read before the maximum is reached count of bytes to read. The second Long is the count of bytes
    read.

    This does *not* override a `BoundedInputStream` subclass' implementation of the [`BoundedInputStream.onMaxLength(long, long)`](BoundedInputStream.html#onMaxLength(long,long))
    method.

    Parameters:
    :   `onMaxCount` - the [`ProxyInputStream.afterRead(int)`](ProxyInputStream.html#afterRead(int)) behavior.

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.

    Since:
    :   2.18.0
  * ### setPropagateClose

    public [BoundedInputStream.Builder](BoundedInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") setPropagateClose(boolean propagateClose)

    Sets whether the [`ProxyInputStream.close()`](ProxyInputStream.html#close()) method should propagate to the underling [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").

    Default is `true`.

    Parameters:
    :   `propagateClose` - `true` if calling [`ProxyInputStream.close()`](ProxyInputStream.html#close()) propagates to the `close()` method of the underlying stream or `false` if
        it does not.

    Returns:

extends [AbstractOrigin](AbstractOrigin.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")<[File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io"), [AbstractOrigin.FileOrigin](AbstractOrigin.FileOrigin.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.build")>

A [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io") origin.

  * ### filter

    public static [File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")[] [filter](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/FileFilterUtils.html#line-238)([IOFileFilter](IOFileFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter") filter,
    [File](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")... files)

    Applies an [`IOFileFilter`](IOFileFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter") to the provided [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")
    objects. The resulting array is a subset of the original file list that
    matches the provided filter.

    ```
    Set<File> allFiles = ...
    Set<File> javaFiles = FileFilterUtils.filterSet(allFiles,
        FileFilterUtils.suffixFileFilter(".java"));
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `filter` - the filter to apply to the set of files.
    :   `files` - the array of files to apply the filter to.

    Returns:
    :   a subset of `files` that is accepted by the
        file filter.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the filter is `null`
        or `files` contains a `null` value.

    Since:
    :   2.0
  * ### filter

public class [TeeReader](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/TeeReader.html#line-37)
extends [ProxyReader](ProxyReader.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")

Reader proxy that transparently writes a copy of all characters read from the proxied reader to a given Reader. Using
[`ProxyReader.skip(long)`](ProxyReader.html#skip(long)) or [`ProxyReader.mark(int)`](ProxyReader.html#mark(int))/[`ProxyReader.reset()`](ProxyReader.html#reset()) on the reader will result on some characters from the
reader being skipped or duplicated in the writer.

The proxied reader is closed when the [`close()`](#close()) method is called on this proxy. You may configure whether the
reader closes the writer.

Since:
:   2.7

# Class ProxyInputStream

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.io.input.ProxyInputStream

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Closeable, AutoCloseable`

Direct Known Subclasses:
:   `AutoCloseInputStream, BOMInputStream, BoundedInputStream, CloseShieldInputStream, CountingInputStream, MarkShieldInputStream, ObservableInputStream, SwappedDataInputStream, TaggedInputStream, TeeInputStream`

public abstract class [ProxyInputStream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ProxyInputStream.html#line-45)
extends [FilterInputStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io")

A proxy stream which acts as a [`FilterInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io"), by passing all method calls on to the proxied stream, not changing which methods are called.

It is an alternative base class to [`FilterInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") to increase reusability, because [`FilterInputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilterInputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") changes the methods being called,
such as read(byte[]) to read(byte[], int, int).

In addition, this class allows you to:

* notify a subclass that *n* bytes are about to be read through [`beforeRead(int)`](#beforeRead(int))
* notify a subclass that *n* bytes were read through [`afterRead(int)`](#afterRead(int))
* notify a subclass that an exception was caught through [`handleIOException(IOException)`](#handleIOException(java.io.IOException))
* [`unwrap()`](#unwrap()) itself

* ## Method Details

  * ### afterRead

    protected void [afterRead](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ProxyInputStream.html#line-160)(int n)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Called by the `read` methods after the proxied call has returned successfully. The argument is the number of bytes returned to the caller or
    [`EOF`](../IOUtils.html#EOF) if the end of stream was reached.

    The default delegates to the consumer given to [`ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder.setAfterRead(IOIntConsumer)`](ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder.html#setAfterRead(org.apache.commons.io.function.IOIntConsumer)).

    Alternatively, a subclasses can override this method to add post-processing functionality without having to override all the read methods.

    Note this method is *not* called from [`skip(long)`](#skip(long)) or [`reset()`](#reset()). You need to explicitly override those methods if you want to add
    post-processing steps also to them.

    Parameters:
    :   `n` - number of bytes read, or [`EOF`](../IOUtils.html#EOF) if the end of stream was reached.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - Thrown by a subclass or the consumer given to [`ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder.setAfterRead(IOIntConsumer)`](ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder.html#setAfterRead(org.apache.commons.io.function.IOIntConsumer)).

    Since:
    :   2.0

  * ### beforeRead

    protected void [beforeRead](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ProxyInputStream.html#line-202)(int n)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Invoked by the `read` methods before the call is proxied. The number
    of bytes that the caller wanted to read (1 for the [`read()`](#read())
    method, buffer length for [`read(byte[])`](#read(byte%5B%5D)), etc.) is given as
    an argument.

    Subclasses can override this method to add common pre-processing
    functionality without having to override all the read methods.
    The default implementation does nothing.

    Note this method is *not* called from [`skip(long)`](#skip(long)) or
    [`reset()`](#reset()). You need to explicitly override those methods if
    you want to add pre-processing steps also to them.

    Parameters:
    :   `n` - number of bytes that the caller asked to be read.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if the pre-processing fails in a subclass.

    Since:
    :   2.0

for [`File`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/File.html "class or interface in java.io")s and [`Path`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/Path.html "class or interface in java.nio.file").

[org.apache.commons.io.file](org/apache/commons/io/file/package-summary.html)

Provides extensions in the realm of [`java.nio.file`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/package-summary.html).

[org.apache.commons.io.file.attribute](org/apache/commons/io/file/attribute/package-summary.html)

Provides help using [`java.nio.file.attribute`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/attribute/package-summary.html) types.

[org.apache.commons.io.file.spi](org/apache/commons/io/file/spi/package-summary.html)

Provides extensions in the realm of [`java.nio.file.spi`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/file/spi/package-summary.html).

[org.apache.commons.io.filefilter](org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/package-summary.html)

Provides the an interface [`IOFileFilter`](org/apache/commons/io/filefilter/IOFileFilter.html "interface in org.apache.commons.io.filefilter") that combines both
[`FileFilter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FileFilter.html "class or interface in java.io") and [`FilenameFilter`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/FilenameFilter.html "class or interface in java.io").

[org.apache.commons.io.function](org/apache/commons/io/function/package-summary.html)

Provides IO-only related functional interfaces for lambda expressions and method references.

[org.apache.commons.io.input](org/apache/commons/io/input/package-summary.html)

Provides implementations of input classes, such as [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") and [`Reader`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Reader.html "class or interface in java.io").

[org.apache.commons.io.input.buffer](org/apache/commons/io/input/buffer/package-summary.html)

Provides implementations of buffered input classes, such as
[`CircularBufferInputStream`](org/apache/commons/io/input/buffer/CircularBufferInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input.buffer") and
[`PeekableInputStream`](org/apache/commons/io/input/buffer/PeekableInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input.buffer").

[org.apache.commons.io.monitor](org/apache/commons/io/monitor/package-summary.html)

Provides a component for monitoring file system events (directory and file create, update and delete events).

[org.apache.commons.io.output](org/apache/commons/io/output/package-summary.html)

Provides implementations of output classes, such as [`OutputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/OutputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") and
[`Writer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io").

[org.apache.commons.io.serialization](org/apache/commons/io/serialization/package-summary.html)

Provides a framework for controlling the deserialization of classes.

public static class [ThrottledInputStream.Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ThrottledInputStream.html#line-75)
extends [ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder](ProxyInputStream.AbstractBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")<[ThrottledInputStream](ThrottledInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input"), [ThrottledInputStream.Builder](ThrottledInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input")>

Builds a new [`ThrottledInputStream`](ThrottledInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

## Using NIO

```
ThrottledInputStream in = ThrottledInputStream.builder()
  .setPath(Paths.get("MyFile.xml"))
  .setMaxBytes(100_000, ChronoUnit.SECONDS)
  .get();
```

## Using IO

```
ThrottledInputStream in = ThrottledInputStream.builder()
  .setFile(new File("MyFile.xml"))
  .setMaxBytes(100_000, ChronoUnit.SECONDS)
  .get();
```

```
ThrottledInputStream in = ThrottledInputStream.builder()
  .setInputStream(inputStream)
  .setMaxBytes(100_000, ChronoUnit.SECONDS)
  .get();
```

Since:
:   2.16.0

See Also:
:   * [`get()`](#get())

    public [ThrottledInputStream](ThrottledInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") [get](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ThrottledInputStream.Builder.html#line-109)()
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Builds a new [`ThrottledInputStream`](ThrottledInputStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input").

    You must set an aspect that supports [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()), otherwise, this method throws an exception.

    :   `UnsupportedOperationException` - if the origin cannot be converted to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io").
    :   `IOException` - if an I/O error occurs converting to an [`InputStream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/InputStream.html "class or interface in java.io") using [`AbstractStreamBuilder.getInputStream()`](../build/AbstractStreamBuilder.html#getInputStream()).

    See Also:

  * ### setMaxBytes

    public [ThrottledInputStream.Builder](ThrottledInputStream.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.io.input") [setMaxBytes](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/io/input/ThrottledInputStream.Builder.html#line-137)(long value,
    [ChronoUnit](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/time/temporal/ChronoUnit.html "class or interface in java.time.temporal") chronoUnit)

    Sets the maximum bytes per time period unit.

    For example, to throttle reading to 100K per second, use:

    ```
    builder.setMaxBytes(100_000, ChronoUnit.SECONDS)
    ```

    To test idle timeouts for example, use 1 byte per minute, 1 byte per 30 seconds, and so on.

    Parameters:
    :   `value` - the maximum bytes
    :   `chronoUnit` - a duration scale goal.

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - Thrown if maxBytesPerSecond <= 0.

    Since:
    :   2.19.0
